### Job summary

Department Summary 
Financial Crime is commonly referred to as Financial Security at Crédit Agricole. The Financial Security Department is split into 2 teams (i) FS Advisory & Governance and (ii) Fraud & Complex Investigations. This vacancy sits within the FS Advisory & Governance team. FS provides CA-CIB London Branch and Crédit Agricole SA London Branch with controls and procedures for them to comply with the internal FS (financial crime and sanctions) policies and procedures, local regulatory obligations and the bank’s objective of reducing financial crime within the financial sector. 

Key Responsibilities of the Department 
The FS Department in the UK is responsible for: 
·         Oversight of the branch financial crime program through multiple workflows and internal processes. 
·         Ensuring the bank is fully compliant with the provisions of all relevant legislation. 
·         Acting as the UK primary point of contact and subject matter experts (SME) for the businesses and Group with regards to financial crime matters. 
·         Ensuring Senior Management is kept informed of updates and the general financial crime risk framework of the branch. 

Key Role Responsibilities 
The role requires involvement, as required, in assisting FS to fulfil its legal and regulatory obligations in the UK. This is a hands-on role which requires substantial contribution in the day-to-day activities and decisions of the team. The incumbent will have Financial Crime advisory experience with a strong interest in, and some exposure to, governance. 

·         Regulatory Watch: anticipate opportunities and challenges based on new / upcoming regulatory changes. Monitor industry guidance, enforcement actions, general notices, reports and reviews. Conduct gap analysis where required and work with stakeholders on follow-up action plans where required. Lead on some work streams related to the implementation of new/updated regulations and escalate updates where necessary. 
·         Industry Engagement: attend and contribute to industry forums, meetings and working groups on behalf of FS London. 
·         Training: support in the creation, coordination and deliver training based on policy updates, industry updates and refresher sessions as required. Conduct training needs analysis, monitor the FS Training Plan and work with internal and external trainers. 
·         Policies: support in liaising with Head Office on the consultation of Group guidance notes and policy updates. Review proposed updates from a UK regulatory perspective. Review and update existing local (UK) policies as applicable. 
·         Procedures: work with FS management to create and/or enhance UK desktop procedures. Contribute to Group procedures as required by Head Office. 
·         Reporting: Contribute to and/or deliver management information to senior management and London committees 
·         Communication: Draft and distribute communication and relevant material to stakeholde

Cultivarium builds scientific tools that turn biological discovery into real-world capability. As a Frontier Research Contractor, we provide technical solutions and hands-on support to partners working on the problems of today. Born a Focused Research Organization, we are drawn to the hardest technological problems in biology and built to tackle them with intensity. We prize builders who efficiently leverage resources to deliver tangible solutions at the frontier, for outsized societal benefit. Our ambition is to study and engineer non-model organisms across the entire tree of life.

What we are looking for

We're looking for a computational biologist who is genuinely curious about the strange corners of biology, and rigorous about the genomics that explain them. You'll apply population and comparative genomics to organisms across the tree of life, building the pipelines and analyses that turn raw sequence into biological insight. A successful candidate is fluent in population genomics and organellar genetics, comfortable working at scale on messy datasets with no off-the-shelf reference workflow, and drawn to exotic systems most labs never touch.

You'll create impact by bringing deep genomic expertise to non-model systems, developing novel approaches to analyze and integrate diverse biological datasets, and turning population-scale sequence into evidence that drives decisions.

This is an in-person role at either our Watertown, MA USA or London, UK location.

Responsibilities:

- Design and run pipelines for population- and comparative-genomic analysis across non-model organisms (e.g. variant calling, population structure, selection scans, and phylogenomics) and extract robust signal from population-scale datasets.

- Assemble, annotate, and curate genomes and pan-genomes for organisms with no existing reference, and integrate genomic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic data to connect genotype to phenotype.

- Analyze nuclear and organelle, such as mitochondrial and chloroplast, genome variation including heteroplasmy, cytonuclear coevolution, and haplotype structure within and across populations and species.

- Apply machine learning where it adds real leverage (e.g. predictive modeling of gene function and trait architecture).

- Partner with wet-lab scientists to design experiments and interpret results, and generate clean, well-documented, reproducible code.

- Present your work, mentor teammates, and share computational-biology best practices.

- Bring high agency and high standards: take ownership, give and receive candid feedback, and push the team to be its best in service of the science.

Basic Qualifications:

- You believe there's tremendous signal hiding in noisy biological measurements, and that we've barely begun to tap what's possible with the data we already have and the experiments still to come.

- Authorized to work without sponsorship.

- PhD in population genetics, evolutionary biology, computational biology, genomics, or in a related field.

- Demonstrated experience with population- and comparative-genomics methods at population scale, including variant calling, annotation, and comparative analysis using tools such as GATK, bcftools, vcftools, PLINK, ANGSD, and scikit-allel, orchestrated in pipelines (e.g. Nextflow, Snakemake).

- Proficiency in Python and/or R with standard bioinformatics libraries (e.g. Biopython, Bioconductor, pandas), and collaborative version control (Git).

- A strong scientific communicator who presents complex analyses clearly to interdisciplinary audiences, with a creative, detail-oriented, collaborative approach.

Advanced Qualifications:

- Hands-on experience analyzing large, population-scale genomic cohorts.

- Experience with organellar genome analysis (e.g. mitochondrial and chloroplast variation, heteroplasmy, and cytonuclear interactions).

- Experience with long-read sequencing, structural variation, or pan-genome analysis.

- Familiarity with machine learning or foundation models applied to biological sequences (e.g. ESM, Evo, Nucleotide Transformer).

- Experience with cloud computing environments (AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure) for large-scale data processing.

- A track record of scientific contributions through publications, open-source software, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.

- A genuine fascination with exotic non-model systems. Bonus for hands-on experience with any of:

- Oxytricha (programmed genome rearrangement)

- sacoglossan sea slugs (kleptoplasty, stolen-plastid retention)

- apple snails, Pomacea (camera-eye regeneration)

- mitochondria and chloroplasts (cytonuclear coevolution)

- tardigrades (anhydrobiosis and extremotolerance)

- bdelloid rotifers (ameiotic evolution and pervasive horizontal gene transfer)

• Familiarity with observability and monitoring tools such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, Amplitude or similar
• Confidence working with AI-assisted tools and the ability to extract insight through effective prompting
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly in translating technical findings for non-technical teams

• High attention to detail combined with operational curiosity and continuous-improvement mindset
• Willingness to work rotating shifts as part of a 24/7 global operations model

About the Team

DoorDash’s mission is to grow and empower local economies. By building intelligent, last-mile delivery technology for local cities, DoorDash connects people with the local businesses they care about — helping grow businesses and the communities that support those businesses. At DoorDash, there are three audiences that are at the core of every decision we make - our Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers. The Research team has a direct link to uncover the unmet needs and pain points of each of these audiences. We bring their voices into the business in order to help set the strategic vision for all of DoorDash’s current and future products.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Principal Researcher to be a strategic research leader for EMEA, shaping what DoorDash builds next. You’ll combine deep expertise in qualitative and quantitative methods to find the unmet needs, behavioral shifts, and market openings that point to new products and new growth. You’ll work as a peer to senior product, design, engineering, data science, and business leaders, and your work will directly inform roadmaps, investment decisions, and company-level strategy.

This role is built for a seasoned researcher who is equally comfortable in a living room interview, a survey dataset, and a leadership review, and who uses AI as a daily tool to move faster and see further, without giving up the judgment that makes research trustworthy. You’ll also raise the bar for the wider research practice by mentoring researchers, sharing methods, and helping the team define what great looks like in an AI-enabled era.

What You’ll Be Doing

Shape Product Strategy: Translate deep understanding of Consumers, Merchants, and Couriers into a clear point of view on where DoorDash should play and win. You’ll frame the highest-stakes questions, bring evidence to roadmap and investment debates, and influence decisions at the director and executive level.

Detect New Opportunities: Proactively identify emerging needs, behavior changes, and white space that point to new products, new verticals, and new growth levers. You’ll size and validate opportunities with a mix of foundational discovery, market and competitive context, and behavioral data, and turn them into concepts teams can act on.

Lead Mixed-Methods Research: Design and run rigorous research end to end, choosing the right method for the question: ethnography, in-depth interviews, diary studies, and usability testing alongside surveys, conjoint and MaxDiff, segmentation, experiment design, and behavioral and log analysis. You’ll triangulate across sources so the “what,” the “how much,” and the “why” tell one coherent story.

Partner with Data Science and Experimentation: Work closely with data science and analytics to connect qualitative insight to A/B test design, metrics, and product outcomes, and to explain the “why” behind results. You’ll help teams learn from what worked, what didn’t, and what to test next.

Apply AI to the Research Craft: Use AI tools and LLMs in your daily workflow for synthesis, analysis, survey and discussion guide design, and scaling qualitative depth, and design human-in-the-loop checks that catch confident but wrong outputs. You’ll help the team identify where AI accelerates research and where it should not be trusted, and contribute to shared prompts, workflows, and standards. You’ll also study how people experience AI-powered features across DoorDash’s products.

Influence and Communicate: Tell compelling, decision-ready stories that move partners from insight to action. You’ll adapt depth and format to the moment, from a fast directional read that unblocks a team this week to a foundational body of work that anchors a multi-year strategy, and you’ll follow through to see that findings change what gets built.

Lead Through Others: Serve as a thought partner and mentor to researchers across levels, review and elevate research quality, and help partners run good research on their own where that makes sense. You’ll help set the team’s research agenda, methods, and standards, and contribute to hiring and growing the team.

Operate Across Brands and Regions: Bring a global lens to your work, partnering across brands, markets, and cultures and adapting approaches to local context so that insights scale beyond a single market.

What We’re Looking For

• 10+ years of experience in user, market, or product research at a technology company (or equivalent depth), with a track record of leading ambiguous, high-visibility work at staff level or above

• Demonstrated impact on product strategy: examples where your research changed a roadmap, unlocked a new product or line of business, or redirected significant investment

• Proven ability to detect and shape new product or growth opportunities, from early signal through validated concept

• Expert command of both qualitative and quantitative methods, including interviews, ethnography, and usability testing as well as survey design, statistical analysis, and experimentation. Working knowledge of SQL, R, or Python for pulling and analyzing your own data is a plus

• Hands-on experience using AI and LLMs in research (for example, synthesis, analysis, prototyping, or scaling qualitative work), with sound instincts about where they help and where they mislead. Experience researching AI-powered products is a plus

• Experience in consumer, two-sided or multi-sided marketplace, logistics, commerce, or local services contexts is a plus

• Exceptional storytelling and executive presence, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders without authority and build trust across product, design, engineering, data science, and business teams

• A bias for speed and pragmatism: comfortable delivering directional insight quickly while knowing when a decision calls for deeper rigor

• Experience mentoring or coaching researchers and raising the quality of a research practice

• Advanced degree in HCI, Psychology, Sociology, Anthropology, Economics, Statistics, Survey Methodology, or a related field preferred, or equivalent practical experience

About the Role

We are looking for experienced engineers to join the EU Traffic team, based at Deliveroo, part of DoorDash, and help build the next generation of DoorDash’s Traffic platform. We are building a single, shared platform designed to serve DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt, so your work will shape reliability and security for all three marketplaces. Our team owns the infrastructure that carries every request into and through that platform: the edge, where we manage Cloudflare (CDN, DNS, rate limiting, bot mitigation) and the ingress systems for external traffic, and service-to-service (S2S) communication, where we run the service mesh and the authentication that secures calls between thousands of services across multiple regions.

You will work on core components of our traffic stack, including our Cloudflare edge configuration (managed as code), and service-to-service authentication and authorization (workload identity, token issuance and validation at the mesh layer). This role sits at the intersection of distributed systems, networking, and security. It includes designing, building, and maintaining systems that must operate reliably and efficiently across some of the most critical and latency-sensitive workloads at DoorDash, from the first byte at the edge to the last hop between services.

You will report to the Engineering Manager of the EU-Traffic Team within the Infrastructure organization. This role is hybrid working from London.

You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Design and build large-scale distributed systems that are high RPS and latency sensitive

• Troubleshoot, debug, and fix issues that affect production and maintain our SLAs

• Work collaboratively with other platform and product engineers to deliver on feature requests and solve their problems

• Find ways to improve the team’s productivity and operational capabilities through the use of automation, AI tools, and other avenues

• Participate in a shared on-call rotation and help lead production investigations and incidents, with support from teammates

• Mentor and learn from teammates through design reviews, pairing, and incident reviews

• Solid understanding of networking fundamentals like TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTP/2, gRPC, Load Balancing

• Background working on and debugging high-QPS or latency-sensitive systems

• You’re curious, collaborative, and comfortable making progress in ambiguity

• You work AI-first: you delegate to and orchestrate coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) across design, implementation, testing, incident response, and releases

If you don’t meet every requirement but are excited about this work, we’d still love to hear from you.

Bonus points if you…

• Experience with programming languages like Go, C++, Python or Rust

• Experience with AWS, especially with networking primitives like LBs, Privatelink, etc. and Kubernetes or other container management tool

• Experience with service mesh technologies such as Envoy, Istio or Linkerd

• Familiarity with xDS or control plane architectures

• Experience building RPC frameworks or client-side networking libraries

• Experience with Infrastructure as Code tooling like Terraform

• Experience with Gitops delivery tooling such as ArgoCD, Helm, Atlantis.

• Track record of sharing prompts, tooling, and practices that make a whole team faster with AI

Broadcast & Live Operations 
United Kingdom

Position
This role is offered on a UK employment contract. Candidates must be based in the UK as we are unable to support remote working from outside the country due to local employment and tax legislation.

Deltatre's Content Operations team runs live and video-on-demand (VOD) content across a range of sports and entertainment platforms. We ingest, enrich, schedule, publish and monitor content so that fans find the right event, highlight or replay, presented the way each client intends.
As Content Operations Manager, you will handle the day-to-day running of live and VOD content across a designated client portfolio, combining hands-on content management and image creation with operational coordination. You'll work alongside our Senior Content Operations Managers on planning, prioritization and delivery, and take on more independence and breadth as you grow in the role.

Responsibilities
Content lifecycle (live and VOD)
• Work across the full VOD lifecycle – media ingestion, transcoding, metadata enrichment, playlisting, publishing and front-end verification.
• Schedule, onboard and validate live and upcoming events on daily, weekly and seasonal cycles, accurately and on time.
• Support live operations with real-time monitoring, troubleshooting and delivery coordination.
Publishing, playlisting and presentation
• Action ad hoc and recurring client requests, prioritized with the Senior Content Operations Managers.
• Build playlists, set ordering logic and manage front-end presentation and promotion – with direction from the Senior Content Operations Managers at first, then increasingly on your own.
• Make sure all content, including shoulder programming such as pre- and post-game shows and highlights, is published and displayed in line with agreed principles.
• Run hero updates when assigned or when working the relevant shift.
• Create thumbnails for upcoming events, highlights and replays and, where appropriate, hero images from templates.
• Build thumbnail templates from brand guidelines.
• Contribute to delivery of proof-of-concepts for prospective clients.
Metadata management
• Create and document metadata across VOD content, including titles, descriptions, tags and geo-restrictions.
• Keep metadata neutral, clear and consistent, and follow each client's specific requirements.
• Update and iterate metadata documentation as requirements change.
• Write and implement descriptions for upcoming live events.
Quality assurance and audit
• Conduct regular audit checks on content playback, metadata accuracy and front-end presentation.
• Keep systems and platforms consistent through daily and weekly validation.
Operational delivery and stakeholders
• Support the Senior Content Operations Managers with day-to-day delivery across your assigned client portfolio.
• Respond to operational issues and support real-time decisions.
• Flag issues, dependencies and potential delays early, and suggest improvements to workflows and processes.
• Work with live and schedule operations colleagues to keep content delivery seamless.
• Provide real-time updates and reporting, and escalate risks to management.
• Handle day-to-day client requests from start to finish.
Training and knowledge sharing
• Help onboard and train new team members on best practice and quality standards.
• Train new self-service clients on our systems and platforms.
• Share client knowledge so the team doesn't depend on any one person.

Requirements
This is the experience that will help you hit the ground running.

Required
• 3+ years' experience in content operations, media operations or digital publishing for a streaming, broadcast or sports media platform.
• Hands-on experience ingesting, scheduling and publishing VOD content in a content management system (CMS) or video platform.
• Working knowledge of the VOD workflow end to end: ingestion, transcoding, metadata, playlisting and front-end verification.
• Experience supporting live event operations, including scheduling and real-time monitoring.
• Experience writing and maintaining metadata (titles, descriptions, tags) to a style guide or client specification.
• Experience creating thumbnails and images in Adobe Photoshop, including building templates from brand guidelines.
• Experience running quality checks on content playback, metadata or front-end presentation.
• Experience handling day-to-day client or stakeholder requests and escalating risks clearly and early.
• Experience writing or maintaining process documentation and checklists.
• Able to work late midweek and weekend shifts around live events.
Valued
• Experience with geo-restrictions, rights windows or content availability rules.
• Knowledge of sports formats and programming, such as pre- and post-game shows, highlights and replays.
• Experience training colleagues or clients on systems and tools.
• Experience contributing to proof-of-concepts or onboarding for new clients.
• Experience across multiple front ends (web, mobile, connected TV).

Who Thrives Here
This is a breadth role. You'll move between clients and types of work as demand requires, from metadata and thumbnails to live event scheduling and client requests, often within the same shift. Live sport sets the rhythm: from September to May, expect around one late midweek shift a week and two to three weekend shifts a month at busy times, with far fewer from June to August. Live schedules change, so the pattern isn't fixed.
You'll do well here if you take work from request through to completion without needing to be chased, and say early when something is unclear, delayed or at risk. You know when to solve a problem yourself and when to escalate it, you keep documentation and checklists accurate, and you share what you know so the team isn't relying on you alone.

Process and what to expect
• Introductory conversation – a chance to get to know each other and answer your questions about Deltatre.
• 1-hour Technical round of Interview – we will deep dive on your experience and past responsibilities.
• 1-hour Competency Based Interview – situational questions based on real-life work scenarios.
If any of these formats would be difficult for you, tell us – we adjust regularly and can usually accommodate.
Accessibility and accommodation questions are welcome at any stage. Tell us what would work for you.

The Business Development Manager is a new role responsible for helping to coordinate business development activity across Dentsu Creative. You will work closely with our Managing Director on the implementation of the new business strategy, from identifying new clients and designing prospecting campaigns, through to the delivery of proposals and pitch responses – and you will collaborate with our marketing team to develop sales collateral, case studies and events.

This is a varied, hands-on role that would suit someone who is naturally curious, proactive and enjoys building relationships across the business. You'll work with teams across our UK offices and practice areas, helping to uncover great stories, develop compelling content and ensure Dentsu Creative is always putting its best foot forward. No two days are the same, making this an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys variety and taking ownership of projects.
What you'll do
• Research different industries and companies to help identify new client prospects.
• Prepare and collate the relevant materials to target the desired client list. Work closely with our team designer on new prospecting campaigns from brief through to completion.
• Support agency pitch teams throughout the process, coordinating activity across multiple teams and stakeholders to help keep projects on track, organised and delivered to a high standard.
• Support the creation of pitch content as required, including credentials, RFIs, tenders and pitch presentations, ensuring Dentsu Creative leverages its capabilities, case studies, network and senior talent in the best way possible to win.
• Build a strong understanding of the agency's capabilities, client work and strategic thinking, helping to identify and develop case studies and stories that showcase our best work and support new business conversations.
• Write clear and engaging copy for credentials, case studies, pitch materials, prospecting campaigns and other new business content.
• Work closely with colleagues across the agency to uncover interesting work, client success stories and examples that demonstrate the breadth of Dentsu Creative's capabilities.
• Support the management of our sales pipeline and lead tracking in Salesforce (prior knowledge isn't essential).
• Keep a close eye on competitor activity and industry trends to help identify opportunities.
• Support the marketing team with the planning and execution of events targeting prospective clients, including guest management, venue liaison and event materials.

The work is fast, fluid and exciting, with no two days being the same. You will be part of a close-knit team, juggling multiple pitches and opportunities. We are looking for someone who enjoys working collaboratively, takes pride in producing high-quality work and is keen to learn and grow in a dynamic agency environment.

What you'll bring
• Excellent written communication skills with the ability to write engaging copy for presentations, case studies and client-facing materials.
• An interest in branding, marketing and strategy, with the ability to understand client challenges and translate them into compelling stories.
• Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.
• A proactive approach and willingness to take ownership, using your initiative and looking for opportunities to add value.
• Confident building relationships and working with stakeholders across different teams and levels of the business.
• High attention to detail and pride in producing high-quality work.
• Entrepreneurial and analytical thinker with an interest in understanding markets, brands and business opportunities.
• Proficient in PowerPoint, Word and Excel.
• Relevant experience in Business Development, Marketing, Communications or Account Management within a creative, integrated, digital or media agency is essential.

London | Hybrid

Role Overview
We are now seeking an EHS Advisor to support our UK operations.
Based out of London, this role will provide health and safety support across a range of UK projects, working closely with project teams, site management, subcontractors and senior operational stakeholders.
This is a visible, site-facing role suited to someone who is comfortable engaging with teams on live construction projects. You will carry out inspections, support safe systems of work, review documentation, advise on risk, investigate incidents and help ensure that health and safety standards are consistently applied across our UK project portfolio.
The role will suit someone with experience in construction, M&E, building services, infrastructure or similar project environments who is confident working with site teams and influencing safe behaviours in a practical, constructive way.
Key Responsibilities 
As EHS Advisor, you will:

• Support the implementation of Designer Group’s health, safety & environmental policies, procedures and standards across UK projects.
• Carry out regular site inspections, audits and safety walks.
• Identify risks, unsafe behaviours or non-compliance and work with site teams to close out actions.
• Support project teams with risk assessments, method statements and safe systems of work.
• Deliver toolbox talks, safety briefings and site inductions, as required.
• Monitor PPE compliance, housekeeping, access/egress, plant, lifting operations and general site safety standards.
• Support incident, accident and near-miss investigations, ensuring reports are completed accurately and actions are followed through.
• Monitor the maintenance of health and safety records, inspection reports, permits, registers and site documentation.
• Assist with emergency preparedness, drills and response planning.
• Liaise with project managers, construction managers, subcontractors and client representatives on health and safety matters.
• Build and maintain effective working relationships with client and principal contractor EHS representatives, acting as the primary point of contact for health, safety and environmental matters on assigned projects.
• Promote a positive safety culture across projects, encouraging ownership and accountability at site level.
• Advise management on opportunities for continuous improvement in health and safety performance.
• Monitor environmental performance across projects, identifying risks and opportunities for improvement in areas such as waste management and sustainability.
• Support compliance with UK health and safety legislation, client requirements and Designer Group standards.

What We Are Looking For
We are looking for someone who can bring a practical, site-led approach to health and safety.
You should have:

• Experience in a Health & Safety / EHS Advisor or similar role.
• Previous experience within construction, mechanical and electrical, building services, infrastructure or industrial project environments.
• Strong working knowledge of UK health and safety legislation and construction safety requirements.
• Experience carrying out site inspections, audits, toolbox talks and incident investigations.
• Confidence reviewing RAMS, permits, lifting plans and safe systems of work.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to influence site teams positively.
• A proactive, hands-on approach with the confidence to challenge unsafe practices.
• Good attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate safety records and reports.
• Flexibility to travel to project sites across the UK as required.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will hold:

• NEBOSH Construction Certificate, NEBOSH General Certificate or equivalent (essential).
• NEBOSH Environmental / IEMA Environmental Certificate or equivalent environmental qualification (desirable).
• IOSH Membership or working towards membership (desirable).
• CSCS Card or equivalent site safety skill card (essential).
• Full UK Driving Licence due to the multi-site nature of the role (desirable).

Why Join Designer Group?

This is an opportunity to join a growing international engineering business with a strong project pipeline and a clear commitment to safe delivery.

You will be joining a team where health and safety has real visibility, where your input will directly influence site standards, and where you will work on technically interesting M&E projects across the UK.

What We Offer

• Career progression within a growing international engineering business.
• Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
• A collaborative, safety-focused culture.

• The opportunity to help shape and enhance health, safety and environmental performance across multiple project environments.

You’ll take ownership of the programme from early development through to delivery, ensuring it reflects reality, drives performance, and highlights risk before it becomes a problem.
If you’ve worked in an M&E contractor or construction environment and know how sequencing, coordination and site constraints impact delivery, you’ll fit straight into this.

• Challenge assumptions and provide practical planning advice across the project lifecycle
• Monitor progress on site and align programme with actual delivery
• Support commercial and project teams with planning input for variations and claims

Title: Websites Operations & Delivery Lead
Role Type: Permanent, Full time
Location: London, England
Reports to: Head of Websites Product

About us:
With over 200 brands sold in nearly 180 countries, Diageo is home to some of the world’s most iconic drinks. From Johnnie Walker and Guinness to Tanqueray, Smirnoff and Don Julio, we craft brands chosen for life’s moments — from everyday connections to landmark celebrations.
Bring your talent, curiosity and ambition, and strive for your personal best alongside people who challenge, support and learn from each other. Together, as one outstanding team, we keep learning, improving and setting a higher standard for our brands, our business and each other.
Join us and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.

Purpose of the Role:
 Lead the technical solution design, delivery, operation and secure release for Diageo's many consumer-facing websites — including Guinness Storehouse, Johnnie Walker, Baileys, The Bar, Malts and many more — ensuring they are delivered efficiently, operated effectively and continuously improved. Support platform performance, stability and compliance to enable strong consumer experiences.
This is a hands-on, technical product leadership role: you will turn the product roadmap set by the Head of Websites Product into the right technical design, the right squad and the fastest, safe path to live.

The opportunity:
Diageo is consolidating development of its consumer websites into one strategic vendor and streamlining the tech stack and content operations behind them, with one goal: efficiency. You will design how that platform is enhanced, run and kept safe.

Key Responsibilities:
1. Tech solution design and estimation
• Support the product road mapping journey alongside the Head of Websites Product, to prioritise business opportunities against real cost and effort. Translate product priorities into technical delivery plans and execution.
• Work with the Websites Tech Lead to review existing solutions and identify alternatives in the market — CMS, search, identity, commerce, hosting, AI tooling — that best fit the business needs prioritised by product.
• Champion the target technical design: a consolidated, headless and composable platform, shared components and streamlined content operations across complete portfolio of sites.
• Own build-vs-buy-vs-reuse recommendations and keep technical decisions documented.
2. Squad design and delivery of the product roadmap
• Lead delivery of product roadmap, ensuring high-quality execution at the highest sustainable delivery velocity.
• Define the ideal squad composition with our development partner: roles, seniority, skills mix and capacity (e.g. delivery lead, tech lead, front-end, back-end, QA automation, DevOps, UX/UI), and how squads map to platform, brand builds and run/maintain.
• Define the agile ceremonies and ways of working — sprint planning, refinement, stand-ups, reviews, retrospectives, quarterly planning, Definition of Ready and Done — in a multi-vendor ecosystem and keep improving them.
• Own release management, testing, deployment and operational readiness frameworks.
3. Platform maintenance and tech health
• Own, monitor and improve the maintenance and technical health of the platform: uptime, performance (Core Web Vitals), dependency and version currency, technical debt and cost.
• Manage platform operations, performance and incident resolution across platforms, and own the incident management process end to end — severity model, on-call, escalation, communication and post-incident reviews.
• Run a planned maintenance and tech-debt programme alongside new feature delivery.
4. Compliance, security and vulnerability management
• Ensure security, privacy and compliance requirements are embedded into delivery and operations.
• Support the technical solutions and internal processes that keep every site compliant with the rules for marketing alcohol online: age verification, responsible-drinking messaging, market-specific advertising codes, cookie consent, GDPR and local privacy laws, and accessibility.
• Own the vulnerability review and resolution process with the vendor and Diageo Technology — scanning, pen testing, patching SLAs and secure release.
• Design the cybersecurity and monitoring strategy that gets ahead of threats such as PHP vulnerabilities: a full dependency inventory, automated updates, security scanning before every release, AI-assisted threat detection and alerting, and a regular patch cycle, so fixes are planned work rather than last-minute fire drills.

5. Business translation through KPIs and targets
• Define, track and hit KPIs and targets for delivery velocity, tech health, compliance and the maintenance process. Own communication to the business on delivery, platform health, incidents and risk using KPIs set.
• Work with Head of Product & to define cost, time, consumer experience and risk — for brand, market and senior leadership audiences.
• Hold the development partner to agreed SLAs and KPIs and use the data to drive continuous improvement.

Qualifications and experience:
• Agency-led delivery: a track record of leading digital delivery through an external agency or outsourced partner — setting requirements, squad set-up and SLAs, and holding the partner to account
• Agile delivery and release management: solid experience running agile delivery, releases and platform operations at scale.
• AI Enhanced delivery proven with Data: Experience applying AI-driven automation (e.g. AI coding assistants, automated testing and code review, AI-powered monitoring) alongside relevant platform metrics to raise delivery velocity & improve platform performance
• Proactive security and maintenance: experience designing security and monitoring strategies that get ahead of vulnerabilities (e.g. PHP), patches and third-party changes — dependency management, automated scanning, threat detection, API version tracking — without slowing delivery.
• Compliance in delivery: experience building security, privacy and regulatory requirements into delivery.
• Modern web architecture: strong knowledge of headless platforms, e.g. Contentful or Umbraco, Next.js, React, Vercel, Algolia, Auth0 and Shopify
• Platform consolidation: experience moving legacy websites to a modern stack and bringing many sites onto one platform.
• Global collaboration: a clear communicator who works well across global, multi-functional teams.

Working with Us
Flexibility is key to our success. Talk to us about what flexibility means to you so that you’re supported to manage your wellbeing and balance your priorities from day one.

Our purpose is crafting iconic drinks chosen for life’s moments. And it’s our people, with their different experiences, perspectives and talents, who make that possible.
We value diversity in its broadest sense and want everyone to feel they can belong, contribute and strive for their personal best. You’ll work alongside people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives — challenging, supporting and learning from one another as one outstanding team.
Together, we’re constantly learning and improving, combining the strength of our people, capabilities and iconic brands to set a higher standard, grow and win. Wherever you join us, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute, make an impact and play your part in making life’s moments mean a little more.

job_description:
Project description
Own the technical analysis for our Client's Aladdin Wealth implementation: the project data definitions, source-to-target mappings, interfaces, API integrations and data quality controls.

Take business requirements from the Business Analyst and translate them into buildable technical specifications. Work with developers, integration
architects, data engineers and BlackRock technical contacts to design,
implement and prove the solution.

This is a contract engagement requiring someone productive from the outset, with hands-on Aladdin Wealth implementation experience.
Responsibilities
• TARGET ARCHITECTURE AND INTEGRATION

• Contribute technical analysis to the Aladdin Wealth target architecture: component boundaries, system-of-record considerations, data flows and responsibilities across Aladdin Wealth and the existing application landscape.

• Develop the integration inventory and plan: in-scope inbound and outbound interfaces, sequencing, dependencies and release phasing.

• Analyse event-driven and batch options with the integration architect: triggers, ordering, idempotency, replay, throughput, latency, error handling and recovery.
- Elicit and document non-functional requirements for the integration layer, including volumes, availability, recovery, monitoring and alerting.
- Support technical mobilisation: connectivity and environment dependencies, access requirements, test-data needs and the initial technical backlog.

DATA DEFINITIONS AND MAPPING

• Own project data definitions and source-to-target mappings for data exchanged with Aladdin Wealth, including positions, transactions, security reference data, pricing, benchmarks, classifications, client and account hierarchies.

• Work within the Aladdin Wealth data model and document required mappings, transformations, identifiers and exceptions; do not assume ownership of the vendor's underlying product schema.

• Translate business-approved taxonomy and classification rules into mappings and exception handling.

• Specify portfolio risk attributes as data: source, refresh, lineage and downstream use, in line with business definitions agreed by the Business Analyst and relevant owners.

• Define historical data migration scope, mapping and technical validation approach.

• Maintain data dictionaries, mapping specifications and decisions as scope evolves.

APIS AND INTERFACES

• Analyse Aladdin Wealth API and interface documentation provided for the engagement; specify endpoint or interface use, payload contracts, security requirements, versioning, limits, error handling and retry behaviour as confirmed for the client's implementation.

• Specify in-scope inbound feeds, such as holdings, transactions, reference data and pricing, and outbound data exchanges required by approved business requirements.

• Document interface contracts clearly enough for developers to build and test against.

• Validate feature and interface assumptions with BlackRock and the solution architect. Do not assume that a specific endpoint, payload, event pattern or workflow is available in every Aladdin Wealth deployment.

DATA QUALITY AND RECONCILIATION

• Define technical data-quality checks, completeness and accuracy rules, tolerance handling, exception reporting and remediation ownership with the relevant data owners.

• Design source-to-platform reconciliation, including break identification, triage and resolution.

• Investigate data issues hands-on using SQL and payload inspection; document root cause and corrective action.

TECHNICAL TESTING AND HANDOVER

• Define and coordinate technical test scenarios for data and interfaces, including integration, end-to-end, volume and regression testing.

• Support developers' unit testing and diagnose interface/data defects raised during business UAT; coordinate triage with developers and BlackRock.

• Support cutover and migration readiness, including dress rehearsals and data/interface reconciliation sign-off.

• Produce technical run-books, monitoring requirements and support documentation for hypercare and BAU handover.

SKILLS
Must have
• 3+ years in technical or solution analysis on wealth-management, private-banking or asset-management platform implementations.

• Proven hands-on delivery of Aladdin Wealth at scale, including target architecture input, integration planning and source-to-target data mapping.
Direct implementation experience is the primary selection criterion.

• Practical experience with Aladdin Wealth APIs or interfaces, including analysis of documentation, payloads, constraints and error handling.

• Proven delivery of inbound and outbound integrations involving Aladdin Wealth, with data mapping and reconciliation.

• Strong experience in financial-services data: positions, transactions, security/reference data, pricing, benchmarks, classifications and client/account structures.

• Experience specifying event-driven and batch integration patterns in a regulated environment.

• Able to work directly with developers and architects: discuss designs, challenge assumptions and produce precise build-ready specifications.

• Hands-on SQL; able to inspect JSON/XML payloads and work from API/interface documentation.

• Jira, Confluence, Visio ; API testing tools such as Postman; Excel for data analysis.

Nice to have
• Designed or implemented a BlackRock integration layer within a global wealth platform programme.
• Historical data migration from a legacy proposal or portfolio platform.
• Python for data validation or reconciliation; Snowflake/data-lake, Kafka or similar integration patterns.
• Exposure to adjacent platforms (Avaloq, Temenos, FNZ, SimCorp or Charles River); custody, core banking or OMS interfaces.
• Multi-entity or multi-jurisdiction delivery experience.

Job Description:
Department: Front Office Data Products

The Front Office Data Products team serves a variety of stakeholders across the Front Office, including traders, risk and senior management. We work with lots of different internal and external data sources, building and maintaining data pipelines, data models, and data products to support trading decisions and critical business processes. The team is currently expanding its capabilities to support real-time use cases alongside existing batch processing workflows, and is also expanding its Python data visualisation capabilities.

Position purpose
We are looking for a hands-on Senior Data Engineer to join our team to accelerate the delivery of high-value data products to the business. This person will be someone with strong Python fundamentals, experience with orchestration tools and Python data visualisation/UI tooling (ideally Plotly Dash) and will be someone who can communicate effectively with both business stakeholders and technical colleagues.

Main responsibilities
• Build and maintain data pipelines that integrate with existing trading workflows and business processes, including operational ownership (monitoring, alerting, incident support) and embedding data quality controls (validation, anomaly detection).

• Utilise streaming technologies and event driven architecture to build real time visualisations
• Develop dashboards and data products using Python UI tools (Plotly Dash, Streamlit or similar)
• Participate in peer reviews and uphold engineering standards across the team (coding conventions, testing, CI/CD, observability, security-by-design).
• Tune and optimise SQL queries for performance
• Work with DevOps processes (Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, Docker, Kubernetes)
• Take ownership of work end-to-end: prioritise effectively, communicate with stakeholders, plan out the work, manage risks and dependencies, and drive tasks through to completion.
• Be a role model for Python (and data engineering) best practices in the team

Experience and technical requirements
Essential
• Strong Python and SQL experience
• Data orchestration tools (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect)
• Designing database schemas and ORM models (e.g. SQLAlchemy)
• SQL query performance tuning and optimisation
• Python UI/dashboard tools (Plotly Dash, Streamlit or similar)

Strongly Preferred
• Kafka or other streaming technologies (e.g. Azure Event Hubs)
• Kubernetes
• Docker and containerisation
• Azure Cloud services (Blob Storage, Application Insights, KeyVault, Azure DevOps)
• Commodities trading or financial services background
Nice to have
• Dagster
• Tableau experience

ABOUT EDRA

Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations.

We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build.



THE ROLE

We're building a learning system that teaches AI agents how enterprises actually work. Our system starts from what a customer already has: knowledge base articles, support conversations, tickets, system logs, and agent traces. From that evidence it reverse-engineers how the business actually runs and writes the process down as instructions a person can inspect and an agent can execute, with confidence scoring to know when to automate and when to seek human input.

We're looking for AI Research Engineers who have built complex, production LLM-based systems. Whether you've scaled LLM workflows handling millions of requests, built multi-agent systems in production, or designed evaluation frameworks for enterprise deployments, we want people who bring intensity and self-direction to their craft. You'll work on our agentic learning environment: the loops that turn human corrections and agent outcomes into better knowledge and instructions over time. The job combines applied research with ownership of production systems. You find a failure, form a hypothesis, run the experiment, and ship the fix into real customer workflows.

You'll spend most of your time advancing our core context-learning library and the harness that powers our agents across every customer. The work spans continuous learning, context engineering, agent orchestration, and evaluation. You'll contribute to our knowledge benchmarks and to the self-improving capabilities of the harness.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and extend our core context-learning library, turning customer-informed problems into reusable platform capabilities.

 - Design and implement LLM-powered systems and agentic workflows from concept to production.

 - Build agentic features for knowledge management: agents that can edit, update, and maintain large knowledge bases autonomously.

 - Build continuous learning loops that use human corrections and production outcomes to find knowledge gaps, detect changed procedures, and improve prompts and instructions.

 - Build reliability and confidence systems: evaluation frameworks, confidence scoring, and logic for when to automate and when to escalate to a human.

 - Architect async, scalable systems that handle complex AI orchestration.

 - Contribute to the direction of our AI strategy and product capabilities.



WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

The environment at GBI will allow researchers to undertake ambitious, long-term, collaborative research, and we will actively support the translation of research to commercial applications, where appropriate.

The Plant Biology Institute has long-term substantial funding to support the unique scale and ambition of its vision.

**Your Role:**

EIT is seeking an experienced **Event Delivery and Genotyping Manager** to join the Crop Transformation Pipeline team within the Plant Biology Institute. This role will lead molecular event confirmation, genotyping assay strategy, event advancement decisions and delivery of high-quality gene edited and transgenic crop events to downstream trait and product teams.

The successful candidate will be a technical authority in genotyping technologies for transgenic and gene edited crops, with strong experience in event characterisation, assay development, sample tracking, molecular data interpretation and project delivery. They will connect transformation, tissue culture, greenhouse, vector design, bioinformatics and trait teams to ensure that events are confirmed, prioritised and handed over with robust data packages.

This role is critical to building an industrial-grade event delivery capability for crops including corn, wheat and other strategic species. The candidate will establish event stage-gate criteria, molecular QC workflows, genotyping vendor strategies, LIMS-enabled sample tracking and performance metrics that improve speed, quality and predictability of event delivery.

The candidate will own the downstream event confirmation and delivery process, ensuring that regenerated plants and events are sampled, genotyped, QC-reviewed, prioritised and handed over with clear molecular data packages.

**Your Responsibilities:**

- Lead the event delivery workflow from transformation output through plant recovery, sampling, molecular confirmation, quality review, advancement decisions and handover to trait, greenhouse or product teams.
- Design, validate and implement genotyping assays for transgenic and gene edited events, including transgene presence/absence, edit detection, zygosity, copy number, junction assays, backbone absence, on-target and off-target analysis, segregation tracking and event integrity.
- Apply appropriate genotyping technologies such as endpoint PCR, qPCR, ddPCR, KASP, HRM, Sanger sequencing, amplicon sequencing, targeted sequencing, NGS and targeted capture approaches to support event selection.
- Partner with the Vector Design Manager to ensure every construct is paired with a fit-for-purpose molecular assay plan before transformation begins.
- Develop event stage-gate criteria and decision frameworks for advancing gene edited and transgenic events based on edit outcome, transformation quality, copy number, expression/reporter data, regeneration status and downstream programme needs.
- Coordinate sample collection, DNA extraction, plate maps, barcoding, chain-of-custody, sample submission, vendor shipment and data return across internal laboratories and external service providers.
- Work with bioinformatics and data teams to analyze edit outcomes, chimerism/mosaicism, indel profiles, sequence confirmation, off-target risk, event integrity and molecular quality metrics.
- Own event inventory management, genotype data capture, sample traceability and event status dashboards using ELN, LIMS and structured data systems.
- Track key pipeline metrics including event yield, transformation efficiency, edit frequency, assay success rate, QC pass rate, sample turnaround time, regeneration-to-confirmed-event conversion and event delivery timelines.
- Manage external genotyping, sequencing and molecular characterisation service providers, ensuring quality, turnaround time, budget and data format expectations are met.
- Create SOPs, sample submission templates, assay validation standards, QC checklists, data interpretation guides and event handover templates.
- Develop detailed project plans, resource forecasts, risk registers and milestone dashboards for event confirmation and delivery activities.
- Train and mentor scientists, research associates and technicians in sample tracking, genotyping workflows, assay interpretation and event advancement criteria.
- The successful candidate will combine technical depth in plant genotyping and event characterisation with strong operational discipline. They will ensure that transformation outputs are converted into well-characterised, decision-ready events that can be advanced efficiently and confidently.

- Improve event advancement decisions by ensuring transformation outputs are molecularly confirmed, QC-reviewed and prioritised using clear stage-gate criteria.
- Reduce wasted downstream effort by filtering events early using robust genotyping, molecular QC and data-driven decision-making.
- Support translation of scientific discoveries into commercially applicable crop improvement tools and trait products, including IP and regulatory-ready data packages.

## Requirements

**Essential Skills, Qualifications & Experience:**

- PhD in Plant Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Genomics, Crop Science or a related discipline, or MSc with significant relevant industry experience. At least 5-7 years of experience in plant biotechnology, genotyping, molecular characterization or event advancement.

At the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT), we’re on a mission to translate scientific discovery into real world impact. We bring together visionary scientists, technologists, engineers, researchers, educators and innovators to tackle humanity’s greatest challenges in four transformative areas:

- Health, Medical Science & Generative Biology
- Food Security & Sustainable Agriculture
- Climate Change & Managing CO₂
- Artificial Intelligence & Robotics

This is ambitious work - work that demands curiosity, courage, and a relentless drive to make a difference. At EIT, you’ll join a community built on excellence, innovation, tenacity, trust, and collaboration, where bold ideas become real-world breakthroughs. Together, we push boundaries, embrace complexity, and create solutions to scale ideas from lab to society.

 **Welcome to the Generative Biology Institute:**

Led by Founding Director Jason Chin, the [Generative Biology Institute](https://eit.org/gbi) (GBI) at the Ellison Institute of Technology is tackling the key challenges in making biology engineerable, and thereby releasing the unrivalled power of biology for the benefit of humanity.

The vision of GBI is to lay the foundations for engineering biology, and unlock its potential for good. To achieve this, we must overcome two key challenges. First, we need the ability to write in the natural language of biology, enabling the rapid and scalable synthesis of entire genomes with precision. Second, we must understand what to write - determining which DNA sequences will generate biological systems that perform the desired functions. Addressing these challenges will allow us to harness the full power of biology to create transformative solutions across health, agriculture, clean energy and more.  

The Generative Biology Institute commenced operations in 2025, occupying newly renovated bespoke space in the Oxford Science Park. The team will later move to a purpose-made facility in the Oxford Science Park, currently under construction. Once complete, this state-of-the-art facility will include more than 40,000 m² of research laboratory and office space.  It will house over 30 groups and up to 600 employees at scale, focused on solving the two critical challenges in making biology engineerable and applying the solutions to addressing the global challenges encapsulated in EIT’s Humane Endeavours.

**The AI & Robotics Team**

The AI & Robotics team at EIT brings together AI research, robotics and scientific expertise to make biological matter computable and testable, at scale, and by any scientist. We build generative and predictive models of biological molecules and systems, physics-grounded simulation and design tools, and autonomous laboratories that generate the data these models learn from and test the designs they propose.

**Project Monera**

You will be joining the project Monera, a joint project across the Generative Biology Institute and the AI & Robotics team building multi-modal generative models of whole organisms, starting with _Escherichia coli_ in order to understand and predict an organism's phenotype from its genome and environment and, in time, to design genomes for a desired function. The team works as one integrated computational and experimental group: experimentalists generate genetic variation and quantitative measurements at scale (growth and fitness, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics), the models are trained and validated on that data, and the results shape the next round of experiments and insights. The experimental work is based in GBI's laboratories in the Oxford Science Park, alongside GBI's automation capability and in daily contact with the AI scientists in the AI & Robotics team.

**Job Summary**

We are building a joint experimental computational team focussed on building, training and validating multi-modal biological models.

The team will: i) generate experimental perturbation and measurement data at scale, ii) build multi-modal biological models and, iii) use the experimental data they generate to train and validate the multi-modal biological  models they build.

In this role you will: i) perform experimental genome engineering work to generate genetic variation at scale and/or ii) design and implement scalable biological measurement over one or more modalities. Where appropriate the work will leverage the substantial automation capability within the institute. Your work will be performed under the guidance of Jason Chin.

You will be part of a single team composed of AI scientists and synthetic biologists working together. We are looking for colleagues with deep expertise in genome engineering and/or quantitative phenotyping of model bacterial species such as _Escherichia coli_. The role requires the ability and willingness to work as part of a cross-disciplinary team at the interface of computational and wetlab biology. Our team ethos is based on mutual learning, strong peer-to-peer support, and a deep sense of scientific curiosity and ambition.

This is your opportunity to be part of cutting-edge research within an institute dedicated to engineering biology at an unprecedented scale. You will be leveraging GBI’s exceptional facilities, sustained funding, and collaborative environment. You will design and execute experiments, contribute to high-impact publications, and play a key role in the training and mentorship of junior researchers and students. Working at the interface of biology, AI, technology, and engineering, you will help shape GBI’s vision to reimagine what’s possible in biology.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Design, execute, and troubleshoot experiments, including the development of novel methodologies and adaptation of existing techniques to new applications. In particular, the successful applicant will utilise genome engineering strategies in the lab to produce a diversity of microbial strains as the source of training and validation data in a high throughput fashion. In addition, they will also design and prototype a range of experimental measurement strategies for characterising these strains at scale.
- Collaborate with other GBI scientists from other groups expert in synthetic biology, automation, bioinformatics, -omics and machine learning, and AI scientists from the AIR institute, as required.
- Analyse complex datasets using computational and statistical tools, interpreting results in the context of broader research goals.
- Contribute intellectually to the research direction by identifying opportunities for innovation and refining research questions.
- Prepare and publish high-quality scientific papers, reports, presentations, and protocols.
- Present research at national and international conferences, seminars, and internal meetings.
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams within GBI, EIT, and external partners to advance complementary workstreams.
- Build and maintain research infrastructure, laboratory capabilities, and cutting-edge technologies.
- Mentor and support junior researchers, including PhD students and research assistants.
- Translate research findings into commercial or translational opportunities in alignment with EIT’s mission.
- Identify and pursue opportunities for intellectual property generation and protection.
- Ensure research activities comply with EIT’s policies, legal requirements, and best scientific practice.

_This list is not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to undertake additional tasks and duties commensurate with the role._

## Requirements

**Relevant, Skills and Experience:** 

- Completed a PhD in a relevant field (e.g., synthetic biology, computational biology and AI, microbial genomics, cell biology, genomics, robotics and automation, metabolomics, and proteomics.).
- Track record of delivering ambitious research projects to a high standard.
- Strong track record in research, ideally in molecular biology, synthetic biology, or related fields.
- Skilled in data analysis and interpretation; experience with genomic analysis, automation, or computational tools desirable.
- Proven ability to work independently, think creatively, and solve complex experimental problems.
- Experience publishing in high-impact journals and presenting at international conferences.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with experience collaborating in multidisciplinary teams.
- Capacity to build and sustain productive collaborations internally and externally.
- Resilience, adaptability, and enthusiasm for working in a fast-paced, high-growth research environment.
- Deep scientific curiosity and the drive to run ambitious experiments at scale, which can be used for the training and validating foundation models for the purpose of understanding and predicting an organism's phenotype from its genome and environment.
- Basic familiarity with machine-learning concepts is welcome (what a model needs from data: coverage of the variable space, controls, replication, consistent metadata).

## Benefits

**Our Benefits:**

- Enhanced sick pay
- Pension - Employer contribution 7.5%, minimum employee contribution 5%

**Welcome to the Institute of Materials & Devices for Life Sciences (MDLS):**

The vision for the Institute of Materials & Devices for Life Sciences (MDLS) at the Ellison Institute of Technology is to advance human health by scaling interdisciplinary science at the interface of chemistry, biology and engineering. Led by Professor Hagan Bayley, it will house more than 100 researchers engaging in three interrelated endeavors; Nanopore Sensing and Sequencing, 3D Tissue Construction, and Device Engineering. The MDLS Institute will expand nanopore science to detect a wider range of biological molecules, including volatiles in human breath. While in parallel, pioneering novel methods that integrate synthetic and living tissues into structures for organ repair. All the research will be underpinned by the development of new devices capable of serving as powerful tools in clinical settings.

**Your Role:**

The Tissue Programme, led by Dr Linna Zhou and Professor Hagan Bayley within MDLS at the EIT, is seeking talented postdoctoral researchers to join its interdisciplinary team. The Programme develops technologies for the fabrication of three-dimensional living, synthetic and hybrid tissues. These platforms are used to generate functional, patterned tissues to model human disease, test therapeutics, modulate tissue function, and support the repair of damaged tissues and organs.

Our research combines advances in stem cell biology, tissue engineering and device engineering to develop next-generation technologies with translational and clinical potential.

The group currently comprises approximately 15 members, including postdoctoral researchers, DPhil students and laboratory technicians.

**We are seeking postdoctoral researchers in the following areas:**

- **Cell Biology:** Candidates should have expertise in stem cell culture and differentiation. Experience with organoid models, including brain, cardiac or immune organoids, and their characterisation would be advantageous. Skills in proteomics, bulk or single-cell RNA sequencing, tissue processing and advanced imaging are also desirable.
- **Electrophysiology:** We seek researchers with experience in cellular or tissue electrophysiology, particularly in investigating the electrical activity of neurons or cardiac cells within three-dimensional tissue models. Experience with patch-clamp recording, multielectrode arrays, calcium imaging, optogenetics or related techniques is highly desirable.
- **Bioinformatics:** We are looking for candidate with experience in omics datasets, including bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and/or proteomics. The candidate will work closely with experimental biologists to design experiments and interpret results; develop reproducible computational pipelines for data processing, quality control and statistical analysis; maintaining well-documented code, databases and data-management workflows; and support laboratory members with bioinformatics training and data analysis.
- **Hydrogel Science:** Candidates should have experience in the synthesis, modification and characterisation of biocompatible hydrogels. A background in polymer chemistry, biomaterials or hydrogel-based cell culture is preferred. The successful candidate will develop hydrogel systems for the three-dimensional printing of stem-cell-derived tissues.
- **Tissue Engineering:** We seek tissue engineers with strong expertise in microfluidics and/or bioprinting for the fabrication of three-dimensional tissues derived from human stem cells. Experience in functional characterisaiton of specific tissues is desirable. Researchers will work closely with cell biologists preparing diverse stem-cell-derived cell types and device engineers developing advanced biofabrication platforms.

- Completion of a PhD years in a relevant field (e.g. human cell biology, physiology and pathology, biophysics, biomedical engineering, and materials science).
- Proven record of research achievements, including publications in high-impact journals and presentations at international conferences.

job_title: Principal Investigators (All Levels) - Generative Biology Institute
job_description:
**Job Summary:**

Responsible for leading and managing an independent research group within the Generative Biology Institute (“GBI”), delivering a program of bold, ambitious and transformational research which is broadly aligned with GBI’s vision of making biology engineerable and unlocking its potential for good

**Generative Biology Institute**

The vision of the GBI is to lay the foundations for engineering biology, and unlock its potential for good. To achieve this, we must overcome two key challenges. First, we need the ability to write in the natural language of biology, enabling the rapid and scalable synthesis of entire genomes with precision. Second, we must understand what to write, determining which DNA sequences will generate biological systems that perform the desired functions. Addressing these challenges will allow us to harness the full power of biology to create transformative solutions across health, agriculture, clean energy and more.

Part of the Ellison Institute of Technology, Oxford (“EIT”), GBI is led by founding Director Jason Chin. It will house 30 groups and more than 500 researchers at scale, focused on solving the two critical challenges in making biology engineerable and applying the solutions to addressing the global challenges encapsulated in EIT’s Humane Endeavors.

GBI will have sustained and substantial funding to support the unique scale and ambition of its ground-breaking vision for engineering biology. GBI researchers will also be supported by cutting edge facilities including mass spectrometry, flow cytometry, sequencing, automation, scientific computing, bioinformatics, and machine learning. GBI will also have access to substantial compute resources that can be leveraged to further accelerate progress. The environment at GBI will allow researchers to undertake ambitious, long-term, collaborative research, and we will actively support the translation of research to commercial applications, where appropriate.

GBI will commence operations in 2025. The team will work from a purpose-made facility in the Oxford Science Park, currently under construction. Once complete, this state-of-the-art facility will include more than 40,000 m² of research laboratory and office space.

Ahead of the launch of GBI in Q4 2025, we are now accepting applications for Principal a0Investigator positions at all levels, including Senior Principal a0Investigator (equivalent to Tenured Professor) and Principal a0Investigator (equivalent to a Tenure-Track Professor) as we build a world-class faculty. We expect to make 5 or more appointments before the end of 2026, with further appointments in 2027 and 2028 as we scale.

**Ellison Institute of Technology, Oxford (“EIT”)**

EIT’s purpose is to have a global impact by fundamentally reimagining the way science and technology translate into end-to-end solutions and delivering these solutions in programs and platforms that respond to humanity’s most challenging problems.

EIT is investing significant resources in a new world-class research and development facility in the Oxford Science Park, including GBI. EIT is committed to cultivating a community where excellence is achieved through collaboration, trust, innovation and tenacity. We foster an environment where everyone’s experience and expertise are valued. We are curious and resilient in our efforts to drive long-term, sustainable innovation to meet humanity’s most enduring challenges.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- To set the research direction for your group and ensuring research activity is consistent with that direction and directly relevant to GBI’s vision.
- To recruit and manage a group of outstanding researchers, which may include postdocs, doctoral students (in partnership with the University of Oxford, we are establishing a doctoral programme in Generative Biology with up to 20 fully funded doctoral student positions per year), research assistants and other scientists.
- To mentor highly promising early career researchers to achieve the group’s goals and progress their aligned career objectives.
- To collaborate with other groups within GBI and with colleagues within the broader EIT family to deliver bold, ambitious and transformational research that would not be possible within an individual group.
- To help shape the facilities in GBI as part of the scientific strategy for delivering GBI’s vision.

## Requirements

**Essential Knowledge, Skills and Experience:**

- A PhD in a relevant scientific discipline, such as synthetic biology, computational biology and AI, microbial, plant and human cell biology, genomics, robotics and automation, and nucleic acids chemistry.
- A strong publication record in your field, demonstrating the ability to deliver bold, ambitious and transformational advances.
- Track record of building and managing collaborations, both internally and with external academic and/or industry partners, to enhance research capabilities.
- Strong communication and leadership skills, with the ability to engage with senior researchers, technical teams, and external stakeholders.
- We welcome applications from researchers who have experience running their own group as a Professor, Associate Professor, or Assistant Professor, and from those seeking their first independent position.
- We also actively encourage applications from those who have worked in an commercial setting, such as a biotech and companies leveraging AI for research.
- Assessment of applicants with respect to knowledge skills and experience criteria will be calibrated for career stage.
