Hyperlayer is the intelligent banking platform built for the agentic economy: the financial control layer that sits above banks' existing cores, enabling next-generation Smart Accounts, without ripping anything out. From a single integration, we give financial institutions a secure rules and orchestration engine that lets them design, launch and scale hyper-personalized products in weeks while preserving stability, compliance and control. And there's nothing like us anywhere in the world.
Hyperlayer works with Tier 1 and Tier 2 FIs across the UK, US, EMEA and Hong Kong, with an award-winning UK consumer app (HyperJar) sitting in the group. We're creating the fintech category that every bank in the world needs: programmable, governed, agent-ready accounts. Your job is to make sure our audiences know that.

About The Role
As Chief of Staff Associate, you'll work closely with our Chief of Staff and have high exposure to our COO and CEO, helping to keep Hyperlayer's most important corporate projects moving. You'll support everything from funding rounds and setting up our entities abroad to corporate governance, investor relations, legal operations and audits, while bringing structure and efficiency to how the business runs day to day. It's a varied, high-visibility role that offers a rare view of how a scaling fintech is run from the top, and as Hyperlayer grows there's real scope to take on greater ownership of projects and help shape how the Chief of Staff function evolves.
This is an office-based role, with regular in-person collaboration in the office.
What You'll Do
• Strategic corporate projects: Support the Chief of Staff on major strategic initiatives, including funding rounds and the establishment of our US entity, coordinating workstreams, tracking progress and keeping stakeholders aligned.
• Corporate governance: Help manage board and shareholder processes, including preparing board materials, maintaining statutory records and registers, and making sure governance requirements are met on time.
• Investor relations support: Act as a point of contact for investor data requests and administrative requirements, preparing accurate information and keeping our data room organised and up to date.
• Legal operations: Bring dedicated focus and structure to legal admin: managing the contract lifecycle, maintaining a central contract repository, tracking key dates and renewals, and coordinating with in-house counsel.
• Audits and client due diligence: Coordinate the company's response to audits and client due diligence requests, gathering documentation from across the business, managing timelines and making sure responses are accurate and complete. This work is periodic but substantial, so you'll be comfortable reprioritising when a large request lands.
• Internal communications: Plan and draft internal communications, such as company updates, all-hands materials and leadership announcements, helping keep everyone informed and connected.
• Operational efficiency: Identify opportunities to improve how we work, then design and roll out better processes, tools and documentation.
• Ad hoc projects: Take on a variety of projects as business needs evolve, working with teams across the company.
Qualifications
• 3–5 years of experience in a role such as business operations, company secretarial, legal operations, consulting, or a similar generalist position. 
• Experience at a B2B SaaS fast-growing start-up, ideally in fintech, is a must.
• Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage several workstreams at once and prioritize when needed.
• Clear, confident written communication, with the ability to prepare documents for audiences ranging from colleagues to investors.
• Close attention to detail and a careful, discreet approach to handling confidential information.
• Comfort working with people at all levels, including our CEO and COO, external advisers and investors.
• Experience supporting a funding round, investor reporting or a data room process.
• Familiarity with UK corporate governance and company secretarial requirements, such as Companies House filings.
• Exposure to audits, client due diligence or compliance questionnaires, particularly in fintech or financial services.
• Experience with international entity set-up.
• Experience using legal operations or contract management tools.
Using AI at Hyperlayer
Hyperlayer is hyper-focused on making the most of AI across every workstream, and this role is no exception. As Chief of Staff Associate, you'll be expected to use AI tools to work smarter and identify opportunities where AI could streamline our operational processes and help put those improvements into practice. We expect the person in this role to set the right example for the rest of the org on how AI can enhance and improve day-to-day work. 
Working at Hyperlayer
We value our team and we are proud to offer some great benefits:
• A performance-based employee bonus scheme.
• 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays, a day off on your birthday, and an additional day per year of tenure to a maximum of 30.
• Critical illness and life insurance cover.
• AXA PPP Health Insurance, including gym offers.
• Cycle-to-work scheme.
• Referral bonus scheme.
• Workplace nursery scheme.
How to apply
Please click on the 'Apply' button, you will be asked to provide an updated CV and answer some questions. For further information about this vacancy, you can contact us at people@hyperlayer.com.
Right to work
Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role unless stated otherwise.
Equity, diversity, and inclusion
Hyperlayer's mission is to make a positive impact on people's lives, making it easier for everyone to manage their money.
Hyperlayer's commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion is a key part of this; it helps us better serve our customers, employees, and business partners from every background.
We are constantly learning and striving to do better, and we expect all staff to actively take part in this process.
Data Privacy
As part of our recruitment process, Hyperlayer collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants.
We are committed to being transparent about how we collect and use this data and to meeting our data protection obligations. To read more click here.

About IFS Logistics
IFS Logistics helps enterprise shippers connect transport data, manage carrier spend, and automate execution. The product began as 7bridges and is now part of IFS, with a small, focused team working closely with the commercial organisation.
We build SaaS products that customers can run themselves. The platform handles busy, data-heavy logistics operations, so reliability and clear operational visibility matter every day.
The role
You will join Diego Silva, our Lead DevOps Engineer, as the second DevOps specialist responsible for the platform. You will take ownership of substantial workstreams while partnering closely with application and data engineers.
There is useful work to do from day one. We want every merge request reviewed, production deployments controlled, and releases running to a predictable cadence. Those practices are not yet consistent across the team. Our monitoring also needs to cover more of the application and data estate, and our pipelines need stronger detection, recovery and ownership when something fails.
You will help turn those goals into working systems: better signals, safer delivery paths, faster recovery and infrastructure the team understands. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys improving a live platform rather than waiting for a perfect starting point.
What you'll work on
• Build useful observability. Improve metrics, logs, traces and alerts across the Django API, data pipelines and warehouse so the team spots problems early and can diagnose them quickly.
• Improve CI/CD. Make GitLab pipelines fast, dependable and difficult to bypass, with review and deployment controls built into the workflow.
• Reduce operational risk. Remove direct-to-production paths, improve release controls and help the team establish a reliable weekly release rhythm.
• Manage cloud cost. Make GCP spend visible by workload and product area, then reduce waste without compromising service quality.
• Develop infrastructure as code. Improve our Terraform and Kubernetes setup so environments are reproducible, secure and clearly documented.
• Strengthen data-pipeline reliability. Add failure detection, freshness checks, replay paths and clear ownership across Datastream, Pub/Sub, dbt and BigQuery.
• Respond and learn. Help shape incident management and on-call practices, then turn recurring failures into automated checks and safeguards.

What we're looking for
• Strong experience running production services on GCP.
• Practical knowledge of Kubernetes and Terraform, including operating and improving infrastructure rather than only deploying to it.
• Experience designing and maintaining CI/CD pipelines in GitLab or a similar platform.
• Evidence that you have instrumented a real system and improved its metrics, logging, tracing or alerting.
• Examples of treating cloud cost as an engineering concern: attributing spend, finding waste and making informed trade-offs.
• Experience operating data pipelines, such as streaming ingestion, warehouse loads, dbt transformations or similar workflows.
• The confidence to challenge an unsafe change and explain what needs to happen before it can ship.
• Practical experience with AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude, including how you provide context and verify infrastructure changes before accepting them.
• The ability to assess an imperfect system, decide what matters most and carry the improvement through to production.
Nice to have
• Enough Python experience to investigate or fix issues in a Django application.
• Security or compliance work in an enterprise SaaS environment.
• Experience designing incident-management or on-call processes.
• BigQuery cost and performance tuning.
Tech stack
GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform and GitLab CI/CD. Python and Django REST, TypeScript, Node and React. BigQuery, dbt, Cube Cloud and Superset. Pub/Sub and Datastream. The team uses Cursor and Claude for development, Notion for specifications and Jira for delivery.
What success looks like in the first six months
• Our monitoring identifies production problems before customers report them.
• Pipeline failures are detected quickly, assigned clearly and recoverable without improvised fixes.
• Merge-request review and controlled production deployment are enforced through the delivery pipeline.
• Weekly releases run predictably without creating unnecessary overhead for engineers.
• GCP spend is attributable to workloads and product areas, with clear action taken on the main cost drivers.
• Application and data teams have a responsive platform partner who improves their ability to ship safely.
Why we're hiring now
The team is growing and the platform needs to support a faster pace of delivery. That requires better visibility, stronger data pipelines and release controls that work without relying on individual memory or manual intervention.
Diego currently carries too much of that responsibility alone. This role adds the capacity to improve the platform while still supporting the product in production, and gives the team another engineer who can take a problem, form a plan and see it through.

IFS Logistics (built and launched as 7bridges, now part of IFS) is an AI-native enterprise logistics platform. We unify transport data, optimise carrier spend, and automate execution for enterprise shippers and logistics companies. We're a small, dedicated team inside IFS, reporting into the commercial organisation rather than central R&D. Pure SaaS, zero consultancy.
The role
This is not a traditional "add AI to an existing system" role. You will own the product surface of our audit product end to end — the checks that tell a customer a delivery was late or a carrier charged them incorrectly, the queue where those findings get reviewed and actioned, and the self-serve configuration that lets a customer build their own checks without us.
Audit & Visibility is becoming a standalone product. A staff engineer leads the squad and brings the backend depth; you bring the product surface. You will set the approach for it, partner directly with the squad's Product Lead on product, and be the second technical voice in the squad. You are also the day-to-day mentor for the Junior engineer joining alongside you — that is part of the job, not an extra.
Your depth is frontend and product engineering. Every engineer here is expected to be genuinely fullstack; the profile describes where your depth is, not a boundary you stay inside. You will write Django, design the API contract you consume, and reason about what BigQuery and dbt are doing underneath your screens.
What you'll work on
• The audit review queue at real scale — tens of thousands of findings per tenant, filtered, triaged, actioned and evidenced.
• Self-serve check configuration: customers building, previewing and versioning their own audit checks. "Customers configure and manage it, not IFS" is a product principle, not an aspiration.
• Explainability for incorrect-charge detection — why this charge was flagged, against which rate card, at which version — reproducible months later for a dispute.
• The Django endpoints, data contracts and pagination behaviour behind all of it.
• Where the agent sits in each of these flows: agentic audit creation, human review at minimal, meaningful points, and the guardrails that make that safe against a customer's freight spend.

What we're looking for
• Around five to eight years building and shipping production software, with real depth in React, TypeScript, state and interaction design at scale.
• You have owned a product surface end to end including the ambiguity in it — you closed the open questions rather than waiting for someone to close them for you.
• Genuinely fullstack: you write the Python/Django side, you argue about the API contract, and you know when a client-side answer is the wrong answer.
• Strong on performance and scale in the interface: pagination, virtualisation, server-side filtering, and knowing which of those the data volume actually demands.
• You build human-in-the-loop and explainability interfaces and treat auditability as a feature, not logging.
• You raise the bar on other people's work. Review, pairing and direct feedback are things you do by default, and you are happy mentoring an engineer earlier in their career.
• AI-native in practice: Cursor and Claude daily, good at giving an agent the right context, better at spotting when its output is confidently wrong.
• You form and state a view. Ambiguity is the job, not a blocker.
Nice to have
• Design-system ownership, or working shoulder to shoulder with a designer on a complex data surface.
• Django REST, BigQuery, dbt, Cube Cloud, GCP.
• LLM agents, RAG or evals in production.
• Shipped an agent that does real work, like agentic audit or fulfilment-rule automation, and the instinct to build a simulation to prove the logic first.
• Logistics, supply chain, freight, or any finance-adjacent domain where being wrong costs money.
Tech stack
React, TypeScript · Python (Django REST) · BigQuery, dbt, Cube Cloud, Superset · Pub/Sub, Datastream · GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitLab CI/CD · LLMs, RAG, agent frameworks, evals · Cursor + Claude, Notion (SDD Central), Jira.
What success looks like — first 6 months
• You own the audit review and configuration surface end to end, and the open questions in it get closed by you.
• Self-serve check configuration is in production, with preview and versioning, and customers use it without us.
• The queue performs at the largest tenant's data volume, measured, not assumed.
• The Junior engineer in the squad is productive and shipping reviewed work independently, and can say what they learned from you.
• Quality standards in the squad are visibly higher: code review on all merge requests, no direct-to-prod, acceptance criteria per ticket — real, not aspirational.
Why this role exists now
Audit & Visibility is becoming a standalone product and the product surface is where its value is either visible or invisible to a customer. The Staff Engineer holds the backend and leads the squad; they cannot also be the only person setting the approach on the product side. We are shifting from feature-driven engineering to agent-led product architecture, and this is one of the surfaces where that shift has to actually land.

INEOS is a global manufacturer of petrochemicals, specialty chemicals and oil products with an overall turnover of about $55 billion and 25,000 employees. INEOS operate a large set of production units on 148 sites in 26 countries.

As one of the INEOS Business Units, INEOS Trading and Shipping (IT&S) is responsible for the supply of gas and liquid feedstocks to the INEOS assets as well as third party storage, shipping and trading of those feedstocks.

The trading activity includes the procurement, transportation and sale through complex supply chains involving pipelines, terminals, ships, barges and rail. This equates to thousands of bulk transportations per annum across our global supply chains.

WHY JOIN US?

IT&S has a strong ambition to grow its trading portfolio substantially over the coming years. The current mandate focusses on trading around assets and contracts in Europe, the US and China as well as proprietary paper and physical trading books.

The Quantitative Researcher role is an opportunity to join the front office of INEOS Trading & Shipping at an exciting point in its growth.

You'll join a lean and agile team where you'll have genuine ownership rather than simply maintaining established models and systems. You'll help shape how we use data, quantitative research and automation across Trading & Shipping, with the opportunity to build tools and analytical capability from the ground up.

ABOUT OUR OPPORTUNITY

The physical market is our core business, where we trade Ethane, Naphtha and LPG. We also require a strong view on Crude, Natural Gas, Oil Products and Freight. A key part of the role will be developing a deep understanding of Natural Gas Liquids (NGLs), the full refining barrel, and global shipping balances and trends, translating this insight into actionable trading opportunities.

The analysis team has three main purposes:

• Build and manage a suite of fundamental and quantitative models to support Traders whilst creating PnL value via trading strategies to inform the longer-term strategic direction across IT&S.

• Provide analysis and insight to IT&S teams to inform commercial decision-making.

• Deliver regular market intelligence updates to IT&S teams and management, to ensure they are kept updated and have support for commercial decisions.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

• Build and manage the IT&S data lake, organising complex and unstructured data to enable quantitative research across our Trading and Shipping activities.

• Develop robust data pipelines and quantitative models, turning complex datasets into advanced analytics and actionable trading insight.

• Create and own dashboards that clearly visualise data, model outputs and market trends, alongside more complex models focused on driving trading value.

• Lead the automation of existing and new processes as well as updating our systems to allow more time for creative trading and shipping analysis.

• Provide analysis and strategic insight for critical commercial negotiations and decision-making across Trading and Shipping teams.

• Utilise statistical models and automation to feed supply/demand balances across our traded products.

• Take ownership of process improvement and analytical projects, both short- and medium-term.

ABOUT YOU

You’ll enjoy working at the intersection of markets, quantitative analysis and technology. You're intellectually curious, commercially minded and comfortable taking ownership of ambiguous problems rather than waiting for a predefined solution.

We're looking for someone with:

• A Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics or a closely related quantitative discipline

• A genuine interest in commodity markets, quantitative research and trading

• Strong quantitative, analytical and modelling skills

• Strong Python skills for data analysis and modelling, including extensive experience with pandas and related libraries

• Experience in data visualisation/dashboarding, ideally Power BI

• An understanding of data engineering fundamentals including scheduling, automation, reproducibility, with a focus on building robust solutions that don’t fall over quietly

• Strong SQL and database skills, including data modelling, cleansing and optimisation

• Experience developing data pipelines and working with APIs

• The ability to learn new tools and business concepts quickly

• The ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to commercial stakeholders

• An inquisitive, collaborative mindset and the ability to operate effectively as priorities change

Desirable, but not essential

• Familiarity with cloud-based data infrastructure

• Knowledge of physical commodity or shipping markets

WHAT WE OFFER

Alongside the opportunity to build your career within a global Trading & Shipping business, our benefits include:

• 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays, with the option to purchase up to 5 additional days through salary sacrifice

• Contributory pension with employer contributions

• Free on-site gym

• Enhanced family leave

• Employee Assistance Programme

• Benefits platform offering a range of discounts

• Access to discounted private medical and travel insurance

• Salary sacrifice car scheme

• Cycle to Work scheme

• Employee referral bonus opportunity

Senior Manager, Data Transparency and Regulatory Disclosure
Global Regulatory Affairs Excellence, R&D
Director, Head of Regulatory Clinical Trial Excellence & Data Transparency
Paris, France & London, United Kingdom

WHAT - Summary & Purpose of the Position
Reporting to the Head of the Regulatory Clinical Trial Excellence & Data Transparency within GRA Excellence, the Senior Manager, Data Transparency and Regulatory Disclosure (DTRD) plays a strategic and operational leadership role in advancing Ipsen’s global clinical data transparency and disclosure agenda. This position serves as a subject matter expert, supporting cross-functional teams and strategic partners to ensure compliance with global and local transparency regulations, while fostering a culture of excellence, innovation, and collaboration.
Key Responsibilities:
• Lead or support the planning and execution of clinical data disclosure activities across public registries and regulatory platforms (e.g., CTIS, EMA Policy 0070, Health Canada PRCI).
• Act as the primary DTRD contact for assigned therapeutic areas (e.g., neuroscience, rare diseases, oncology), managing end-to-end disclosure processes and advising on regulatory requirements.
• Govern and support access to information requests under Freedom of Information (FOI) laws (e.g., US FOIA, EMA Policy 0043), ensuring timely and compliant responses.
• Manage relationships with external vendors supporting transparency, lay language summaries, and redaction services, ensuring quality, timelines, and budget adherence.
• Communicate complex strategic concepts clearly and effectively, tailoring messages to diverse internal and external audiences.
• Lead cross-functional collaboration to ensure transparency deliverables remain on track and within scope.
• Drive process improvements and implement new technologies to enhance operational efficiency and compliance.
• Contribute to regulatory intelligence, external engagement, SOPs and training material development to align with evolving global standards.
• Demonstrate thought leadership by presenting industry trends, benchmarking insights, and best practices to internal stakeholders and at external events.
• Proactively identify areas for improvement and develop strategic solutions to mitigate risks and maintain business continuity.

WHAT - Main Responsibilities & Technical Competencies
1. Management of Therapeutic Area (TA) Disclosure Activities
- Accountable for assessing the applicability of clinical studies and marketing applications for disclosure under US, EU, and other applicable regulations and Ipsen policy, and for planning and managing disclosure activities accordingly.
- Act as the DTRD TA lead for assigned therapeutic areas (e.g., neuroscience, rare diseases, oncology), offering expert guidance on disclosure requirements and best practices, while balancing compliance and transparency obligations with a global strategic perspective and the need to safeguard Ipsen’s interests.
- Review study protocols and product-related documents to identify confidential information and determine suitability for public disclosure.
- Act as study team member and participate in study and asset team meetings to raise awareness of disclosure requirements throughout the product lifecycle.
- Plan and coordinate the preparation of:
o Study information for public registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov, EU Clinical Trial Register, CTIS, EU RWD Catalogue).
o Lay protocol synopses and lay summaries.
o Anonymized/redacted documents for public registries, journal publications, or ad hoc requests.
o Anonymized/redacted package for clinical data publication under Policy0070 and PRCI.
o Access requests or response to access requests under FOI laws.
- Prepare response to agency queries related to CTAs, clinical data publication, and access requests.
- Maintain accurate tracking of disclosure activities and ensure documentation is up to date in systems such as eTMF, iDOC and relevant disclosure software.

2. Vendor Management & Partnership Oversight
- Oversee work delegated to preferred vendors supporting submissions to clinical public registries, preparation of lay summaries, and anonymization/redaction services.
- Act as the key point of contact for vendor coordination and dispatch project-related work in alignment with the Function Head guidance.
- Collaborate with vendors and internal stakeholders to optimize efficiency, ensure quality deliverables, and maintain strong partnerships.
- Monitor vendor performance to ensure adherence to quality and compliance standards, escalating issues to the Function Head as needed.
- Support the Function Head in planning and managing budgets for outsourced activities, including contract renewals and participation in procurement-led tender processes.

3. Global Operational Excellence & Transversal Activities
- Manage shared mailboxes for internal and public inquiries, ensuring timely and compliant responses.
- Develop and execute integration plans for new assets entering the pipeline.
- Support Function Head in cross-functional activities and/or projects, including:
o Governance of Ipsen’s data transparency activities across departments (i.e., including voluntary data sharing and publications).
o Oversight of Ipsen.com content related to clinical trials and transparency.
o Participation in steering committees and project kick-offs.
- Lead or contribute to process improvement and digital transformation initiatives to enhance operational efficiency in alignment with team and business needs, vision and global strategy.
- Work as key GRA/GRA excellence or DTRD contact on activities/project managed by other departments as agreed with Function Head and/or GRA LT.
- Contribute to Regulatory Clinical Trial Excellence activities, including supporting the coordination of regulatory governance routines and other CRO partnership or internal clinical trial workstreams and initiatives led or supported by Regulatory.

4. Quality & Compliance Activities

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of Quality Documents, including team-specific and cross-functional SOPs, as well as training materials, to support the effective implementation of disclosure processes and DTRD responsibilities.
- Act as Business Process Owner for assigned SOPs.
- Provide quarterly compliance and KPI reporting for the assigned portfolio of activities.
- Identify, escalate, and report compliance issues and risks, and manage quality events as required.
- Participate in audit and inspection readiness activities, acting as a subject matter expert. Serve as the DTRD point of contact during audits and inspections, as needed.

5. Regulatory Intelligence & External Engagement
- Monitor global regulatory developments and emerging industry standards related to clinical data transparency.
- Perform benchmarking and contribute to regulatory watch activities.
- Inform team and Function Head of relevant updates and their operational implications.
- Represent Ipsen in industry communities, conferences, and working groups to share insights and gather best practices.
- Contribute to the development of Ipsen’s thought leadership in transparency through external presentations and publications.

HOW - Behavioural Competencies Required)
• Ensures Accountability
• Communicates effectively
• Collaborates
• Excellence in execution
• Manages Ambiguity

HOW - Knowledge & Experience
Knowledge & Experience (essential):
• 5-7 years of experience in a transparency/disclosure or regulatory affairs position in the pharma industry.
• Comprehensive understanding of the R&D and Global Regulatory Affairs environment, drug development process, and transparency regulations and standards.
• Experience in project management, cross-functional collaboration, strategy/policy development, and education on best practices.
Knowledge & Experience (preferred):
• Experience in one of Ipsen’s therapeutic area: oncology, rare diseases, and neuroscience.
• Experience in Anonymization/Access to Information management.
• Experience in industry forums.
• Experience managing vendors and budget.
Education / Certifications (essential):
• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in life sciences

Education / Certifications (preferred):
• Master's or PhD in a discipline relevant to the pharmaceutical industry and regulatory affairs/clinical development.
Language(s) (essential):
• Excellent written and spoken English.

Hybrid in London / Remote within the UK



We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer

You'll own the Lending API in Germany, which banks, fintechs, brokers, and comparison sites build on to offer iwoca's finance to their customers. You'll decide how it evolves and help build the features that make partners choose iwoca.



The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.



The team

Introducer Tech builds the systems that partners in Germany use to refer businesses to iwoca. The aim is to get new partners integrated quickly and to make applying simple for their customers. The team also looks after how partners earn commission.

Its work covers three main areas:

 - The Lending API. Developing the versioned API and the webhooks that keep partners up to date on their customers.

 - The Introducer Portal. Building the web app that German brokers log in to, to submit applications and upload documents.

 - The sign-up journey. Improving how businesses apply and how well they convert, after a partner referral.

The team is growing to have two product managers, who each focus on either the broker or the partner flow, and three engineers across the backend and frontend, including this hire.

The team currently works in sprints, with three stand-ups a week and planning every two weeks. However, there is room to adapt how it works as it grows.



The role

You'll be the senior engineer behind iwoca's broker and partner channels in Germany, from the tools partners integrate with to the internal systems that broker account managers use.

Ownership and autonomy

 - Own the Lending API in Germany end to end, deciding what to build, when to release a new version, when to retire an old one, and what iwoca can promise partners.

 - Own the developer portal and every tool partners use to integrate, from documentation that their developers and coding agents can build from to self-serve testing that needs no help from iwoca.

Impact

 - Ship the features that make partners choose iwoca, starting with pre-qualification, which shows a customer what they could borrow before they apply.

 - Make integration quick and simple, so a partner can go live with few questions and little hand-holding.

 - Automate parts of the broker funnel and the internal CRM that broker account managers use, cutting friction and the lag between a decision and the action that follows, and building agents wherever they help.

Growth trajectory

 - Set the team's technical direction and shape the product and technical roadmap alongside the product manager.

 - Align designs with the UK engineers who share the API, so German requirements shape the design from the start.

 - As well as being hands on, you’ll develop your mentoring and coaching skills. You’ll help lead the team as the most senior engineer.

 - Backend engineering. You've designed and built production backend systems in Python – ideally with Django, though FastAPI or Flask count too. You've used PostgreSQL or another relational database in production, and kept it fast and maintainable.

 - Measurement. You've used data, metrics, or A/B tests to check whether a change had the effect you intended.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better.  - 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

 - A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

 - 3% pension contributions on total earnings.

 - An employee equity incentive scheme.

 - Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

job_title: Course Director: UX, UI, and AI
job_description:
You've been designing long enough to have watched tools become essential and then disappear. You know which design skills are timeless and which ones expire. **The human-centered design skills are where your heart is**, and you know that AI will take over much of the tool-based design work soon.

You see the fear around AI, and you understand where it comes from. But you also see the opportunities, and you want to show people how to work with AI in a way that benefits their lives, their users, and the world.

You can name the **ten leading designers** who should be teaching the world’s best courses and Master Classes right now. You know what each of them does better than anyone else, and where their gaps are.

Now you get the opportunity to decide what hundreds of thousands of designers learn next.

The industry leaders whose expertise you'll be turning into courses and Master Classes include **Don Norman and Vitaly Friedman**, as well as Design Leads at **Netflix, LinkedIn, Meta, and Adobe**. Don Norman also chairs our executive board.

You'll be involved in the entire process of creating our courses and Master Classes, and you'll lead many of the decisions, so there are incredible opportunities for you to **take initiative, make meaningful contributions, and grow**. Forget political struggles or long, pointless debates. You’ll be in a team with minimal distance between idea and action, where decisions are made ultra-fast.

## Join the Global Leader in Online Design and AI Education

IxDF is the world's largest online design and AI education platform, with over 1,150,000 enrollments since 2002. We hold the trust of industry giants like Adobe, NASA, and IBM, who rely on our courses to train their teams. Prestigious universities, including MIT and the University of Cambridge, integrate our material into their curricula. Help us **take online education to new heights** and **make a meaningful impact on humankind**.

At IxDF, we’re not just a company but a movement dedicated to making high-quality design and AI education accessible to everyone, everywhere.

We've pioneered online design education since 2002. We have over 1,150,000 enrollments and 1,583 company members, with more than 40 courses, 160 Master Classes, and thousands of open-source design resources, created by our team in collaboration with 240 industry leaders.

With learners from over 100 countries, your work will empower people worldwide.

## We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team

We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on:

- **Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI**: lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers. **This is the role described here.**

- **[Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI](https://ixdf.org/about/careers/education-designer-ux-ui-and-ai)**: lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there.

- **[Our Course Writers and Editors](https://ixdf.org/about/careers/course-writer-and-editor-ux-ui-and-ai)**: lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the user’s perspective.

We're a flexible team, and you'll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why.

**You, the Course Director**, decide what belongs in our curriculum and who should teach it. You reach out to the world’s leading experts, plan the courses with them, and shoot courses with them. When an Education Designer brings you a course outline, you're the one who says what's missing, what doesn't belong, and how to optimize the learning outcome so designers can succeed today. You'll work closely with our **Co-Founder**, your **Team Lead**, our other **Course Directors**, and the **Education Designers**, and you'll plan and create courses alongside them. Our Course Writers and Editors take the finished material the last mile: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team.

## Your Role at IxDF

- **Be a core part of our Editorial Team**. You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design.

- You'll research what already exists in a topic area, so that what we build is genuinely unique. You'll look at **where design and AI are heading, what designers need** that nobody has taught well yet, and **what we should retire** because the field has already moved on.

- **Find the people who should teach it.** You decide a topic is worth a course, you work out who should teach it and why, you write the email, and you get the yes. Then you plan the content with the industry leader and agree what the course must leave a learner able to do.

- **Decide what each expert should teach.** The best designers know a great deal, and a course that tries to capture all of it becomes an information dump. You develop a point of view on what a designer genuinely needs from them, and you hold the course to it.

- **You'll decide which skills our courses teach**, both to people entering design and to experienced designers leveling up. Our goal is to help designers thrive in the age of AI and work responsibly, so their users can thrive too.

- Ensure our course participants finish each course with a solid portfolio project they can show a hiring manager.

- **Help us decide what AI should do for our course participants**. Personalized learning paths, constructive AI feedback on portfolio work, practice environments where people run real design tasks and get feedback. You'll also help us improve the user flows on our own platform, so that learning at IxDF is as well designed as what we teach. You'll work on this with our founders, designers, and dev team.

- **Make an impact as you pressure-test the courses** our Education Designers plan. An Education Designer sends you a course outline, and you read it against everything you know about the field and about how people learn design, then give constructive feedback on what's missing, what doesn't belong, and where the structure can be improved. **You know the limits of your own expertise**, and you research your way past them before you weigh in. You'll also plan, structure, and create courses yourself, alongside them.

- You're one of the people **whose judgment the rest of the team leans on.** You show our Education Designers what ten or twenty years in the field taught you to look for. In return, our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, and our other Course Directors give constructive feedback on the courses you lead. You'll work in a **diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment** where you'll grow personally and professionally.

- **Act as guardian of our quality bar**. When a course goes out under our name, it has to be better than anything else available on the topic. On the courses and Master Classes you lead or review, you're the one who spots what's not good enough yet and works with the team to fix it.

- **Bring your subject matter expertise** to our writers, community managers, and social media team, so our design thinking stays consistent across everything we publish.

- **You help produce Master Classes**. We produce 3 per month. Over email, you reach out to designers whose work you admire, invite them to create one with us, plan the content, and produce the live session. **Timelines vary enormously:** with Don Norman or Vitaly Friedman it can be two weeks from first email to publication, because we work with them often. With a new expert, it can be half a year. Once the session is recorded, you get the footage and the transcript, and you decide with the Education Designers and Team Lead which existing course benefits from which snippets, and where they go.

- **Focus on what matters** as you take raw expert video material, course and Master Class transcripts and footage featuring global industry leaders, and turn it into educational material that teaches new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design. You'll work across UX design, human-computer interaction, design thinking, UI design, psychology, and AI.

- **Design for a diverse, global audience.** Some of our courses and Master Classes serve working designers who want to grow into more senior work. Others serve people moving into design from other fields. Often, a course will serve both in the same lesson. Getting both right without watering either down is a rewarding design challenge.

- Give the video team **constructive feedback** on course and Master Class videos, from on-screen text and b-roll to graphics and animation, so each video is engaging to learn from and accurate from a design perspective.

- **Fly out and meet the global industry leaders in design in professional studios across the world.** You'll shoot the course content there with some of your colleagues. Expect this a few times a year at minimum. Some of us love that part and join every studio production; others keep it to those few trips. Both work for us. On average **we shoot 4-6 new courses per year.**

- Expect to have several courses moving at once at different stages: one you're planning with an expert, one being shot, one in production, and one published course that you're reviewing and improving.

- **Find room for improvement** by looking at completion rates, learner feedback, and the portfolios course participants produce, then go back and fix what isn't excellent yet. Use the power of incremental, modular design as you help push the quality of our educational materials to new heights, surpassing even the very best in industry and academia. We're always learning, always improving, always raising the bar in everything we do and ship.

- **Maintain and improve our crystal-clear documentation** so our knowledge resources stay up-to-date, easy to find, and provide instant value to our internal teams. Clarity is key. Any line of documentation should be self-explanatory.

- We're proud to have assembled **a remarkable team of unicorns** who uplift, motivate, and push each other to excel daily. There's a seat open for someone who shares our passion for excellence. Could that be you?

## About You

- You have at least **10 years of hands-on design experience. Thirty is not too many.**

- You have a **network among designers you respect**, and you're **comfortable writing to someone you admire** and presenting them with an opportunity.

- You know what the design community wants to see, and what it needs to learn.

- You're kind, and you have the **social intelligence and empathy to** engage well with very different kinds of people. Much of this job is convincing busy, accomplished people that what we're building is worth their time.

- **You can show us something you built or led**: a product, a design team, a course, an AI teaching app, or a conference track. We're excited to hear what it was, your thinking behind it, how long it took you to create, what went wrong, and how you improved it.

- You can take a **broad, complex design practice and turn it into a step-by-step learning sequence** that'll make a beginner feel and act confident. You can look at a plan for teaching something and **see what's missing** before anyone builds it.

- You're a **practical idealist**. You know how to create great results through incremental quick wins and MVPs, and you know when to go all in and make something perfect.

- You’re a **forward thinker** who isn’t afraid to innovate and try new things before others have.

- You **collaborate with AI in everything you do**. You use AI to research, structure, write, and create faster, and you know how to take **human leadership**, so the **outcome is 100% yours** and better than you could have created without AI.

- You’re **eager to help people build UX and UI skills** because you know they’re more relevant than ever in the age of AI.

- You can **teach a career changer** the powerful skills of great design, and you can **guide an experienced designer** in upskilling. Perhaps you've mentored people, or you’ve run your own company helping clients level up.

- You **give constructive feedback people can act on**, and you can tell a talented colleague how they can improve their work without them becoming defensive.

- You're genuinely **curious** about how AI is changing design work and design education.

- You're **fluent in written and spoken English** and you can explain complex ideas clearly.

- You’re enthusiastic about learning by doing and are **committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills**.

- You **spot problems** before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report.

- You **value teamwork**, prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals and harmony in the workplace.

- You're **self-motivated**, and you love **creative freedom**, **independent judgment**, and the **responsibility** that comes with both.

- You’re driven by the desire to **make a positive impact in the world** and to improve the lives of others.

- If you still love designing in Figma and building interfaces with AI, there's room for that here. Some of our Course Directors design hands-on; others have moved fully into direction. Both work for us.

- Most of the work happens from your **home office,** but you're **willing to travel a few times a year** to shoot courses.

- You're located in a **time zone** between UTC-6 (Austin, Chicago) and UTC+8 (Singapore, Perth), which includes all of Europe.

## Bonus Points

None of these are required, but each of them would make us even happier.

- You've **led a design team.**

- You **publish your own thinking on design**: articles, a book, educational material, a blog, or a social media presence.

- You've **spoken at design conferences**, or you're on a first-name basis with people who do.

- You've **created design systems**. Organizing complex material so other people can put it to use is a lot of what you'll be doing.

- You've worked as an **editor**, or you've created **online courses**.

- You have the graphic design skills to create image-based and interactive content for courses, articles, and social media.

- You've **built AI-supported learning tools** yourself, or you've used AI to build products.

- You hold a **bachelor's or master's** degree in UX, UI, HCI_,_ AI, or a similar field.

- You’ve **collaborated with video production teams**.

## What We Can Offer

- **A highly valued role**: You'll shape our core product, our courses and Master Classes.

- **Reach and impact that are difficult to find anywhere else in this field.** A design leader might shape the work of thirty people on their team. Your decisions about what we teach will reach hundreds of thousands. They'll build better careers and design a better world for all of us.

- **Access:** the designers you'd normally see on a conference stage are the people you'll email, plan with, and sit across from in a studio. Our name opens doors. An email from IxDF gets read, so the reach you have now is the floor, not the ceiling.

- **Autonomy**: Nobody will ever hand you a template and tell you to fill it in.

- A **global, purpose-driven team: work remotely** alongside passionate professionals from all over the world, united by a **common mission** to create the best possible design and AI education in the world and make it accessible for everyone.

- **Our co-founder and co-CEO, Rikke, will work closely with you**. She and our other co-founder, Mads, built IxDF from nothing, with no investment capital, so we would stay free to make world-class design education affordable to everyone. She was the sole editor and video editor for many of our early years, so she's shaped our course planning, expert interviews, video shoots, and content editing from the inside. She's still hands-on in everything we do, and she still films educational videos herself, in places like the US, the North Pole, and Nepal.

- A **full-time position** within a fully remote organization. Video-based collaboration with your colleagues from elsewhere on the planet, and we get together in person each year, on a team trip or for a studio production.

- Bi-weekly **knowledge-sharing sessions** and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work.

- A work culture with no **fluffy titles, political agendas, or corporate drama**. Your colleagues value **your warm character, your strong work ethic, and the results you deliver**. If you embody old-school virtues of always striving to deliver results, learn and become better every day, you'll thrive at IxDF.

- A daily mission to help impact, **empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people** by creating **affordable high-end design education** for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too.

- **Colleagues with four to forty years of experience**, and a culture where we follow the best idea, not the longest résumé.

- A company **where the distance between idea and execution is minimal.** We're a highly agile organization with **zero bureaucracy or corporate politics** – and with **exceptional order and efficiency**.

- A company culture where **passion meets high performance and excellence**. To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process, **you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline**.

- We thrive because we have a **hands-on attitude and a bias towards action** as opposed to fluff-filled, unrealistic strategies. You'll need **crisp execution skills yourself** and the ability to **impress your colleagues with concrete results**, just like they'll impress you.

- We built online design education before people believed in it. AI is now changing what designers do, and they carry a bigger responsibility than ever. You'll be at the **forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it**. You'll help **set a direction** that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world.

**How to Learn More and Apply**

To submit your application as well as learn more about our Work Culture and Values, please visit [https://ixdf.org/about/careers](https://ixdf.org/about/careers)

Please apply as soon as you can. We’re firm believers in “the sooner, the better” and we look forward to working with you!

## Join Our Mission

Are you a high performer **with heart** who wants to help millions of people design better lives?

Then we'd love to meet you!

## Your Role at IxDF

- **Be a core part of our Editorial Team.** You'll collaborate with IxDF editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design.

- **Design for a diverse, global audience.** Some of our courses and Master Classes serve working designers who want to grow into more senior work. Others serve people moving into design from other fields. Often, you'll teach both in the same lesson. Getting both right without watering either down is a rewarding design challenge.

- **Make an impact as you decide how the courses you lead come together.** You establish what a course participant should be able to do by the end of a course, then you plan, structure, and create the core content that gets them there. What comes first, what builds on what, and how people level up step by step with ease and joy from confused to competent. You'll work across UX design, human-computer interaction, design thinking, UI design, psychology, and AI.

- Design the exercises, portfolio activities, design templates, and assessments that **turn passive watching into active designing**. You write the exercises that make a course participant apply an idea to their own portfolio project, the templates that scaffold that work, and the assessments that reveal whether they understood and can apply it, or whether they just watched. You write the headings and hooks your structure calls for, and our Course Writers and Editors own the final wording. Every course should leave a participant with a portfolio case study they can show a hiring manager.

- **Set and raise the standard for our assessments,** so a correct answer proves understanding, not just recognition, and a good question teaches as well as tests.

- **Make expert knowledge understandable.** You take raw expert video material, course and Master Class transcripts and footage featuring global industry leaders, and turn it into educational material that teaches timeless human-centered design and AI.

- **You help produce Master Classes.** We produce 3 per month. Over email, you reach out to designers whose work you admire, invite them to create one with us, plan the content, and produce the live session. **Timelines vary enormously**: with Don Norman or Vitaly Friedman it can be two weeks from first email to publication, because we work with them often. With a new expert, it can be half a year. Once the session is recorded, you get the footage and the transcript, and you decide with the Course Directors and Team Lead which existing course benefits from which snippets, and where they go.

- You **plan the course content in collaboration with the global industry leaders** in design and then **fly out to meet them in professional studios across the world**. You'll shoot the course content there with some of your colleagues. Expect this a few times a year at minimum. Some of us love that part and join every studio production; others keep it to those few trips. Both work for us. On average **we shoot 4-6 new courses per year.**

- **Our courses combine written and video lessons.** You'll work closely with the video team, giving constructive feedback on on-screen text, b-roll, graphics, and animation, and telling them which takeaways need a visual, so each video is more engaging to learn from and accurate from a design perspective. You'll also work closely with our growth team.

- **Balance the big picture with the smaller details.** Expect to focus on **one large course creation project per quarter**, alongside small, continuous improvements to what's already published.

- **Find room for improvement** by looking at completion rates, learner feedback, and the portfolios course participants produce, then go back and fix what isn't excellent yet. Use the power of incremental, modular design as you help push the quality of our educational materials to new heights, surpassing even the very best in industry and academia. We're always learning, always improving, always raising the bar in everything we do and ship.

- **Maintain and improve our crystal-clear documentation** so our knowledge resources stay up-to-date, easy to find, and provide instant value to our internal teams. Clarity is key. Any line of documentation should be self-explanatory.

- **You won't do this alone.** You'll work with our Course Directors, your Team Lead, and our Co-Founder to pressure-test the structure: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether it holds together. You'll work in a diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment where you'll grow personally and professionally.

- **We’re committed to excellence,** and we seek a like-minded enthusiast to join us. This role is not for the average. Ahead of you is a highly rewarding and enriching journey.

- We're proud to have assembled a **remarkable team of unicorns** who uplift, motivate, and push each other to excel daily. There's a seat open for someone who shares our passion for excellence. Could that be you?

## About You

- You have at least **5 years of hands-on design experience**.

- You've **facilitated workshops** repeatedly, run a beginner course, mentored designers, or built curricula for online courses.

- You can **show us something you built**: a course, a workshop series, live Master Classes, an AI teaching app, or a mentoring program. We’re excited to hear what it was, why you built it the way you did, and how long it took you to create.

- You can take a **broad, complex design practice and turn it into a step-by-step learning sequence** that’ll make a beginner feel and act confident.

- You can teach the same idea in different formats: a 60-minute workshop, a written lesson, a 90-second video. You know what a medium does well and what it can't carry, and you know what to cut when the format gets shorter.

- You're a **practical idealist**. You know how to create great results through incremental quick wins and MVPs, and you know when to go all in and make something perfect.

- You **collaborate with AI in everything you do**. You use AI to research, structure, write, and create faster, and you know how to take **human leadership**, so the **outcome is 100% yours** and better than you could have created without AI.

- You know the difference between **timeless human-centered design skills and skills in tools that change**. You’re passionate about the first, because they’re the most interesting to you and you know that AI will take over much of the tool-based design work soon. You’re eager to help people build UX and UI skills because you know they’re more relevant than ever in the age of AI.

- You can **teach a career changer** the powerful skills of great design, and you can **guide an experienced designer** in upskilling to a more senior role.

- You're genuinely **curious** about how AI is changing design work and design education.

- You're kind, and you have the **social intelligence and empathy** to engage well with very different kinds of people.

- You're **fluent in written and spoken English** and you can explain complex ideas clearly.

- You’re enthusiastic about learning by doing and are **committed to putting in the effort to continuously improve your skills**.

- You **spot problems** before anyone else notices them, and when something goes off track you come back with a solution rather than a report.

- You **value teamwork**, prioritize collaboration, and focus on collective goals. You give constructive feedback that others can act on, and you take it the same way. When someone shows you how your idea could be better, you're interested rather than defensive.

- You're **self-motivated**, and you love **creative freedom**, **independent judgment**, and the **responsibility** that comes with both.

- You’re driven by the desire to **make a positive impact in the world** and to improve the lives of others.

- Most of the work happens from your **home office,** but you're **willing to travel a few times a year** to shoot courses. You're located in a **time zone** between UTC-6 (Austin, Chicago) and UTC+8 (Singapore, Perth), which includes all of Europe.

## Bonus Points

None of these are required, but each of them would make us even happier.

- You've **published** educational material under your own name or **spoken** at design conferences.

- You've worked with an **LMS or an online learning platform**.

- You've **built AI-supported learning**: tutors, adaptive paths, automated feedback. Or you’ve used AI to build products.

- You hold a **bachelor's or master's** in UX, UI, AI, or a similar field.

- You have your **own blog or social media page** where you create and share original content.

- You have **collaborated with video production teams**.

- Bi-weekly **knowledge-sharing sessions** and 4 meeting-free days weekly for focused work.

- A daily mission to help impact, **empower, and enrich the lives of millions of people** by creating **affordable high-end design education** for everyone across the planet. It'll be yours too.

- **Colleagues with four to forty years of experience**, and a culture where we follow the best idea, not the longest résumé.

- A company **where the distance between idea and execution is minimal.** We're a highly agile organization with **zero bureaucracy or corporate politics** – and with **exceptional order and efficiency**.

- A company culture where **passion meets high performance and excellence**. To help us improve the world, and yourself in the process, **you'll need grit, strong work ethic, long-term thinking, and self-discipline**.

- If you want even more opportunities to show the world what you can do, you’re in luck! When you're willing to do the hard work of learning and growing, then you’ll find virtually **limitless opportunities with us.**

You'll be at the **forefront of teaching designers to work with AI and to design responsibly for it**. You'll help **set a direction** that shapes both the designers we teach and the people who use what they build. Together, we'll design a better world.

What This Job Involves

The Governance Lead owns the end-to-end governance framework for the account, ensuring a robust, multi-layer governance structure and meeting cadence is in place to oversee successful programme delivery and a transparent, high-trust partnership between the client and JLL. Where the role has historically been coordination-led, it is now scoped as a strategic ownership role: the Governance Lead is accountable not only for tracking and reporting performance, but for driving the KPI framework itself — setting direction on what is measured, how it is governed, and how outcomes translate into improvement action across the account.
The role brings together contract governance (Master Service Agreement / Appendix 9 compliance, change control, escalation management) with performance and KPI ownership (design, tracking, reporting and improvement planning), giving the account a single senior point of accountability for how governance and performance are managed and evidenced.

Reporting line: Reports directly to the Global Account Director.

The role will be based in the UK and require regular attendance at the London office.

Strategic Scope

• Act as the single senior owner of the account's governance framework and its performance narrative — connecting contractual governance obligations to measurable business outcomes for both HSBC and JLL.

• Set the direction for how KPI and performance data is used across the account: not just reporting the numbers, but shaping what is measured, why, and what action it should drive.

• Provide HSBC Executive Management and JLL leadership with a credible, evidence-based view of contract health, governance and KPI risk, and performance trends.

• Represent governance and performance management as a strategic capability within the account, rather than a purely administrative or reporting function.

Key Responsibilities

Governance Framework & Contract Compliance
• Own the account's governance structure and meeting cadence, ensuring alignment with MSA / Appendix 9 (Governance) requirements.

• Ensure MSA governance requirements are adhered to across the account, tracking that all required meetings and forums take place.

• Own the change control process, ensuring it is robust, consistently followed and appropriately documented.

• Ensure escalations are raised to the appropriate governance forum and resolved in a timely manner.

• Ensure annual goals and objectives are mutually agreed with the client and cascaded through the organisation.

• Collaborate with other Tier 1 partners to ensure consistency of governance approach across the wider platform and programmes.

KPI Ownership & Performance Management
• Own the account's KPI framework end-to-end: definition, data sourcing, tracking, reporting and improvement action planning across all functional leads and disciplines.

• Hold functional and regional leads to account for KPI performance, driving a consistent, evidence-based approach to performance management across the account.

• Partner with JLL's Business Intelligence team to design and maintain efficient, effective KPI tracking and reporting tools that evidence performance and compliance against the MSA.

• Analyse year-to-date metric variances; recommend and implement corrective actions and improvement plans, and track them through to resolution.

• Maintain a deep working knowledge of contract KPIs and reporting requirements, acting as the escalation point for KPI-related queries.

• Own the client survey process end-to-end — design, deployment, performance tracking and resulting action planning.

• Provide reporting on the agreed cadence to give HSBC Executive Management clear visibility of performance against KPIs and broader contract health.

Business Reviews & Reporting
• Own tracking and reporting of the Operational Responsibility Matrix (ORM), which defines the scope of services under the contract at market level, ensuring it remains accurate, current and aligned to contractual scope.

• Coordinate and prepare Quarterly (and other cadence) Business Reviews, incorporating feedback and driving continuous improvement in format and content.

• Own collation of regional data, updates and progress into a single, coherent account-level view.

• Own management and submission of the Account Business Plan.

Governance & KPI Risk Management

Risk ownership under this role is scoped specifically to risk arising from KPI performance and the operation of the governance framework itself. Wider account, operational, health & safety, and commercial risk is owned by other functions and is out of scope for this role.
• Identify and track risks arising from KPI underperformance or adverse metric trends, and recommend corrective actions (e.g. targeted improvement plans, process change) to bring performance back on track.

• Identify and manage risks to the integrity or effectiveness of the governance framework itself — e.g. gaps in meeting cadence, non-adherence to MSA governance requirements, weaknesses in the change control process — and drive resolution through the appropriate governance forum.

• Maintain a governance and KPI risk log, ensuring issues are escalated appropriately and tracked through to closure.

• Escalate any risk identified outside this scope (operational, commercial, health & safety, or other) to the relevant risk owner promptly, rather than managing it directly.

Continuous Improvement
• Shape and deploy a process management mentality that leverages JLL best practice, acting as the go-to person for governance process and principles at all levels.

• Drive ad hoc projects to improve efficiency, engagement and/or performance across the account.

• Promote the exchange of best practice to and from JLL; showcase JLL innovation, including facilitating relevant speakers or subject-matter input into governance forums.

• Create, develop and deliver best-in-class training and reference materials (e.g. MSA / contract overview documentation) to support account and transition teams.

• Maintain a structured communication plan to drive governance adoption and roll out new initiatives from Regional Operations, following up until adoption is achieved.

KPI Ownership Matrix

The table below sets out the areas in which the Governance Lead holds direct ownership of KPI definition, tracking and improvement action — as distinct from areas where performance data is contributed by functional leads but governed centrally by this role.

Monthly MSA / Appendix 9 compliance tracking & compliance evidencing
Monthly / Quarterly Account-wide performance KPIs framework design, tracking & improvement planning
Owns the process design, deployment & action planning per survey cycle for Client satisfaction (survey programme)
Ongoing / as raised process governance & documentation in Change control
Ongoing / as raised identification, escalation routing & resolution tracking (KPI and governance-framework risk only) for KPI & governance risk register
Annual, tracked quarterly, submission & progress tracking of the Business Plan delivery
Quarterly / as scope changes tracking & reporting of contracted scope at market level for the Operational Responsibility Matrix (ORM)
Per agreed cadence, owns consolidation & narrative for leadership for Executive reporting

Core Competencies

• Understands the drivers of value and risk within KPI performance and the governance framework, and the impact of changes in contract scope.

• Strong understanding of governance frameworks, operational processes and operating governance models, including change control.

• Able to use data to build a case and communicate a clear, evidence-led narrative — comfortable in the detail and confident presenting a structured argument.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills; a strong, structured communicator able to advise and influence senior client leadership, SMEs and JLL leadership.

• An enthusiastic, positive collaborator, able to work effectively across a distributed team regionally or globally.

• A proactive, continuous-improvement mindset, with the ability to simplify complex issues to influence stakeholders at all levels and secure approvals.

Required Skills & Experience

• Significant experience in governance, PMO or contract management within a large, complex account.

• First-hand experience of contract management and managing governance structures and processes.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging senior client leadership.

• Clear, measurable track record of managing and improving process performance.

• Technically proficient in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).

• Excellent organisational, reporting and facilitation skills; able to multi-task and prioritise effectively.

• Flexible and adaptable to change; able to work independently as well as within a team.

We are searching for the best talent for an Associate Director, Safety Analysis Scientist, located in Maidenhead, United Kingdom. This is a hybrid position that requires you to be on site three days a week.

Purpose:

The Associate Director (AD) Safety Analysis Scientist (SAS) provides scientific expertise and leads the safety assessment of assigned products. The AD SAS, in partnership with the Medical Safety Officer (MSO), is responsible for the preparation of scientific safety analysis and evaluations, which are required for regulatory compliance and to aid in safety-related decisions for marketed products and products in development.

The AD SAS will support product Safety Management Teams (SMTs) and work in close collaboration with other cross-functional safety partners to determine a product’s safety strategy, complete safety analyses and evaluations, proactively review safety data/lead safety data review meetings and interpret safety information to make a recommendation, supporting SMT deliverables as required.

The AD SAS will assist the Medical Safety Officer (MSO) with activities related to the SMT and with contributions to key safety and clinical documents.

This is a practical, junior-to-mid-level role supporting the Group Data Protection Officer (DPO) and the wider Legal and Data Protection team by managing core privacy workflows across the Group.
The post-holder will own the day-to-day operation of key data protection processes — including DPIAs, data subject rights requests, personal data breach triage, supplier and data processing agreement reviews, and governance reporting. The role operates with a degree of autonomy over process and workflow, escalating legal, high-risk, contentious and regulated-business matters to the Group DPO or Legal for decision.

Key responsibilities
DPIAs and privacy by design
• Operate the DPIA screening process and maintain the central DPIA register

• Review screening questionnaires and identify when a full DPIA is required

• Facilitate assessments with project and business teams, documenting processing, necessity and proportionality, risks, mitigations, owners and review dates

• Escalate high residual risk, novel processing, international transfers, AI use, special-category data and proposed prior consultations to the Group DPO

Data subject rights requests
• Log, acknowledge and coordinate DSARs and other rights requests

• Agree search scope with relevant business areas, maintain response timetables and track disclosure materials

• Support the review, redaction and preparation of responses

Personal data breaches
• Receive and triage incidents promptly

• Coordinate containment, fact gathering, investigation records and root-cause analysis

• Maintain the breach register and notification timetable

Supplier and DPA reviews
• Conduct first-pass reviews of data processing agreements and supplier privacy due diligence

• Check core Article 28 UK GDPR requirements, including security evidence, sub-processors, international transfers, breach assistance, audit rights and exit arrangements

Governance, advisory and awareness
• Support ROPA, data mapping, policy updates and privacy champion engagement

• Act as point of contact for routine operational data protection queries from the Group's non-regulated businesses

• Monitor legislative and regulatory developments and propose updates to templates and processes for Group DPO approval

Essential
• 1–3 years' practical data protection, compliance, legal operations or privacy experience

Desirable
• IAPP CIPP/E, CIPM, BCS or equivalent privacy qualification (or active progress towards one)

• Exposure to DPA negotiation, international transfers, AI governance or privacy-by-design reviews

• Familiarity with SharePoint, workflow tools and data-mapping or privacy-management platforms

What we offer

• Exposure to a broad range of data protection matters across multiple business lines

• Hybrid or fully remote and flexible working arrangements
