We are looking for an experienced analytical scientist to join our Innovation team at LGC Assure in Fordham. This is a hands-on role focused on independently developing, optimising and validating analytical methods using LC-MS, troubleshooting complex analytical challenges and developing new testing solutions to support our specialist laboratories.
Working across different areas of the business, you will take ownership of method development projects from initial investigation through to validation and implementation. You'll need strong practical LC-MS expertise, a structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to deliver robust analytical solutions within a busy commercial testing environment, balancing multiple projects and deadlines.
If you enjoy solving complex analytical problems, developing new approaches and working collaboratively to turn scientific challenges into practical solutions, this could be an excellent opportunity to make a direct impact on our scientific capabilities.
What you'll be doing
• Independently develop, optimise and validate analytical methods using LC-MS, taking ownership of projects from initial feasibility and method development through to validation and implementation.

• Troubleshoot complex analytical challenges, identifying root causes and developing practical solutions to improve method performance and analytical reliability.

• Develop and optimise extraction methods and sample preparation workflows to meet different sample matrix and testing requirements.

• Configure, operate and optimise LC-MS instrumentation to generate reliable, high-quality analytical data.

• Analyse and interpret complex scientific data, identifying trends, investigating issues and supporting evidence-based decisions.

• Support innovation projects across the business, working with laboratory teams to develop new testing capabilities and improve existing methods.

• Manage multiple projects and competing priorities, delivering high-quality outputs within agreed timelines.

• Produce clear scientific documentation, including technical reports, validation summaries, standard operating procedures and project updates.

• Present scientific findings and project outcomes confidently to internal teams and external customers.

• Support customer discussions by explaining analytical approaches, providing scientific insight and contributing to technical solutions.

• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance laboratory processes, analytical methods and ways of working.

• Maintain accurate records and ensure work is completed in accordance with ISO 17025 requirements and applicable quality standards.

You are an experienced analytical scientist with strong practical LC-MS expertise and a track record of developing and improving analytical methods. You're comfortable taking ownership of scientific challenges, investigating problems independently and working with colleagues across different disciplines to deliver effective solutions.
You enjoy working in a fast-paced laboratory environment where scientific quality, customer requirements and delivery deadlines are equally important.
You will have:
• A degree in Chemistry or a relevant scientific discipline.

• Significant, recent hands-on experience using LC-MS instrumentation in an analytical laboratory.

• Demonstrable experience independently developing, optimising and validating analytical methods, rather than solely operating established methods or providing instrument support.

• Practical experience troubleshooting analytical methods and instrumentation, identifying root causes and implementing solutions.

• Experience developing extraction methods and sample preparation workflows.

• Experience working in a busy analytical laboratory, ideally within commercial testing, contract testing or a similarly delivery-focused environment.

• A sound understanding of chromatography and analytical method validation principles.

• The ability to interpret complex analytical data and communicate scientific findings clearly.

• Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, prioritise competing demands and deliver to deadlines.

• Excellent written communication skills, including experience producing technical reports and scientific documentation.

• Confidence presenting scientific information to a range of audiences, both internally and externally.

• A collaborative approach, with the ability to work effectively as part of a team while independently managing your own workload.

• Knowledge of ISO 17025 accreditation standards and laboratory quality systems.

• Experience with GC-MS/MS, high-resolution accurate mass (HRAM) analysis, or anti-doping, sports medication or supplement testing would be advantageous but is not essential.

You'll join a specialist scientific team where your expertise will directly contribute to developing new analytical capabilities and solutions that support our customers and the wider business. The role is responsible for the operational engineering leadership to all areas of the section to meet the required performance levels via sustainable improvements in engineering standards and equipment reliability. 

You are responsible for developing, maintaining, and continually improving the equipment & maintenance systems and procedures to deliver improved performance across the Section. 

The role will be accountable for the Section M&R Budget, controlling costs to achieve optimal Safety, Quality, GE and Waste performance as well as strong, visible on the floor leadership & strategic planning. 
Reporting to the Section Lead, the role requires strong relationships with Technical Leads and Shift Technicians & business partnering to the Operations Managers (Cell Leads) for both Crème egg & Chocolate Making. The role is part of the PM Pillar team for the site 

How you will contribute 

Safety & Compliance 
• Own and lead the cell's safety programmes — including Equipment Safety, Process Safety, Contractor Safety, Isolation Awareness, Engineering Workshop Management, Permit to Work, and Complex Management — driving the required workflows and improvement plans. 
• Ensure all relevant statutory and regulatory requirements are fulfilled through robust preventive maintenance plans. 

Maintenance Strategy & Planning 
• Partner with the Cell Lead and Technical Lead to manage maintenance planning and day-to-day maintenance activities. 
• Develop and continually improve AM and PM schedules through routine review and data-driven refinement. 
• Drive the creation and implementation of Standard Maintenance Procedures (SMPs) across your section. 
• Conduct equipment criticality assessments and establish optimized maintenance strategies accordingly. 
• Work with the Cell Technical Lead to develop maintenance plans, procedures, and checklists for routine tasks, shutdowns, and major overhauls — identifying resources, estimating time and costs, and coordinating with external contractors where required. 
• Plan and lead significant maintenance outages, rebuilds, and re-life activities. 

Continuous Improvement & IL6S 
• Operate as an active member of the PM Pillar, adopting IL6S tools and implementing effective maintenance standards. 
• Collaborate with cell teams and other leaders to tackle top-loss problems, agree best practice, and roll it out consistently. 
• Support continuous performance and productivity improvements across the section (GE, Waste, etc.). 
• Actively participate in design reviews and Maintenance Prevention workshops. 

Quality 
• Maintain a full understanding of all Quality Procedures relevant to equipment performance, and a working knowledge of all others within the operation. 
• Partner with Quality and Cell Teams to identify and reduce quality-related losses. 

Technical Documentation & Obsolescence 
• Maintain up-to-date technical documentation for all section equipment, incorporating every improvement or modification. 
• Manage equipment obsolescence in your area — develop the replacement roadmap, drive masterplan actions, and prepare CAPEX proposals. 

Projects & Cost Management

What’s the role 

Shell UK Mobility & Convenience operates one of the UK's largest company-owned retail networks, with the convenience shop proposition playing a critical role in customer experience, non-fuel sales, margin delivery, waste control and network profitability. 

As the Inventory Planning Manager, you will be accountable for managing product forecast exceptions to improve convenience retail product availability, inventory health and order proposal replenishment performance across the Shell UK convenience retail network. You will lead the optimisation of forecasting and replenishment capability through the RELEX platform, ensuring the right products are available at the right time while balancing sales growth, waste, working capital and operational efficiency. 

This is a business-outcome focused role, expected to own performance, shape planning governance, influence cross-functional priorities and translate data, system recommendations and operational insight into practical action that improves customer experience and strengthens profitability. 

Success in this role will be measured through the following business outcomes: 
• Improved on-shelf availability and reduced lost sales across priority customer missions and categories. 
• Improved inventory productivity through stronger stock cover, replenishment parameters and working capital discipline. 
• Reduced waste, markdown exposure and stock obsolescence, particularly in fresh, chilled, frozen, food-to-go and other high-volatility categories. 
• Improved forecast accuracy and replenishment effectiveness through high-quality data, clear governance and robust planning routines. 
• Stronger delivery of commercial plans, including promotions, seasonal events, range changes, new product launches and delists. 
• Increased adoption and maturity of Relex as a core business planning capability across Convenience Retail & Services.

• Availability and sales protection: Own availability and replenishment performance across the network, identifying risks to customer availability, lost sales and commercial delivery and prioritising action where intervention creates the greatest business value. 
• Inventory optimisation: Balance availability with stock cover, waste and working capital by maintaining effective replenishment parameters, reviewing inventory productivity and challenging overstock or understock positions. 
• Relex capability ownership: Lead the business use, governance and continuous improvement of Relex forecasting and replenishment processes, ensuring system recommendations are reviewed, challenged and translated into effective business action. 
• Exception-based planning: Establish and lead daily and weekly exception-management routines that focus attention on the highest-value issues across demand, supply, stock, data, supplier service and site execution.

- explore creative concepts

- accelerate production workflows 

- improve creative quality and efficiency

- Contribute to creative briefs and campaign planning. 

- Share ideas openly and help solve creative challenges together. 

- Support the continual evolution of our content pipeline. 

Help Shape the Future 

We're constantly evolving how we create content. 

You'll help us: 

- improve creative workflows 

- evaluate emerging AI tools 

- identify opportunities for automation 

- share knowledge across the team 

- raise the quality and efficiency of digital fashion production

Within your first six months you'll have: 

- Delivered multiple fashion collections into Avakin Life. 

- Developed AI-powered workflows that improve creative efficiency. 

- Become a trusted contributor within the Content Development team. 

- Helped evolve our digital fashion pipeline. 

- Contributed ideas that improve player engagement and commercial performance. 

- Shared knowledge that helps others adopt new creative tools and techniques.

- Have a genuine passion for fashion and digital creativity. 

- Stay curious about emerging technologies. 

- Enjoy experimenting with new ideas. 

- Balance artistic creativity with commercial thinking. 

- Take ownership of your work. 

- Collaborate openly and generously with others.

- Experience developing AI workflows, prompt libraries or creative automation.

About

• Own problems end to end, from discovery and design to production and iteration. You take initiative instead of waiting to be told.

• Partner with Product and Design to shape what we build, focusing on outcomes for customers rather than sheer output.

The role will work closely with business services stakeholders across the firm (including the firm’s Chief Information Officer, Director of AI & Innovation, Head of Information Security and COO).

This will include developing and maintaining contract templates, policies and guidelines to streamline contract management processes, and providing appropriate training to internal stakeholders.

You will also support the Chief Risk & Legal Officer and the Risk team on wider legal and regulatory risk matters, including data protection compliance (such as data subject requests and data breaches), reviewing client terms and proposed amendments to the firm’s terms of business, and updating risk policies.

You will also mentor and support junior members of the team.

- draft, review, and negotiate a wide range of commercial contracts, including supplier agreements, service contracts, IT software, hardware, licensing and SaaS agreements, including for AI products and services or products involving AI-enabled features, NDAs and licensing agreements;
- provide strategic legal advice during contract negotiations to minimise risk and ensure favourable terms for the firm;
- identify and assess potential legal risks in contracts and procurement activities, proposing risk mitigation strategies;
- ensure that all contracts comply with applicable laws, regulations, and the firm’s policies; and
- develop and maintain contract templates, policies, and guidelines to streamline contract management processes.

- advise on and oversee the legal aspects of the firm’s procurement processes, ensuring compliance with internal policies and applicable laws;

• The drive to push AI forward across people, processes and product – with measurable results.

• Solid security, compliance and resilience fundamentals.

• A habit of writing things down, and the standing to hold architecture decisions and explain them to leaders, partners and investors alike.

**About the role**

You will play a key role in designing, implementing, and maintaining our clients’ cloud infrastructure, ensuring it is secure, scalable, and highly available. You will provide dedicated cloud and infrastructure support within your team.

## Key responsibilities

Delivery of high quality cloud-based technical solutions for our clients:

- Collaborate within cross-functional teams to implement cloud architectures that meet the client’s requirements around scalability, performance, and security
- Deploy and manage cloud resources, containers, and related services using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools like Terraform or CloudFormation
- Configure and maintain networking, security, and access control in the cloud environment
- Implement and maintain robust security practices to protect data and resources in the cloud environment
- Develop and maintain automated processes for provisioning, monitoring, and scaling cloud resources, including the use of CI/CD pipelines to streamline application deployments
- Monitor cloud infrastructure for performance bottlenecks and proactively optimise resource usage
- Implement load balancing, caching, and content delivery solutions to ensure high availability and performance
- Design and maintain backup and disaster recovery solutions to ensure business continuity in the event of system failures or data loss
- Create and maintain runbooks including configuration management and standard operating procedures
- Provide high tier support for client applications and infrastructure, including occasional on call cover
- Ensure any necessary compliance standards are met and certifications are maintained 

Evangelising the adoption of cloud technology and adherence to prescribed best practices:

- Evaluate and recommend cloud services, tools, and solutions to meet common client scenarios
- Stay up-to-date with industry trends and emerging technologies, and share knowledge with the team
- Collaborate with other teams within Made Tech to ensure alignment with cloud best practices

## Skills, knowledge and expertise

## **Essential**

- Prior experience in a cloud engineering role, with a strong foundation in successfully building and deploying services in the cloud
- Knowledge of cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure and GCP
- Hands on experience delivering software and knowledge of modern software engineering best practices
- Experience with containerisation and orchestration tools (e.g. Docker, Kubernetes) 

## **Desirable**

- Experience working in a technology consultancy environment
- Experience working within multidisciplinary teams with product, design, and technical disciplines all successfully collaborating
- Relevant cloud certifications such as AWS Cloud Practitioner, Developer, DevOps Engineer, Security, Advanced Networking or Azure Developer, Security, DevOps, Network Engineer
- Knowledge of cloud vendor partner programs, such as AWS APN and Azure Partners
- Experience with well-architected frameworks
- Knowledge of UK public sector technology guidance and frameworks, such as NCSC’s Cyber Assessment Framework (CAF) and the Technology Code of Practice (TCoP)
- Familiarity with Python, Bash and Javascript
- Agile practices such as Scrum, XP, and/or Kanban
- Experience using Test Driven Development (TDD)

Lead the Experience Design aspects of one or more of our client engagements. Partner closely with user researchers, interaction designers, content designers, engineers, data analysts, and client product owners to make ongoing, recommended improvements that drive better user and business outcomes. ## Job description

Made Tech helps UK government and public sector organisations build better digital services - and security is central to that mission. As a Lead Security Engineer in our Cyber practice, you'll be the most senior security engineering voice on client engagements, setting technical direction for how organisations design, build, and defend secure systems. You'll work across complex government programmes where the stakes are real: services that affect citizens, systems that hold sensitive data, and teams that need to move quickly without cutting corners.

This isn't a role where you sit at the edge of delivery reviewing outputs. You'll be embedded in multidisciplinary teams, shaping how security is engineered into everyday work - from threat modelling and architecture at design time to hardened, monitored systems in production. You'll build trusted relationships with client engineering leads, platform teams, and senior stakeholders, translating between deep technical decisions and the trade-offs senior leaders need to understand. You'll bring the judgement to know when a heavyweight security architecture is warranted and when a lighter-weight, faster-moving approach serves the engagement better. 

At Lead level, your impact extends beyond the immediate team. You'll establish security engineering standards and reference architectures across engagements, grow the technical capability of the people around you — colleagues and client engineers alike — and contribute to how Made Tech's Cyber practice develops as a community. If you'd rather build the paved road than police the off-road, who treat security as an engineering discipline rather than a compliance exercise, and who cares about leaving client teams genuinely stronger than you found them, this role is for you. 

## Key responsibilities

- **Own end-to-end technical security architecture across engagements.** Design secure-by-default reference architectures, set patterns for identity, network, and data protection, and maintain living technical standards — feeding directly into how teams build, not just how they're audited.
- **Lead vulnerability remediation as an engineering programme.** Define the prioritisation framework — drawing on EPSS, KEV, CVSS, and asset criticality — set remediation SLAs, own the risk-acceptance register, and drive fixes directly into delivery backlogs alongside product teams. Report programme KPIs (MTTR by severity, backlog age, coverage, recurrence rate) to senior stakeholders.
- **Drive security into the team's normal engineering rhythm.** Embed threat modelling, secure code review, SAST, SCA, dependency policy, and container scanning into design and delivery cycles — building the tooling and automation that make this the default, not a specialist handover at the end of a sprint.
- **Navigate UK government security standards with confidence — as an engineer, not a paperwork exercise.** Design systems and controls that satisfy the NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework, GovAssure, Cyber Essentials, and HMG Security Policy Framework, applying them proportionately across engagements as guardrails that enable safe delivery, not barriers to it. Engage with government security communities and coordinate with departmental technical teams.
- **Communicate security risk in terms that drive engineering decisions.** Report system posture, remediation programme performance, and architectural risk to senior client stakeholders — tailoring the frame for the audience and structuring reports around the decisions the reader needs to make, not just the findings.
- **Set the standard for incident response and detection engineering.** Build and drive adoption of detection, alerting, and IR tooling across engagements, own the IR-to-vulnerability-management feedback loop, and coordinate cross-team exercises including known-exploited-vulnerability scramble drills.
- **Grow the people around you.** Mentor colleagues across the practice and at client organisations, pair on complex or unfamiliar engineering problems, and create structured development opportunities — including for client engineers who may not yet have strong security habits. 

- **Contribute to Made Tech's Cyber practice beyond delivery.** Shape practice standards, contribute to hiring and technical calibration, build and share expertise externally, and help grow a security engineering community that raises capability across the organisation.

## Skills, knowledge and expertise

**Essential**

- Deep hands-on experience designing and building secure cloud architectures (AWS, Azure, or GCP) at scale, including IAM, network segmentation, and data protection patterns.
- Proven track record embedding security tooling and automation into CI/CD pipelines and engineering workflows across multiple teams.
- Strong proficiency in at least one programming/scripting language, used to build production-grade security tooling (not just scripts).

**Desirable**

The following would strengthen your application. We don't expect every candidate to bring all of these.

**Certifications**

- OSCP, OSWE, or equivalent offensive security credential
- AWS/Azure/GCP security specialty certification
- CKS (Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist)

**Capabilities and experience**

- Experience establishing and operating vulnerability remediation programmes at organisational scale — including risk-based prioritisation using EPSS, KEV, and asset criticality, and driving fixes across multiple delivery teams.
- Evidence of designing systems that satisfy UK government security frameworks — GovAssure, CAF, Cyber Essentials, HMG Security Policy Framework — in a complex multi-supplier or multi-team environment, as an architect rather than an assessor.
- Experience conducting or coordinating technical security reviews and penetration testing in UK public sector contexts, including remediating findings and briefing senior technical stakeholders.
- Working knowledge of exposure management beyond CVE-only approaches — incorporating misconfiguration, identity exposure, and attack-path analysis using cloud-native tooling (AWS Inspector, GuardDuty, Security Hub, or equivalents).
- Experience securing software supply chains — SBOM generation, dependency provenance, artifact signing — and integrating this into build pipelines rather than a standalone assurance process.
- Experience building or shaping security engineering capability within a consultancy, programme delivery, or multi-client environment — including growing technical skills in colleagues and client teams.
- Evidence of acting as a trusted technical adviser to senior client stakeholders — anchoring recommendations on engineering outcomes, challenging briefs constructively, and making security value visible through what gets shipped.
- Experience setting team ways of working in iterative delivery environments — establishing retrospective cadences, collaborative problem-solving norms, and pairing practices that spread security knowledge across the team.

**Tooling and practice familiarity**

- Deep familiarity with structured threat modelling approaches — STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK, attack trees — and experience embedding these into agile delivery ceremonies.
- Experience integrating SAST, SCA, dependency scanning, and container security tooling into CI/CD pipelines as part of a shift-left security approach, including building custom tooling where off-the-shelf doesn't fit.

- You're comfortable working both collaboratively and on your own as location and task requires.

Job Description:
Customer Experience Strategist
CX, Service Design & UX | UK Hybrid

We’re looking for a Customer Experience Strategist to join Remedy Edge’s growing Experience team.

This is a hands-on strategy role sitting across customer experience, service design, digital product thinking and UX.

You’ll help us understand what patients, HCPs and other healthcare audiences need, identify where experiences aren’t working, and translate those insights into better journeys, services, tools and digital experiences.

What makes the role different?
Our Experience team often works upstream of traditional creative and production.

One project might involve understanding friction across a complex patient or HCP journey and redesigning the service around it. Another might involve helping define a new digital tool, platform or support experience, developing its architecture and user flows, prototyping how it could work and testing the concept before it moves into full design and build.

So we’re looking for someone comfortable moving between: research → CX strategy → service design → UX → prototypes → testing.

You won’t need to be a UI designer or developer. But you should understand experience and UX deeply enough to help define what should be created, why it matters and how it should work.

What you’ll be doing:
· Develop customer journeys and experience strategies.
· Identify customer needs, behaviours, barriers and opportunities.
· Create journey maps, service blueprints and future-state experiences.
· Help design new services, tools and digital experiences.
· Develop UX principles, information architecture and user flows.
· Work with wireframes and prototypes to make ideas tangible.
· Contribute to concept and usability testing.
· Facilitate workshops and confidently work directly with clients.
· Collaborate with designers, creatives, technologists and developers.
· Work on global programmes that create master experiences for local markets to adopt and adapt.
· Contribute to pitches and the continued growth of Remedy Edge’s Experience offer.

What we’re looking for:
You will have extensive relevant experience across areas such as Experience Strategy, CX, service design, UX strategy, digital product or service design, or digital transformation.

You’ll have strong human-centred thinking and be comfortable taking work from an ambiguous customer problem towards a practical experience solution.

We’d particularly like to see experience in:
· Customer or user research.
· Journey mapping.
· Service design.
· UX principles.
· Information architecture and user flows.
· Wireframes or prototyping.
· Client-facing strategy and workshops.
· Collaborating with design and technology teams.

Experience with Figma or similar design and prototyping tools is useful. Curiosity about AI-enabled prototyping and new ways of making and testing ideas is encouraged.

Healthcare experience would be helpful, but it isn’t essential. We’re also interested in people from agencies and consultancies working across complex, service-led or regulated industries.

Why Remedy Edge?
We’re building Experience as a strategic capability that connects CX, service design, product thinking and UX, rather than treating UX simply as downstream design or production.

That means you’ll get the opportunity to help clients decide what experience should exist and how it should work, then make that strategy tangible enough to prototype, test and ultimately build.

Job summary:
Working within the Engagement Strategy team, the Senior Engagement Strategist is responsible for leading the development of integrated, omnichannel engagement strategies and customer experiences for our clients’ brands.

At its core, the role is about understanding audiences, their behaviours and needs, and the environments in which they engage with healthcare brands. The Senior Engagement Strategist brings together audience insight, customer experience, channel strategy, content, data, technology and measurement to create clear, actionable engagement strategies that deliver against client and brand objectives.

The Senior Engagement Strategist will lead engagement strategy projects and pitches from brief interpretation through to strategic development and client-ready recommendations, working with oversight from senior leadership where appropriate. They will collaborate closely with media, data and analytics, creative, technology and account teams to turn strategic thinking into practical, integrated campaign plans.

About you:
You’re a strategic thinker who understands how people engage with healthcare brands and can turn complex information into clear, actionable recommendations. You’re confident working across the full omnichannel ecosystem and understand how audience needs, content, channels, data, technology and measurement connect to create effective customer experiences.

You’re comfortable taking ownership of a project from brief through to recommendation, while bringing the right people together to strengthen the thinking. You can confidently engage clients, lead workshops and present your point of view, and you know how to balance strategic ambition with practical delivery.

You’re curious about people, behaviours, technology and the changing healthcare landscape. You’re collaborative by nature, able to work effectively across disciplines, and are ready to provide guidance and support to more junior members of the team.

Essential Functions:
Engagement Strategy
• Lead engagement strategy projects and pitches end-to-end, turning complex or unclear briefs into a clear strategic approach and activation-ready, client-ready recommendations, with little senior oversight.
• Develop integrated omnichannel engagement strategies and customer experiences across HCP, patient and wider healthcare audiences.
• Apply audience segmentation, persona development and behavioural/customer insight to inform engagement strategy, synthesising qualitative, quantitative, attitudinal, behavioural and performance evidence alongside relevant data, research and market inputs.
• Develop engagement frameworks across the customer journey or adoption ladder, identifying key moments, barriers, triggers, content needs and engagement opportunities, and translating these into clear strategic priorities and actions.
• Develop channel strategies across markets and specialties, defining the role of paid, earned, shared and owned touchpoints and translating channel analysis and audience behaviours into actionable omnichannel plans.
• Define how engagement should be sequenced and orchestrated across moments, including messages, content needs, behavioural triggers, channel roles and next-best actions.
• Develop joined-up omnichannel ecosystems that define how content, channel roles, data flows and technology work together across those moments, including how CRM, tracking, personalisation, behavioural triggers, next-best actions and audience-specific content delivery can tailor engagement across channels.
• Develop both global and local customer engagement strategies, including launch planning and optimisation of established brands.

Client Leadership & Workshops
• Build strong and trusted relationships with clients, acting as a strategic engagement partner and confidently articulating the agency's point of view.
• Design and facilitate client workshops that move strategic thinking forward, including audience development and prioritisation, journey mapping, channel planning, tactical ideation and engagement ecosystems.
• Present complex thinking clearly and persuasively, challenging assumptions where appropriate and turning strategic recommendations into a clear course of action.
• Identify engagement opportunities within existing and prospective client business and help shape the strategic response, contributing to organic growth and new business.

Cross-functional Activation
• Work closely with media, data and analytics, creative, and account teams to turn engagement strategy into practical, integrated campaign plans.
• Bring together, brief and challenge specialist inputs across media, data, technology and other disciplines, ensuring they contribute to a coherent, customer-centric engagement strategy and activation-ready plan.
• Inspire and empower creative teams by providing a clear strategic foundation for ideas that can work effectively across channels.
• Develop relationships with relevant external partners, platforms and technology providers where appropriate.

Measurement & Optimisation
• Define KPIs, learning agendas, optimisation frameworks and reporting requirements in partnership with data and analytics teams as part of the engagement strategy.
• Use performance data and learning to identify opportunities to optimise customer experiences, channel activity and engagement plans.
• Build learning and optimisation loops that help teams refine the experience and improve future activation based on performance.
• Stay abreast of developments in data, technology, platforms and healthcare engagement to identify opportunities for innovation and effectiveness.

Team Contribution
• Support the development of engagement strategy capabilities across the wider team through knowledge sharing and by providing guidance and constructive support to more junior team members within project work.
• Share relevant learning and developments in omnichannel engagement, customer experience, data and innovation across the agency.
• Model high standards of collaboration, responsibility, accountability and inclusive working.

What you'll bring:
• Strong relevant experience in digital and omnichannel engagement strategy, with healthcare or pharmaceutical experience and a strong understanding of HCP, patient and wider healthcare audiences.
• A proven ability to independently own complex engagement strategy work from an ambiguous brief through to a high-quality, actionable client deliverable, while working with little senior oversight.
• Strong strategic storytelling and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex information simple and create clear, compelling, decision-ready recommendations.
• Confidence engaging senior clients, facilitating decisions and bringing together multidisciplinary teams without relying on formal authority.
• Strong analytical and organisational skills, with curiosity, rigour and sound judgement in interpreting audience, behavioural, market and performance evidence.

We are looking for an experienced Business Analyst to support the design and implementation of the future operating model for the Office of the CIO, with a particular focus on technology risk management, governance, controls and SMF24 compliance.
This is a hands-on transformation role requiring someone who can work across Technology, Risk and senior stakeholders to translate regulatory and risk-management requirements into a practical and sustainable operating model.

The role will help define how the Office of the CIO operates in BAU, including its governance structure, accountabilities, decision rights, risk and control processes, management information, committee framework and escalation routes.

The successful candidate will combine strong business analysis and target operating model experience with practical knowledge of technology/operational risk, governance and the Senior Managers & Certification Regime (SM&CR).

About the Job

What you’ll spend your time doing

Operating Model & Governance
• Support the design of the target operating model for the Office of the CIO.
• Assess current governance, risk, control and reporting arrangements and identify gaps against the required future state.
• Define future-state capabilities, processes, roles, responsibilities, decision rights and operating procedures.
• Establish clear interfaces between Technology, the Office of the CIO, Risk, Compliance and other governance functions.
• Develop governance structures, committee arrangements and Terms of Reference, including membership, decision rights, escalation routes and reporting requirements.
• Support implementation and transition of the new operating model into BAU.

Risk Management & Controls
• Support the development of the CIO/Technology Risk Management Framework and associated standards.
• Define risk ownership, control ownership, risk processes and governance requirements.
• Develop clear accountability across Lines 1, 1.5 and 2, including RACIs and escalation routes.
• Review existing risk and control processes, identifying gaps, duplication and unclear accountability.
• Support the definition of risk identification, assessment, acceptance, monitoring and reporting processes.
• Ensure risk and control information is effectively incorporated into CIO governance and management reporting.

SMF24 & Regulatory Governance
• Translate SMF24 responsibilities and accountabilities into effective governance, processes, controls and management information.
• Map SMF24 accountabilities to governance forums, controls, decision rights and escalation routes.
• Develop responsibility and accountability mapping that demonstrates clear ownership and oversight.
• Support the establishment and mobilisation of governance forums required to support SMF24 responsibilities.
• Ensure the operating model supports appropriate governance evidence and demonstrable management oversight.

Business Analysis
• Facilitate workshops with Technology, Risk and senior stakeholders.
• Elicit, analyse and document business, governance and regulatory requirements.
• Produce current and future-state process maps, RACIs, capability models and operating model documentation.
• Perform gap and impact assessments.
• Translate complex risk, regulatory and technology concepts into clear, concise documentation.
• Develop options and recommendations to support senior management decisions.

What you’ll need

We are looking for someone who can operate at the intersection of technology, risk, regulation and operating-model design.

You should be comfortable moving from high-level operating model discussions with senior stakeholders into the detail of processes, controls, RACIs, governance forums and management information.

Most importantly, you will bring a pragmatic mindset. The objective is not simply to document regulatory requirements, but to turn them into clear, workable governance and risk-management arrangements that can be embedded successfully into BAU.

For this particular role there are some important qualifications and experience we need you to have. These include:

Essential 
• Strong Business Analyst experience within financial services or another highly regulated environment.
• Proven experience designing or implementing target operating models.
• Practical experience of technology risk, operational risk, governance and controls.
• Working knowledge of SM&CR, ideally including direct exposure to SMF24.
• Experience translating regulatory requirements into processes, controls, governance and accountabilities.
• Experience designing governance structures, Terms of Reference and committee arrangements.
• Strong understanding of the Three Lines model and the interaction between first and second-line risk functions.
• Experience creating process maps, RACI/accountability matrices, governance frameworks and control documentation.
• Strong workshop facilitation, analytical and stakeholder-management skills.
• Excellent communication skills and confidence working with senior Technology and Risk stakeholders.

Desirable 
• Previous experience within an Office of the CIO, Technology Risk or CIO Governance function.
• Experience supporting an SMF24 holder or equivalent senior accountable executive.
• Experience developing executive or Board-level risk and governance reporting.
• Experience delivering governance or risk capabilities as part of a major transformation.
• Insurance or London Market experience.

Description
We are a research-driven biopharmaceutical company. Our mission is built on the simple premise that if we “follow the science”, great medicines can make a significant impact to our world. We have an exciting opportunity for a new Associate Principal Scientist to join our Oncology health economic modeling team in the Health Economic and Decision Sciences group. The preferred location for this role is West Point, PA; although alternate locations may be considered, including Rahway, NJ; Boston, MA; the UK, and Switzerland. Hybrid and flexible work arrangements are possible, consistent with local office and country policies.
The Health Economic and Decision Sciences (HEDS) department is part of our Company’s Biostatistics and Research Decision Sciences (BARDS) organization. BARDS is responsible for strategic design and analysis to enable informed decision making in the discovery, development and delivery of our Company’s innovative products, and is a leader in quantitative scientific methodology and its application to enable the targeting, discovery, development, manufacturing, and marketing of drugs and vaccines for the benefit of patients and global public health. In collaboration with internal and external partners, the BARDS-HEDS department specifically provides strategic and technical leadership to enable patient access, measure and quantify the value of our Company’s products, inform internal and external decisions, and shape methodology and external health policy and practice. This position will focus on health economic modeling for oncology products.

Role
Under the direction of an HEDS Senior Director, the Associate Principal Scientist provides strategic development and use of industry-leading predictive and economic models to enhance our understanding of disease and to quantify and communicate the value of our oncology products to patients, providers, and payers.

ABOUT MUBI

MUBI is a global streaming service, production company and film distributor dedicated to elevating great cinema. To make this possible, we create, curate, acquire and champion visionary films, bringing them to audiences all over the world. We have a team of brilliant, dedicated and passionate people to help bring our mission to life. From London to New York, Istanbul to Paris, and Berlin to Mexico - we work together to realize MUBI’s vision.

That’s where you come in! Join our global team and help us make great cinema accessible to everyone, everywhere.




ABOUT THE ROLE

MUBI reaches its members directly through its owned and operated surfaces, as well as through a wide set of partners/vendors: streaming platforms, channels, OEMs, telcos, cinemas, publishers and brand partnerships. We are reshaping our Business Development function to focus on a number of larger, strategic bets, and we are looking for the leader who will own it.

You will inherit a portfolio of partnerships, a clear mandate to concentrate it, and the backing of the executive team to pursue the handful of deals that can further accelerate MUBI's subscriber and revenue trajectory. You will set the strategy for the function, originate and negotiate its most important agreements, and hire and mentor a Business Development Manager who takes on day-to-day operations and the smaller partnerships so you stay on the deals that carry the largest opportunity.

The role reports directly to the Chief Product Officer, because most of what we want to do next (subscription bundles, membership benefits, platform and device relationships, our cinema programme) is built in close partnership with Product.

We work hybrid-remote where we require 3 office days in London and New York. Our core days are Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday, with the flexibility to use our offices on the remaining two days if you wish.




WHERE YOU’LL HAVE IMPACT:

In your first months, you will audit the existing partnership slate with Product, Engineering, Finance and Data, make the keep-or-retire calls on partnerships that consume integration and operations effort without a clear return, and set the bar for what qualifies as a Business Development opportunity at MUBI: does it reach an audience that already looks like a MUBI member, is there an identifiable revenue or retention mechanism rather than exposure alone, and is the effort proportionate to the upside once integration, operations and marketing lift are counted.



From there, your work falls into three areas:

 - Fewer, bigger strategic partnerships. You will originate and lead a small number of large deals, such as Channels, OEM partnerships, and subscription bundles with Tier 1 premium streaming services as the anchor: one subscription, two catalogues, shared subscriber economics and joint marketing. You will know who to call, build the case, run the negotiation and mobilise Product/Engineering, Marketing, Finance and Legal behind the agreement.

 - Membership value, in both directions. MUBI is launching a premium membership tier. You will source the partner benefits that make it worth paying for, with a simple bar: something a film lover would otherwise pay for separately, that fits our curatorial brand. In the other direction, you will place MUBI inside the memberships of quality media and lifestyle brands whose readers look like our members, with attribution that tells us what each partnership produced.

 - Commercial ownership of MUBI GO. MUBI GO gives members a cinema ticket every week, and it is central to our premium proposition. You will own its commercial side: the relationships and terms with cinema partners, volume pricing, new forms of value for members, expansion of the partner base in current markets, and the recommendation on which markets we take it to next. Product and Engineering own the operational execution; the commercial leadership sits with you.



Concretely, you will:

 - Define and own the Business Development strategy, portfolio and OKRs, and report on them to the executive team.

 - Originate, structure and negotiate strategic partnerships end to end, from first conversation to signed agreement to commercial performance after launch.

 - Own the commercial relationships and terms behind MUBI GO, and lead the expansion of its cinema partner base.

 - Build the benefits and partner portfolio for MUBI's premium membership tier, and the programme that places MUBI inside other organisations' memberships.

 - Work with Finance on business cases and the independent review of deal economics, and with Product and Engineering on what each partnership requires in capacity and sequencing.

 - Hire, mentor and develop a Business Development Manager, and build the function's operating rhythm.

 - Represent MUBI with senior counterparts at partners, and bring back a clear read on where each relationship stands and what needs a decision.





WHAT YOU’LL BRING:

 - You have spent significant time originating and closing large commercial partnerships in streaming, subscription media, consumer technology or entertainment, and you have the network that comes with it.

 - You are a natural networker rather than a traditional salesperson. You read a company's value proposition quickly and translate it creatively into deal structures that work for both sides.

 - You push a negotiation to its limit without putting the relationship at risk, and you are not afraid to walk away from a deal that is not good enough.

 - You are as credible with a studio executive as with a cinema operator or a brand partner, and equally comfortable with your own senior stakeholders, including the CEO.

 - You judge yourself on a small number of deals that moved the numbers, not on volume of activity.

 - You bring structure and rigour to a function that has not always had it: a clear portfolio view, honest business cases, crisp reporting and follow-through after signature.

 - You are hungry, you want a mandate you can shape, and you are ready to lead a function rather than a desk.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience.

 - 10+ years in business development, partnerships or commercial strategy, including several years leading strategic partnerships at a streaming, subscription, consumer technology or entertainment company.

 - A track record of originating and closing large, complex commercial agreements (bundles, distribution, licensing or membership partnerships), and of being accountable for their performance after launch.

 - Strong commercial and financial judgement: you can build and defend a business case, model deal economics and prioritise a portfolio.

 - Experience managing and developing people, or clear readiness to do so.

 - Exceptional written and verbal communication, including the ability to present recommendations to our C-Suite and board.

 - Comfort working across time zones and offices with a high degree of autonomy.

 - Direct experience negotiating subscription bundles or channel partnerships with major streaming services or telcos.

 - Experience with theatrical exhibition, cinema partnerships or ticketing.

 - Experience in US, UK, EMEA and Latin American markets.

 - Experience with AI tools in your own workflow.

 - A real connection to cinema and to MUBI's curatorial point of view.

We're hiring a **C++ developer** to work primarily on engraving within the MuseScore Studio team. This is hands-on, experienced independent contributor role with lots of autonomy. You'll take on ambiguous, complex problems and see them through from design to shipping and long-term maintenance.

MuseScore Studio is free, open-source software used by millions of musicians, students, and composers worldwide, so the code you write here has a lot of impact and is used by an active community of creators around the world.

## Key responsibilities

- You'll work on the layout and rendering engine that turns musical data into beautifully typeset, readable scores. It's one of the most interesting and rewarding problems in the product: the difference between a score that looks professionally published and one that just barely conveys the notes. The team is responsible for:
- Domain model - representation of elements of music theory as objects in code (including parts)
- Engraving - arrangement and drawing of objects on the canvas
- Playback - generating events for a synthesizer from objects
- Editing - changing objects and their relationships, taking into account the rules of musical theory
- Infrastructure - read, write to file, import, export, API, commands.

## Required experience

- Significant professional experience as software developer, including modern C++ in a large, long-lived, performance-sensitive desktop codebase.
- Experience owning solutions end to end, from design through delivery and maintenance, not just implementing tickets.
- Committed to code quality, with good judgment for making solid architectural decisions.
- Experience with OOP and domain model design.
- Able to read and understand fairly complex sheet music, with a good understanding of music theory.
- Solid communication and collaboration, comfortable working async across a distributed, global team.
- AI coding-savvy, applying critical thinking to discern when it is the right tool for the job
- Attention to detail: in engraving, small inconsistencies are immediately visible to the musicians who rely on the output.
- An eye for visual design: you know what a beautiful score looks like and care about making that happen.

_Desirable_

- Hands-on experience with MuseScore Studio or a competing notation/composition tool, as a user, arranger, or composer.
- Experience with MIDI and synthesizers
- Experience with asynchronous and multi-threaded code 
- Experience working with fonts, with freetype 
- Experience in rendering and OpenGL

_Bonus Points_

- Experience working on engraving for a music composition software or publisher

## Muse Group empowers music makers

We create the worldʼs most popular apps for playing, recording and composing music. Through our innovative learning tools, expansive music catalogs and free open-source software, we make it easier for millions — from beginners to experienced musicians — to be creative every day. Our talented team of music lovers collaborates all over the globe, from Limassol to Seoul and Boston to Berlin.

We’re an ambitious company with the drive and culture of a startup — with many more exciting Muse Group developments to come. Hal Leonard, which joined Muse Group in 2023, is the world leader in sheet music publishing and music education. The company has a storied history of providing music learners with the very best methods and arrangements of popular music for over 70 years. Hal Leonard is also a major distributor of popular brands of instruments, gear, and software to the music trade worldwide.

WHAT YOU'LL DO


SET DIRECTION AND OWN THE OUTCOME

 - Identify where agentic development can make the greatest difference, using developer feedback, existing experiments and engineering performance data.

 - Set the strategy and priorities across agent execution, repository readiness, CI, security and developer workflows.

BUILD THE FOUNDATIONS

 - Design and build isolated execution environments where agents can work with the right access to code, tools and context, without exposing secrets or sensitive systems.

INTEGRATE AGENTS INTO HOW WE WORK

 - Integrate agentic workflows with GitHub, CI, test infrastructure and code review, so the agentic path becomes the easiest path for engineers.

We’re approaching our tenth birthday and have gone from being a little-known tech start-up to creating our very own community at the heart of the tech and digital epicentre of the UK – Greater Manchester. We also have teams based in London and Malvern/Cheltenham, this role can be based in either of those locations.

Our name Naimuri is Japanese and simply means…

‘nai’ meaning ‘not’
‘muri’ meaning ‘overburden’

These principles apply to every aspect of an organisation from technology, process and infrastructure, through to people, culture and leadership. This means that we empower our teams to do what they think is the right thing, giving them the skills and confidence to explore new ways of working, and to create a bias-free environment, where all our people feel comfortable collaborating to deliver the finest ideas and solutions in an agile environment. 

Our business is focused on 4 cornerstones, which shape and underpin the way in which we go about work and treat each other. These are: Wellbeing, Empowerment, Perpetual Edge and Delivery.

People and culture are at the heart of Naimuri, so that collectively, we can realise our mission of ‘making the UK a safer place to be’.

About the role and team:

Our analysis community comprises of business analysts, change managers, user researchers and user experience designers. You will, therefore, be joining an exciting and growing community which sees individuals closely integrated into technical teams.

You will spend most of your time integrated into one of our software development or data science teams, acting as the link between the technical teams and the customer, collecting and managing requirements, supporting delivery, leading on acceptance testing and keeping a close eye on the end-to-end benefits management process. You will be supporting acceptance testing processes to ensure that intended changes have been correctly implemented and that anticipated benefits have been realised.

This role can be based from London or Malvern.

About you:

You will be passionate about technology and keeping the UK safe. You may have a degree that may be in a related field. You might not, but might instead demonstrate how you have trodden the path for yourself and gained the skills and experience required to be successful in this role.

We would expect you to have experience in the core skills. However, items listed in the general skills are nice to have. They are things that are likely to be used in the role and it is advised that you should have opinions on several of them.

Core skills:

• Eliciting and analysing requirements — both functional and non-functional.

• Ensuring that customer requirements and priorities are accurately documented.

• Organising and prioritising requirements using techniques such as — but not limited to — product roadmaps, epics, user stories and backlogs.

• Generating and defining options.

• Engaging with relevant stakeholders and specialists.

• Evaluating options for financial, technical and business feasibility.

• Developing a business change implementation plan to identify required changes to processes, procedures, systems, structures and ways of working. 

• Using a structured process and set of tools for leading people through change. 

• Implementing organisational business change management practices to support iterative/agile working. 

• Engaging with, and tailoring communication to, stakeholders and everyone impacted by the change. 

• Monitoring the impact of the business change management plan and sustaining and embedding change. 

• Identifying, classifying and prioritising risks — their impact and probability, and mitigation actions.

• Ensuring the customer is ready to operate the new service when it has been deployed.

General skills:

• Ensuring options align with the organisation’s vision, mission, objectives, strategy and tactics.

• Planning, developing and implementing organisational approaches to risk management.

• Planning, designing, managing and reporting on the outcomes of acceptance tests.

• Implementing service acceptance practices to support iterative/agile working.

• Implementing a benefits management framework and approach.

• Identifying and implementing the actions needed to optimise the business impact of individual and combined benefits.

• Confirming the achievement of expected benefits.

Above all else, we look for people with the right attitude and tenacity to continually improve themselves. You’ll have the freedom and autonomy to do your best work, with plenty of support along the way.

Pay and benefits:

Naimuri pays competitively within the industry based on your role's base location rates. The salary for this position is dependent upon your experience. We assess seniority relative to the team at Naimuri during the interviewing process.

A full time working week is 37.5 hours and you have flexibility over when you give that time. We also offer part-time working which can be discussed during the recruitment process. 

Our core hours are 10:00am - 3:00pm and our office hours are between 7:30 and 18:00 Monday to Friday. Most teams have agreed ‘in office’ days to enable collaboration. You may also be required to attend a local customer site regularly or on occasion to travel to other customer sites in the UK or the Naimuri office in Greater Manchester. 

Benefits include:

• Flexible/Hybrid working options

• A performance bonus

• Company bonus

• Pension matched 1.5x up to 10.5%

• AXA group 1 medical cover

• Personal training budget

• Holiday buy-back scheme

• Cycle to work scheme

• Car benefit scheme

Join us as a Customer Due Diligence Analyst, Onboarding at Mettle

- If you have a curious mind and like to work in a fast paced, innovative environment, this is a fantastic opportunity to join us as a Customer Due Diligence Analyst.
- You’ll work diligently and efficiently to protect our customers and the organisation from economic crime
- This is an opportunity to join a supportive team where we’ll also take a real investment in your career development

**What you'll do**

In this role within the Customer Due Diligence function, you will primarily focus on the Mettle proposition, supporting Boxed banking-as-a-service processes as needed. As a key part of our first line of defence against economic crime, you will ensure regulatory obligations are met, conduct efficient account reviews, and risk assess customers using various sources to confirm they meet our risk appetite.

You’ll be responsible for:

- Conducting robust reviews of new Mettle account applications, ensuring our customers align with NatWest Boxed's risk appetite. You'll make fair and proportionate decline decisions where required
- Identifying and mitigating economic crime risks, escalating effectively when needed to protect both our customers and Mettle
- Operating diligently within NatWest Group policies and NatWest Boxed established processes, ensuring compliance and consistency
- Constantly seeking opportunities to enhance our processes for greater effectiveness and efficiency, helping us scale and improve
- Reviewing Know Your Customer (KYC) / Know Your Business (KYB) check reports and application data to prevent application fraud and truly understand the nature and purpose of the account
- Reviewing name screening hits for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), Sanctions, and Adverse Press. This involves escalating true matches or making well-rationalised discounting decisions
- Investigating application fraud and other economic crime-related alerts from internal and external databases, like the Untoward Incident Database (UID) and Cifas
- Contacting customers, managing your chats within our Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and communicating clearly and concisely, always embodying Mettle's supportive tone of voice

**The skills you'll need**

Seeking a curious and innovative individual with CDD or Financial Crime knowledge. Recognised qualifications are helpful but not necessary - we can help you achieve these once you join. Strong communication skills and a focus on positive customer outcomes are essential.

You’ll also need:

- Previous experience in customer due diligence, economic crime prevention, or similar fields (e.g. AML, PEPs/Sanctions, KYC/KYB).
- A curious and analytical mind, adept at applying a risk-based approach to efficiently manage high volumes of work.
- Proven ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, handling multiple priorities with precision and calm.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with a strong command of English.
- Sharp critical thinking, sound decision-making, and exceptional time management.
- Meticulous attention to detail and a proactive, self-starting approach to your work and record-keeping.

- You’ll be educating customers in the different ways to Bank and supporting them in choosing the options that work best for them

## What you'll do

You’ll handle inbound calls from Premier Customers regarding a wide range of queries delivering an exceptional service to everyone you speak to. Whether it’s making payments, dealing with banking queries, providing product information or booking customers in to discuss their finances with a relationship manager, you’ll be there to help.

**Your duties will include**

- Taking full ownership of your calls, solving customers’ queries and providing an outstanding memorable customer experience
- Maintaining relationships with colleagues in your department to support customers and maintain an awareness of the wider aims of the business
- Identifying complaints and errors quickly and making sure that the relationship with the customer is fully restored
- Improving processes and procedures to maximise customer satisfaction and efficiency

You'll have experience working in a customer-focused environment, with a passion for delivering excellent service and building positive relationships with customers. - Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written with the ability to build rapport and adapt your approach to different customers
- Confidence working in a fast-paced contact centre environment, managing a high volume of customer interactions while maintaining attention to detail
- A genuine commitment to putting customers first, going the extra mile to provide a personalised and effortless experience
- A positive attitude towards developing new skills, embracing feedback, and developing your knowledge
- Good technology skills with the ability to multitask whilst talking to customers
- Resilience empathy, and the ability to remain calm and professional when handling a range of customer enquiries

Join us as a Senior Operational Readiness Associate (Financial Crime)

- This is a high-impact opportunity to join NatWest Boxed as a Financial Crime operational subject matter expert, shaping the future of NatWest’s Banking-as-a-Service (BaaS) business.  
- You’ll be part of an innovative, high-performing, and inclusive culture where fresh ideas, collaboration, and personal development are championed at every level.
- Advance your career in a fast-paced, cutting-edge FinTech environment backed by NatWest’s reach and strong balance sheet.  
- Take ownership of embedding robust, compliant financial crime processes and controls to ensure new product and client launches are operationally ready to scale. 
- This role is available for a period of 9 months

What you'll do

As a Senior Operational Readiness Associate, you will serve as the lead Financial Crime operational expert within NatWest Boxed. You will drive operational readiness across all propositions by embedding compliant, robust financial crime processes and controls across our entire product and service portfolio. Your core mission is to make sure that every change across the Boxed product suite is operationally viable, seamless, and optimal for our Anti-Financial Crime operations teams to run.

You’ll also:

- Act as the lead operational SME, architecting compliant, best-in-class operational workflows to power new product and client launches.

- Partner with Product Managers, Product Owners, and Domain Leads to define forward-looking roadmaps that automate operations while advising on capacity and operational feasibility.

- Collaborate directly with frontline Anti-Financial Crime teams to identify pain points, remove friction, and build streamlined, scalable processes.

- Evaluate proposed product solutions for operational viability, identifying risks, dependencies, and required operational capabilities.

- Translate high-level product propositions into crisp, structured financial crime requirements, impact assessments, and clear acceptance criteria aligned with regulatory standards.

- Embed directly within delivery squads alongside Project Managers to ensure all controls, systems, and operational workflows are rigorously tested, compliant, and launch-ready.

The skills you'll need

You’ll bring deep, end-to-end expertise in Financial Crime operational processes and controls, alongside a proven track record of identifying operational risks and executing proactive mitigation strategies. You are a natural bridge between product vision and operational execution, skilled at translating complex concepts into structured operational requirements.

You’ll also need:

- Strong negotiation and interpersonal skills to align priorities and explain complex operational challenges to Project Managers.

- Ability to analyse large amounts of financial crime data to balance customer experience, commercial viability, and operational limits while anticipating downstream impacts.

- Skilled at defining clear operational requirements within established delivery frameworks.

- Proactive and results-driven approach to collaborating in cross-functional squads.

- Knowledge of the regulatory framework and financial crime industry trends and experience in Operational Readiness, Product Operations, process optimization, or transformation, plus knowledge of Savings, Personal Loans, and Current Accounts.

Navan Concierge is a pillar of Navan Signature, a business unit within Navan focused on solving the complex, personal and high-touch needs of our clients. In addition to Concierge, Navan Signature spans Premier (premium corporate travel for professional-services firms), Events (bringing people together through on-platform booking and offline event management), and Specialty (bespoke offerings for niche sectors).

Today, Navan Concierge is an elite team servicing the personal and professional travel requirements of UHNW individuals, their families and family offices. We’re looking for an exceptional leader to expand the current white-glove service across Navan’s client base, doubling the business in year one and contributing to enterprise retention by becoming indispensable to our most influential travelers.

Over the next three years as SVP, Navan Concierge, you will build and execute a strategy to transform Navan Concierge into the leading lifestyle concierge marketplace. Operating as a start up within a leading travel technology company, you will partner with the sharpest minds in travel technology and service to deliver the commercial strategy, partnerships and product for true competitive advantage.

This role will suit a high energy builder: an execution-focused leader who gets things done at pace, influences across functions, adapts quickly, is P&L fluent and holds themselves to exceptional standards.

Key Responsibilities

P&L & Strategy Execution

- Own Navan Concierge’s full P&L, keeping the business profitable and maintaining current margins while it scales in year one.
- Set and execute the multi-year business strategy, commercial proposition, operating model and go-to-market plan; develop an investment plan covering the people, product, technology, supplier and service capabilities required to deliver it.
- Establish clear measures for GBV, revenue, profitability, margin, attachment, service quality and client outcomes. Assess Concierge’s contribution to enterprise stickiness by tracking renewal and churn trends among enterprise customers using the service.

Core Business Strategy: Growth Through Navan Signature

- Grow Concierge through attachment across Navan’s existing client base, identifying UHNW individuals, executives, founders, board members, their families and family offices whose personal, household or family-office travel needs fit the proposition.
- Position Concierge as a distinct Navan Signature proposition that strengthens enterprise relationships and retention, complements corporate travel, and brings a more joined-up service experience to clients and their families.

Commercial & Business Model Design

- Define the commercial model, including membership structures, invite-only access, minimum spend thresholds, service fees and the unit economics required to sustain an attractive margin.
- Assess the case for extending Concierge through independent-contractor advisors, including the investment, commercial, service, compliance and go-to-market models required to scale.

Product, Content & Marketplace Innovation

- Partner with Product and Engineering leaders to shape the capabilities needed while aligning investment with Concierge’s service model, client needs and business case.
- Develop supplier and partner strategies that deliver differentiated access, service recovery and value across luxury hotels, private aviation, villas, ground transport, destination services and other relevant categories.
- Set the service principles, quality measures, escalation paths and operating standards that combine effective technology with exceptional human support, discretion and responsiveness.
- Success is a platform-enabled model that attracts the world’s best independent travel consultants, giving them the competitive edge to surpass expectations of the world’s most demanding travelers.

Talent Acquisition & Team Leadership

- Build the team and leadership capacity to double the currently small scale Concierge business in year one, recruiting and developing the concierge professionals needed to grow while preserving service quality and current margins.
- Where the independent-advisor opportunity is validated, define a compelling value proposition and talent model that complements the core Concierge team and business.
- Lead alignment with Navan Signature and executive peers across Sales, Account Management, Product, Operations, Supplier Relations, Technology, Finance and Legal, securing support for the agreed investment plan and growth priorities.

Candidate Qualifications

- Business leadership: Proven experience building, running and scaling a business or business line, with clear accountability for a P&L and evidence of delivering profitable growth.
- Financial leadership: Demonstrated ability to manage revenue, cost, margin and investment trade-offs; grow a profitable business while protecting service quality and making sound longer-term investment decisions.
- Industry Networks: Deep relationships with top travel advisors, luxury hotel groups, private aviation providers, and destination management companies (DMCs).
- Strategy and investment: Proven ability to set a multi-year strategy, build an evidence-based investment plan, size growth opportunities and make disciplined build, partner and scale decisions.
- Executive leadership: Track record of influencing senior cross-functional peers and leading teams through growth, including Product and Engineering partnerships to deliver differentiated client experiences.
- Location Flexibility: Based in or willing to work out of London, New York City, or San Francisco.

You'll operate across the entire attack lifecycle—from initial access and evasion of EDR, through lateral movement and objective completion—while ensuring the safety, confidentiality, and operational integrity of every engagement. 

You’ll also contribute to our capability development, tooling, and methodologies, while mentoring the next generation of Red Teamers and representing NCC Group in client-facing engagements, including with C-level stakeholders.

• Design, plan, and execute advanced adversary simulation and Red Team engagements aligned with industry standards and regulatory frameworks (e.g., CBEST, TIBER, CORIE, AASE, iCAST, FEER). 
• Maintain a strong focus on operational security and risk mitigation throughout delivery. 
• Communicate risks and safety concerns to clients clearly and proactively before and during operations. 
• Use both off-the-shelf and custom-built tools to achieve objectives and evade detection. 
• Create and maintain custom scripts or tools to automate Red Team activities or exploit environment-specific weaknesses. 
Reporting and Communication 
• Produce high-quality, narrative-driven reports that convey technical detail, context, and actionable insight to both technical and non-technical audiences. 
• Deliver detailed debriefs and presentations to security teams and C-level stakeholders. 
• Translate complex attack chains into engaging, informative documentation. 
• Collaboration and Stakeholder Management 
• Work autonomously on smaller engagements and collaboratively on large-scale, multi-phase assessments. 
• Build strong, lasting relationships with clients and internal teams. 
• Support sales and scoping activity where required, contributing to technical pre-sales conversations. 
Capability Development 
• Share knowledge and develop internal Red Team capabilities through collaboration, tooling contributions, and process improvements. 
• Keep abreast of emerging TTPs, threat actors, and detection technologies, evaluating and integrating relevant techniques. 
Mentorship and Thought Leadership 
• Act as a mentor and knowledge resource for junior consultants and cross-functional teams. 
• Promote a culture of learning, safety, and excellence within the Red Team practice.

Essential: 
• Demonstrable experience delivering high-complexity Red Team engagements end-to-end. 
• Deep understanding of the adversary lifecycle and common tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs). 
• Familiarity with evasion techniques and bypassing controls such as EDR/EPP, email/web gateways, proxies, etc. 
• Experience in stakeholder engagement, with the ability to brief both security professionals and executive stakeholders. 
• Excellent written English and ability to create structured, compelling reporting documents.
Proficiency across multiple relevant technical domains: 
• Microsoft Active Directory 
• Office 365 security mechanisms 
• Cloud security (AWS, Azure, GCP) 
• MacOS and mixed environments

• Experience working under regulatory testing frameworks such as: 
• CBEST, TIBER-EU, CORIE, AASE, iCAST, or FEER 
• Experience in the design or development of Red Team tooling or automation. 
• Familiarity with UK and international cybersecurity frameworks, regulations, and best practices.

Aura is Neo4j’s fully managed graph database as a service. Customers create, scale, and use Neo4j databases in the cloud without installing, clustering, or operating the database themselves. Aura runs on Kubernetes across Google Cloud, AWS, and Azure, and handles provisioning, networking, security, upgrades, and day-to-day operations for those databases.

Composite is the technology behind distributed query execution in Neo4j: one query can span multiple databases. Infinigraph is our database sharding offering for large data volumes, built on a distributed database architecture. Distributed query execution is a complex and interesting topic covering query language design, performant networking, and concurrency. Those capabilities still have to run as a cloud product, and that's where a large part of this role sits: building the Go services and Kubernetes machinery that provision, scale, and operate sharded and composite clusters on Aura, reliably, at the data volumes our customers keep growing into.

As part of an energetic and fun team of engineers, you'll work at the frontier of designing and implementing new capabilities for Neo4j on Aura.

• Building and evolving the Aura control plane for sharded and composite databases in Go, so shards, composite instances, clusters, and their lifecycles are managed declaratively through Kubernetes instead of by hand. • Alongside coding features, we track down easy and tough bugs, fix downstream test failures, document features, join cross-team design meetings, and study the latest database research.
