About the Role
We’re hiring a Senior Engineer to help take our AI-powered risk engineering platform to the next level. Risk engineers are the backbone of multi-million-pound underwriting decisions, but they’re drowning in manual processes. Our agentic platform cuts days of work down to minutes, and we’re live in production with some of the world’s largest insurance organisations.
This isn’t a “build features in isolation” role. You’ll ship AI-powered product end to end, own enterprise client relationships during deployments and PoCs, and shape the technical foundation of the company. Your day might go from pairing on an agentic workflow in the morning to walking a client’s infosec team through a security review after lunch. You’ll work directly with our CTO, our founding engineers, and our CEO, side by side in our Shoreditch office.
What You’ll Accomplish
Ship AI features that work in production. Agentic workflows, LLM integrations, evaluation – you’ll build and ship AI-powered product from prototype to production, and you’re already fluent with AI coding tools as a core part of how you work.
Own the client-facing side of engineering. You’ll represent the engineering team in enterprise settings: leading PoCs, navigating security reviews with IT and infosec teams, and building trust with the people who buy and use what you build.
Shape the technical foundation. Strong Python backend work (Django/Flask), solid database design, Docker and production infrastructure – you’ll make the decisions that the platform is built on for years.
Close the loop between customers and product. You’ll turn field observations and customer pain points into shipped improvements, sitting at the boundary of engineering and delivery.
Use AI to scale yourself. We run lean and use AI tools daily to operate at a level that shouldn’t be possible for a team our size.
What We’re Looking For
Must-haves:
• 3+ years building production Python web applications (Django, Flask, or FastAPI) at product-driven companies
• Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered features or agentic workflows in production – you’ll be productive on our AI stack from day one
• Comfortable across the full stack: you’ve built and maintained both backend APIs and React/Next.js frontends
• Experience representing engineering in client-facing settings: PoCs, onboarding, security reviews, or working directly with enterprise IT and infosec teams
• Strong database design and optimisation skills (PostgreSQL, Redis) and comfort with Docker, CI/CD, and debugging production infrastructure
• Early-stage startup experience – you’ve built products from scratch in resource-constrained environments – balanced with exposure to how well-run engineering teams operate
• Based in the UK with valid work rights (sponsorship available for those already here on a visa)
Nice-to-haves:
• Experience in insurance, fintech, or other regulated industries where reliability and compliance standards are high
• Experience with multiple LLM providers and an understanding of the trade-offs between them
• Open source contributions, technical writing, or talks
How We Work
We’re a small team that operates with high trust and high ownership. We use AI tools daily to move faster than teams 5x our size. We’d rather ship something imperfect today than plan something perfect for next quarter. You’ll be in the office 4 days a week at our Shoreditch space, working side by side with the people building the company.
Benefits
• Employee options in a category-defining, VC-backed startup
• Top-tier office in Shoreditch with great coffee, brand new gym, and generous perks
• Weekly team lunches, learning budget, regular offsites, and full health and pension benefits
Interview Process
• Screening (30 min) – a technical conversation with one of our founding engineers about your background and experience
• Technical deep-dive (60 min) – a second conversation with another of our founding engineers on system design, technical judgment, and real-world problem-solving
• Take-home technical assessment (2–3 hours async + 30 min review) – a practical task on a realistic version of our platform, followed by a review of your decisions with our CTO
• Final round, in person (90 min) – at our Shoreditch office: a 60-minute system design challenge with our CTO based on a realistic client deployment scenario, followed by a 30-minute culture conversation

COMPANY

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.




ROLE

The AIT Systems Integration Engineer owns functional and system-level testing of our spacecraft and the verification tracking for each satellite campaign. Working within the Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) team, you will take the satellite from integrated subsystems to a flight-ready, fully verified vehicle.

You will bridge systems engineering, subsystem teams and the AIT Engineering Functions. You will turn requirements into test procedures, run and lead test campaigns, and make sure every requirement is closed out with traceable evidence before launch. 

The role suits someone who knows SmallSat development approaches, is hands-on with Hardware and Ground Support Equipment (GSE), and understands how satellite subsystems behave together.




RESPONSIBILITIES




FUNCTIONAL AND SYSTEM TESTING

 - Own the functional and system test programme for the spacecraft, from unit-level acceptance, integration, thought to whole System End-to-End Testing.

 - Write, review and run test specifications and procedures, including basic functional testing, FDIR, end-to-end tests and mission/day-in-the-life simulations.

 - Lead test readiness reviews and test review boards, and sign off test reports.

 - Run tests before, during and after environmental campaigns (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMC) to confirm spacecraft health.

 - Diagnose anomalies, raise and track Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), and drive root-cause investigations with subsystem engineers.

 - Develop and maintain automated test scripts and telemetry/telecommand (TM/TC) databases used for testing.


VERIFICATION TRACKING

 - Own the verification matrix (VCRM) for the satellite campaign, mapping each requirement to its method: test, analysis, inspection or review of design.

 - Plan the verification approach with Systems Engineering and keep it current through the campaign.

 - Collect and link verification evidence, and report close-out status against milestones.

 - Prepare verification data packages for key reviews (e.g. CDR, TRR, QR, PSR/FAR) and customer acceptance.


GSE AND TEST INFRASTRUCTURE

 - Specify, integrate and validate Electrical GSE, including power supplies, battery simulators, RF test sets, umbilicals and break-out boxes.

 - Maintain the spacecraft checkout software and ground segment interfaces used on the AIT floor.

 - Make sure GSE is calibrated, configuration-controlled and safe for use with flight hardware.


INTEGRATION AND CAMPAIGN SUPPORT

 - Support subsystem and payload integration, including electrical interface checks, harness verification and safe-to-mate procedures.

 - Plan and schedule system test activities within the wider AIT campaign.

 - Support launch campaign activities, including transport, launch site checkout and launch vehicle interface testing.

 - Work to cleanroom, ESD and flight hardware handling standards, and contribute to lessons learned for future missions.




REQUIREMENTS 

 - Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrical or Systems Engineering, Physics, or equivalent experience.

 - Typically 3+ years in spacecraft AIT, systems integration or test engineering.

 - Hands-on experience with functional and system-level testing of satellites or space subsystems.

 - Familiarity with SmallSat development approaches: agile, rapid iteration, protoflight models, and pragmatic use of COTS components.

 - Working knowledge of satellite subsystems: EPS, OBC/C&DH, ADCS, communications (TT&C and payload RF), propulsion, thermal, structures and payloads.

 - Experience using and setting up GSE, including EGSE, checkout systems and RF test equipment.

 - Experience with requirements verification and maintaining a verification matrix through to close-out.

 - Comfortable with lab equipment: oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, spectrum analysers, logic analysers.

 - Familiarity with common spacecraft interfaces and protocols (e.g. CAN, I2C, SPI, RS-422, SpaceWire, CCSDS).

 - Clear technical writing for procedures, test reports and NCRs.




DESIRABLES

 - End-to-end involvement in at least one satellite mission that reached launch.

 - Test automation and scripting in Python or similar, and experience with spacecraft control or checkout software (e.g. OpenC3/COSMOS, Yamcs, SCOS-2000).

 - Experience planning or supporting environmental test campaigns (vibration, TVAC, EMC).

 - Knowledge of ECSS standards (e.g. ECSS-E-ST-10-02 Verification, ECSS-E-ST-10-03 Testing) or NASA equivalents.

 - Requirements management tools (e.g. DOORS, Jama, Polarion, Valispace).

 - Launch campaign experience at a launch site.

 - Cleanroom and ESD-certified flight hardware handling.

 - Eligibility for UK security clearance, or the ability to obtain it, if required by the programme.




PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES

 - Takes ownership: drives tests and verification to close-out without waiting to be asked.

 - Methodical and detail-focused, with a strong sense of safety and quality around flight hardware.

 - Calm, structured problem-solver when anomalies appear under schedule pressure.

 - Communicates clearly across disciplines, from subsystem engineers to programme managers and customers.

 - Comfortable in a fast-paced SmallSat environment, balancing rigour with pace.

 - Willing to work flexibly during test and launch campaigns, including occasional travel.
   
   


WHY NEWORBIT SPACE?

 - Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

 - Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

 - Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

## **Job Summary**

This post, which commences in August 2027, is for haematology specialty trainees or haematology specialty (locally employed) doctors working in the UK at Specialist Training Level 5 (ST5) or above, who want to pursue a career in Transfusion Medicine. It is a one-year fixed term contract based with the Patient Blood Management team but including sessions across the transfusion directorate aimed at providing subspecialty experience in Transfusion Medicine. This is an established programme for Out of Programme Experience which has gained excellent feedback from previous fellows.

You will be part of a national team working to deliver blood and blood components to patients in hospitals in England.

You will be directly accountable to the Consultant Haematologist Educational Supervisor at NHSBT who will be the consultant working in the centre where you are based.

This is a national vacancy, the successful candidate may be based at any of the following main centres in the UK, final location to be agreed at interview -Leeds/Barnsley, Birmingham, Bristol, Cambridge, London or Oxford.

## **Main duties of the job**

There will be a combination of daytime “duty” work and longer term quality improvement and project work. Duty work will involve taking queries from within the organisation and NHS Trusts, giving clinical advice to inform decisions around individual patients and components. All clinical work will be supervised by a named consultant.

You will be expected to submit at least one project as a conference abstract and/or to a peer reviewed journal. As part of the role, you will deliver teaching to doctors, nurses, biomedical and clinical scientists.

You will acquire subspecialty skills and experience in: Components, Donor Medicine, Red Cell Immunohaematology, Patient Blood Management (PBM).

You will acquire further knowledge of: Histocompatibility and Immunogenetics, Manufacturing and Logistics, Cell, Apheresis and Gene Therapies, Haemovigilance, Research, Audit and Quality Improvement.

You will be supported in pursuing an honorary contract with the Trust to enable you acquire skills in hospital-based transfusion practice (participation in hospital transfusion team meetings etc.)

## **About You**

**Experience and Knowledge**

- Currently working (or have previously worked) at Specialist Training Level 5 (ST5) or equivalent in Clinical Haematology
- Demonstrates the acquisition of the level of knowledge and skills appropriate to the level of training
- Demonstrates an understanding of, and commitment to, a career in transfusion medicine
- Experience of the NHS Patient Blood Management model and transfusion regulations
- Potential to become a leader in chosen field.

**Qualifications and Training**

- GMC registration with a license to practice
- Evidence of good progress in further clinical training
- Evidence of commitment to transfusion medicine as a specialty
- Completed Essential Transfusion Medicine Course (ETM)
- Completed FRCPath parts 1 and 2 (clinical haematology) examinations. Candidates who have completed Part 1 but not Part 2 will be considered. Candidates should not plan to sit FRCPath Part 2 during the fellowship.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Data Center Operations Implementation Manager to own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition of Nscale's data centres — spanning construction, fit-out, and live, steady-state local operations — across an assigned region and set of sites. Rather than owning construction execution itself, you'll be the connective tissue between Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, and local Operations teams — driving a structured, well-documented transition so every site goes live on schedule and ready to support production workloads. This is an individual-contributor role built on strong stakeholder management, cross-functional influence, and travel to sites during critical transition windows.

What You'll Do

Day 0 to Day 2 Transition Leadership

• Own the end-to-end Day 0 to Day 2 transition process for each data centre site within your assigned region — spanning construction, fit-out, and steady-state operations.

• Define and maintain a standardized transition framework and readiness checklist applied consistently across your assigned sites.

• Track and drive closure of cross-team action items, dependencies, and blockers standing between construction handover and operational go-live.

• Identify and escalate risks to go-live timelines, and drive resolution across the relevant stakeholder groups.

Stakeholder & Cross-Functional Coordination

• Track progress and status across Construction, Network Engineering, Compute/Infrastructure Deployment, Facility Engineering, SDM, and local site Operations teams throughout the transition window.

• Partner with Construction teams to track handover status, outstanding items, and site readiness milestones.

• Track Network Engineering's buildout, testing, and cutover activities required for a site to go live.

• Track hardware intake, rack-and-stack, and deployment scheduling with Compute/Infrastructure Deployment teams to stay aligned with the transition timeline.

• Coordinate with Facility Engineering on site systems and infrastructure readiness ahead of transition.

• Engage with the Service Delivery Management (SDM) team to ensure alignment with customer needs, SLAs, security, and facility performance.

• Take part in regular cross-functional syncs and stakeholder reviews to stay current on transition status.

• Contribute to a shared sense of ownership and accountability across stakeholder teams, even without formal authority over them.

Local Day Two Operations Readiness

• Partner with local Operations leads to confirm staffing, training, tooling, and support processes are in place before a site transitions to Day 2 ownership.

• Create and validate standard operating procedures (SOPs) and operational processes required for local Operations teams to run the site post-handover.

• Create the operational site tool bill of materials (BOM) required for local Operations teams to maintain the site post-handover.

• Verify the spare parts bill of materials (BOM) is complete and in place ahead of Day 2 handover.

• Facilitate structured knowledge transfer and handover documentation from Construction, Network, and Compute teams to local Operations teams.

• Confirm monitoring, ticketing, and ITSM processes are validated and operating before a site is handed to local Operations.

• Act as an escalation point for local Operations teams during the early post-handover period to smooth the transition.

Reliability, Safety & Compliance

• Define and enforce Day 2 readiness criteria that a site must meet before transitioning to local Operations ownership.

• Facilitate root-cause analysis for transition delays or gaps surfaced during handover, and drive remediation across teams.

• Ensure health, safety, and environmental requirements are validated and documented as part of readiness sign-off.

• Support certification and audit readiness (ISO 27001, ISO 22237, SOC 2, Cyber Essentials Plus, ISO 22301) ahead of go-live.

Vendor & Supplier Coordination

• Coordinate with construction contractors and colocation providers as needed to close out remaining items affecting the transition timeline.

• Track vendor commitments and SLAs relevant to the transition window, and escalate delays that put go-live at risk.

• Coordinate with the Supply Chain team to align hardware intake and staging with the transition schedule.

Monitoring, Reporting & Analytics

• Track KPIs and KRIs for the Day 0 to Day 2 transition process (time to transition, readiness checklist completion rate, post-handover incident rate, etc.).

• Build and maintain dashboards that track transition status across your assigned site pipeline for all stakeholder teams.

• Produce regular reports for senior leadership on transition status, risks, and blockers.

• Use data-driven insights to identify systemic bottlenecks in the Day 0 to Day 2 process and drive continuous improvement.

Experience & Background

• 3-8 years of experience in data centre operations, program/project management, or infrastructure deployment at scale.

• Proven track record coordinating the transition of new sites into live operations across construction, network, compute, and operations functions.

• Experience operating in a matrixed environment, influencing outcomes without direct authority over every stakeholder team.

• Demonstrated success managing multiple concurrent site transitions in a high-growth, fast-paced environment.

• Background in hyperscale, cloud, or HPC data centre environments (preferred).

Technical Knowledge & Expertise

• Working knowledge of data centre power, cooling, networking, and compute infrastructure, sufficient to coordinate effectively across specialist teams.

• Familiarity with network deployment and cutover processes, and compute/hardware deployment lifecycles.

• Knowledge of Layer 1 network infrastructure, including fiber, copper, optics, and transceivers.

• Familiarity with ITSM tooling, ticketing systems, and monitoring platforms used by local Operations teams.

Influence & Communication

• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence and align Construction, Network, Compute, and Operations teams without direct authority.

• Excellent cross-functional communication skills, able to translate technical detail between teams with different priorities and vocabularies.

• Program management discipline, with the ability to track and drive multiple concurrent workstreams to closure.

• Comfortable operating in ambiguous, matrixed, fast-moving environments.

• Bias toward ownership, pragmatism, and delivering results with urgency.

Operational Excellence

• Rigorous tracking of readiness checklists, risk logs, and action items across many concurrent site transitions within your assigned region.

• Proven ability to build and refine standardized transition frameworks that scale with business growth.

• Strong attention to detail in transition documentation and handover packages.

• Willingness to travel to sites during critical transition windows.

Nice to Have

• Familiarity with network cutover or compute/hardware deployment processes specifically.

• Experience with ITSM platforms and ticketing workflows.

OpenRent is profitable, growing rapidly, and backed by CVC Capital Partners, so we have a very strong financial foundation.

# Application Scientist (Maternity Cover)

**Location: UK**

Fully remote, 12-month fixed-term contract, starting as soon as possible

[Apply Now](mailto:vacancies@optibrium.com)

## Background

Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Cambridge, UK, Optibrium™ develops software and novel technologies to improve the efficiency and productivity of drug discovery. Our solutions support industry-leading research for a global customer base, including top-ten pharma and innovative biotech companies. Our products include:

- [StarDrop](https://optibrium.com/products/stardrop/)™ – Integrated software for small-molecule design, optimisation, and data analysis;
- [Cerella](https://optibrium.com/products/cerella/)™ – A platform that fills gaps in drug discovery data to identify the most promising compounds and experiments; and
- [BioPharmics](https://optibrium.com/products/biopharmics/)™ – A 3D molecular design platform for everything from small molecules to large macrocycles.

We’re looking for an experienced drug discovery scientist to join our Application Science team as maternity cover. You’ll be the trusted scientific partner for a portfolio of our customers: the person they turn to when they want to get more out of our software and apply it to their projects. You’ll help chemists and project teams solve real discovery problems, lead demonstrations and training, and make sure every customer has an excellent experience working with Optibrium.

If you’ve spent your career designing and making compounds and want to use that experience to help many discovery teams at once, outside the lab, we’d love to hear from you. You don’t need to have used StarDrop™ before; we’ll give you a structured onboarding and you’ll work alongside experienced Application Scientists from day one.

## Main Priorities of the Role

- Be the single point of contact for your customers, building strong, long-term relationships with medicinal chemists, computational scientists and project leaders
- Help customers get real value from our software by understanding their science and showing them how to apply StarDrop, Cerella™ and BioPharmics™ to their projects
- Run engaging software demonstrations, training sessions and workshops for prospective and existing customers, mostly online and occasionally in person
- Partner with Account Management and New Business teams on evaluations and renewals, bringing the scientific expertise that shows customers what our software can do for them
- Answer customers’ scientific and technical questions, from interpreting results to installation and licensing, drawing on our developers and science team where needed
- Spot opportunities to increase adoption, and share customer feedback with our product and science teams to help shape future development
- Keep accurate records of customer interactions, licences and support cases

## Experience

The ideal candidate will have:

- Hands-on drug discovery experience in pharma, biotech or a CRO, for example as a medicinal, synthetic or computational chemist
- A PhD or degree in chemistry or a closely related science
- A real interest in how software, data and AI can help scientists make better decisions
- Confidence presenting to and teaching scientific audiences, from bench chemists to senior leaders
- A customer-focused mindset: you enjoy helping others succeed and take ownership of getting things resolved
- Clear, friendly written and spoken communication, with the ability to explain complex ideas simply
- Good organisation, with the ability to manage several customers and priorities at once
- Comfort working with software and troubleshooting issues on Windows, macOS and Linux (we’ll train you on the specifics)
- Desirable: experience using StarDrop or other molecular design and data analysis software, a customer-facing or application science role, or some scripting experience (e.g. Python)

## Our Culture

We’re an established, financially secure business with an entrepreneurial culture, where ideas are welcome from everyone. We value curiosity, collaboration and clear communication. In this role you’ll get to know our AI-driven software in depth and work directly with scientists at leading pharma, biotech and academic organisations around the world, seeing a far wider range of discovery projects than you would within a single organisation.

## What We Offer

A competitive salary, pension contribution, private medical and dental cover, and life assurance, with fully remote working and flexible hours. You’ll also receive full training on our software and the science behind it.

If you’re interested in joining a growing, entrepreneurial team working in an exciting field, please apply with a CV and covering letter to vacancies@optibrium.com (unsolicited applications from agencies will not be accepted).

job_title: Sr. Backend Software Engineer (Infrastructure ML Ops)
job_description:
At Philo, we’re a group of technology and product people who set out to build the future of television, marrying the best in modern technology with the most compelling medium ever invented — in short, we’re building the TV experience that we’ve always wanted for ourselves. In practice this means leveraging cloud delivery, modern tech stacks, machine learning, and hand-crafted native app experiences on all of our platforms. We aim to deliver a rock solid experience on the streaming basics, while cooking up next generation multi-screen and multi-user playback experiences.


SENIOR BACKEND SOFTWARE ENGINEER (INFRASTRUCTURE MLOPS)

The infrastructure team at Philo builds the foundation for a 24/7 live and on-demand streaming product serving video to our growing subscriber base. It provides a platform that enables groups across the company – such as video delivery, product, support, and analytics – to do their best work easily and smoothly. Our systems are highly distributed, horizontally scalable and run in the cloud on Kubernetes. We continuously test and deploy our code and closely monitor the health and performance of our production environment.

We are seeking an enthusiastic Infrastructure MLOps Software Engineer to help us build and improve the ML infrastructure at Philo. We are building out ML and LLM infrastructure and this role will be pivotal in setting direction, adopting best practices, and shipping infrastructure that will be used across the company.

As a sample, the ML infrastructure supports teams like Discovery in building content recommendation models that will help our users find more favorite shows from the large Philo catalog. The engineering team is designing and developing our own agent harnesses to support coding and empowering everyone at the company to get answers across our code bases, analytics, logs, and communication tools. The video player team is using LLMs to classify ads and label our video catalog so that users have a better experience. You’ll build the serving, evaluation and platform infrastructure that these workloads depend on.

Responsibilities:

 - Manage the core infrastructure at Philo with a focus on supporting ML and LLM workloads. This infrastructure is relied on by a large subscriber base of Philo’s product as well as internal stakeholders across the company.

 - Design, build, and maintain cloud infrastructure components (AWS and Kubernetes) using a combination of in-house technology and open source software.

 - Build and scale model serving and inference infrastructure for both real-time recommendation models and LLM workloads — including model servers (e.g. NVIDIA Triton), LLM inference engines (e.g. vLLM, TGI, TensorRT-LLM), autoscaling, and latency/throughput optimization. 

 - Manage GPU and accelerator infrastructure on Kubernetes — scheduling, capacity and quota management, and cost optimization across on-demand and spot capacity.

 - Design, build, and maintain monitoring and observability systems — spanning both system health and model quality (drift, evaluation, and online performance) — that enable Philo engineers and the support team to gain insight and to discover and debug issues.

 - Build and operate model evaluation infrastructure: offline and online eval pipelines, golden/regression datasets, LLM-as-judge harnesses, A/B testing and experimentation, and feedback/ground-truth loops

 - Design, build, and maintain CI/CD systems enabling Philo engineers to create pipelines to test and deploy their code.

 - Establish tools, methods and best practices for other Philo engineers interfacing with the Philo ML infrastructure. Ensure reliability, security, and scalability of the Philo platform. Promote Infrastructure as Code.

 - Work closely with other Philo engineers to deploy and instrument software systems.

 - Drive evaluation, selection, and integration of third-party vendor systems and work closely with vendors to configure and manage them.

Qualifications:

 - 8+ years of software development and infrastructure management experience.

 - 4+ years of experience developing and deploying ML systems at scale across training and inference

 - Experience working with distributed systems and an understanding of microservices architecture principles.

 - Experience with Linux and containerized (i.e. Docker) environments.

 - Experience managing cloud computing environments (AWS or GCP) and configuring cloud services e.g. CloudWatch, Route 53, RDS, ElastiCache, SQS, ALB/NLB/ELB, VPC networking, IAM security.

 - Experience with container orchestration platforms (i.e. Kubernetes), and familiarity with running GPU/accelerated workloads on them (e.g. NVIDIA device plugin, MIG, timeslicing).

 - Strong understanding of networking and internet application protocols including, but not limited to TCP/IP, DNS, and HTTP.

 - Strong understanding of network and application security principles and best practices.

 - Familiarity or hands-on experience with configuration management systems and Infrastructure as Code (e.g. Terraform, CloudFormation).

 - Familiarity or hands-on experience with Monitoring/Observability systems (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana, TICK/InfluxDB, Fluentd, ELK, Datadog).

 - Familiarity or hands-on experience with CI/CD automation systems e.g. Jenkins, Gitlab.

 - Experience with relational and non-relational databases and familiarity with modern data warehousing and querying.

 - Proficient in writing, testing, and profiling software in Golang, JavaScript/TypeScript, C++, Ruby, Python or similar programming languages.

 - Experience and aptitude for collaborating and communicating with internal and external stakeholders in both business and technical roles.

A strong candidate may also have one or more of these:

 - Hands-on experience optimizing inference — dynamic/continuous batching, quantization, KV-cache management, or GPU memory tuning — for low-latency or highthroughput serving. 

 - Experience with ML platform tooling: model registry and experiment tracking (e.g. MLflow, Weights & Biases), feature stores (e.g. Feast, Tecton), and pipeline/workflow orchestration (e.g. Airflow, Dagster, Kubeflow, Ray, Metaflow). 

 - Experience building model evaluation, monitoring, or experimentation systems — including drift detection, LLM-as-judge, or A/B testing for models. 

 - Experience with LLMOps: inference gateways/routers (e.g. LiteLLM), hosted model APIs (Bedrock, OpenAI, Anthropic), RAG pipelines, vector databases (e.g. pgvector, Pinecone, Weaviate), and prompt/version management. 

 - Experience building or operating agent harnesses or tool-using LLM applications in production. 

 - Experience with data and model versioning (e.g. DVC, LakeFS) and data/labeling pipelines. 

 - Experience with cost management / FinOps for GPU and inference workloads

We are language agnostic, but most of our backend code is written in Golang, Ruby and TypeScript, with some C++ and Python. Our services run on Kubernetes, and we practice continuous deployment across all of our systems.

More about Philo

At Philo, we’re a company that puts people first—both our subscribers and our team. We empower our colleagues to do their best work while supporting one another in pursuing shared goals. We value pragmatism, pride in our work, and passion, with transparency and openness as fundamental parts of our culture.

We’re committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility as we grow the Philo team and shape the future of TV. We believe that a diverse range of voices and perspectives enables us to innovate faster and create the best experiences for our subscribers. Philo is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re committed to supporting every candidate and employee. If you need an accommodation at any stage of the process, please email recruiting@philo.com and we’ll work with you to meet your needs.

Philo offers 70+ top-rated networks, including AMC, BET, CMT, Comedy Central, Discovery Channel, Food Network, Hallmark Channel, HGTV, HISTORY, Investigation Discovery, Lifetime, MTV, Nickelodeon, OWN, VH1, We TV, and more. It also includes all the groundbreaking originals and blockbuster movies available with AMC+ and access to HBO Max Basic With Ads and discovery+. Our service also includes 100+ free channels and premium add-ons like STARZ and MGM+.

Our extensive library boasts over 85,000 titles, and our unlimited DVR allows users to save their favorite shows and movies for up to a year, skipping ads for a seamless viewing experience. Stream on up to three devices simultaneously, whether on your phone, tablet, laptop, or TV using Roku, Apple TV, Fire TV, Samsung TV, Android TV, Vizio TV, or Chromecast.

Philo is headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in New York City and Cambridge, MA. Our leadership team includes alums from HBO, Tubi, and Meraki, and is backed by NEA and industry partners like Warner Brothers Discovery, Paramount, AMC, and A&E.

Join us at Philo and be part of a team that's shaping the future of TV!

Phorest started in 2002 on a busy salon reception desk as a simple text-reminder tool.

We’re a product-led SaaS company solving real-world problems across bookings, payments, marketing and business management, with a big focus on building great experiences for both our salons and the people who use our products.

Everything we build helps the salon and medspa industry thrive.

We're also a Certified B Corp, and 25% of the company is owned by Phoresters. When the company grows, everyone has a stake in that.
About the team

Our ambition is to become the number one platform for premium hair, beauty and aesthetics businesses globally. For our Product & Engineering teams, that means understanding the people behind those businesses and building thoughtful, reliable products that make a real difference to how they work.

You’ll join our Checkout team, building the integrated payments experiences behind PhorestPay — from in-salon card payments and online deposits to tipping. The team connects payments with the day-to-day running of salons, spas and clinics, helping them take payments smoothly and spend less time on administration.

We’re a team that cares deeply about the salons, spas and clinics we serve, the quality of our work and each other. We start with understanding what matters to the people using our products, and work together to solve problems that make a real difference to their businesses.

The Opportunity
As a Senior Software Engineer focused on backend engineering, you’ll help shape the next generation of PhorestPay checkout. The basket brings together the items a client is purchasing, so a salon can review the sale and take payment in one place. You’ll help strengthen the systems behind this everyday experience, making it easier to support new ways for salons to take and manage payments.

You’ll work on the backend capabilities behind experiences such as Buy Now, Pay Later, regional payment methods, and future multi-merchant revenue sharing that splits funds between salons and staff as well as new stream of Embedded Finance. This means tackling hard problems across payment flows, data modelling, integrations and reliability, while designing services that can evolve as our products grow.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You’ll partner with Checkout, Payments Integrations, Product and Design to turn an evolving roadmap into reliable, maintainable systems. • Lead the design and delivery of complex backend solutions, including distributed systems, RESTful APIs and message-driven integrations.

• Break down ambiguous problems into clear approaches, identifying technical risks, dependencies and bottlenecks early.

• Work with Product, Design and engineering colleagues to shape plans and make sound trade-offs between reliability, maintainability, delivery pace and business value.

• Lead cross-team technical initiatives, building alignment and communicating decisions clearly to technical and non-technical colleagues.

• Champion test-driven development, CI/CD and robust observability, using monitoring and debugging to improve the reliability and performance of our services.

• Improve engineering standards, architectural patterns and reusable approaches that help teams deliver high-quality software sustainably.

• Mentor and coach engineers, share knowledge and give constructive code-review feedback that strengthens the team’s technical thinking and output.

Who You Are
You’re a senior backend engineer who enjoys solving complex problems and turning them into dependable systems. You take ownership when the path isn’t clear, communicate trade-offs thoughtfully and work well across disciplines. You care about the people and businesses using your software, and you help others do their best work.

You have:

• Significant software engineering experience, typically 7+ years, with depth in backend engineering and a track record of technical leadership and meaningful impact.

• Strong proficiency in at least one object-oriented or functional language, such as Java, Kotlin or TypeScript.

• Experience designing and evolving distributed systems, RESTful APIs and message-driven integrations.

• Strong data-modelling and relational database skills, with a focus on correctness, performance and maintainability.

• Hands-on experience with test-driven development, CI/CD and observability, alongside strong debugging and monitoring skills using tools such as Honeycomb, Datadog or Grafana.

Exceptional by design. A career where you can shape the future of the firm's data.
The opportunity
Join a team where your expertise truly matters. Pinsent Masons is looking for an Interim Data Programme Technical Lead, on an initial 12-month contract, to provide the technical leadership and direction for our strategic data programme.
Working alongside the Programme Manager, you’ll take ownership of the programme’s technical direction, ensuring our data solutions are coherent, secure, scalable and capable of delivering measurable business value. This is a hands-on role, where you’ll lead architects, engineers, developers, analysts and delivery partners, combining technical expertise with confident programme and stakeholder leadership.

• Lead architects, data engineers, BI developers, analysts and integration specialists across internal teams and external delivery partners.
• Shape end-to-end data solution architecture across Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Microsoft Purview, Entra ID and Power BI.

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Integrated Campaign Manager, Brand & GTM to join our Integrated Marketing team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help architect, roll out, project manage, and drive the Go-To-Market (GTM) execution for our major 2027 brand marketing strategy and campaigns and be part of turning brand strategy, positioning, and creative concepts into operational GTM blueprints as we scale our multi-segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) reach across 6 key European markets. If you're excited about high-visibility, full-funnel orchestration and balancing long-term brand equity building with full-funnel conversion, and are passionate about integrated brand and GTM marketing in high-growth B2B SaaS, then this is the opportunity for you!



Please bear in mind this role is a temporary contract of 1 year. 




WHO YOU’LL BE WORKING WITH AND REPORTING TO 

You’ll report to our Director of Integrated Marketing and work closely with teams in Brand Marketing, Digital, Field/Events, Content, PR, Product Marketing (PMM), Marketing Ops, Data, and Sales/Growth channels. Our team is highly collaborative and dedicated to bridging top-of-funnel brand awareness with lower-funnel acquisition, ensuring every campaign moment translates into market salience, customer engagement, and measurable business impact. You’ll also have the chance to partner with teams across country teams, local market stakeholders, Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field squads to ensure success.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

As a Senior Campaign Manager, you will: 

 - Integrated GTM Architecture & Strategic Planning: Translate the overarching 2027 brand strategy into actionable, full-funnel GTM campaign blueprints across SMB, Mid-Market, and Enterprise segments, architecting campaign flighting and distribution models across 6 European markets.

 - The "Master Brief" & Cross-Functional Squad Leadership: Own and author comprehensive Integrated Campaign Master Briefs, leading the operational rhythm of cross-functional squads to execute multi-channel strategies (OOH, Paid Social, VIP activations, Digital, ABM) on time and within scope.

 - Localization & Regional Adaptation: Partner with country teams and local market stakeholders to ensure master campaign frameworks balance global consistency with local relevance and execution precision.

 - Strategic Brand Partnership & Enablement: Serve as the strategic execution peer to the Brand Marketing Lead, while partnering with Sales Leadership, SDRs, and Field teams to equip customer-facing squads with the stories, tools, and campaign momentum needed to capitalize on campaign-generated intent.

 - Campaign Operations, Budget & ROI Accountability: Maintain and protect the integrated campaign master calendar, manage and allocate the multi-country integrated campaign budget, and partner with Marketing Ops, Data, and Brand Intelligence to track brand lift, consideration, pipeline growth, and closed-won impact.




WHAT YOU BRING 


You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

 - A proven track record leading multi-million dollar, multi-country, full-funnel integrated campaigns in high-growth B2B SaaS or tech environments.

 - Deep experience taking high-level brand frameworks and translating them into multi-channel GTM blueprints across varied audience segments (SMB to Enterprise).

 - High proficiency in aligning cross-functional teams (Creative, Digital, PR, Ops, Sales) and holding squads accountable to tight deadlines and complex campaign launches.

 - Deep understanding of how to run campaigns across diverse European markets, with a clear perspective on modular campaign design and local adaptation.

 - Experience with tracking brand-to-pipeline performance metrics, campaign flighting dynamics, brand lift, consideration, and total ROI.

 - A background in integrated marketing, GTM campaign management, or brand marketing orchestration within B2B technology or SaaS.




WHY IS THIS ROLE A GOOD FIT FOR YOU



This role is a good fit for you if:

 - You thrive as the operational bridge between high-level brand strategy and lower-funnel demand generation, turning concepts into structured GTM blueprints.

 - You love leading cross-functional squads across multiple international markets, balancing consistency with local nuances across 6 key European countries.

 - You take pride in end-to-end accountability, from authoring master briefs and handling multi-country budgets to tracking downstream pipeline velocity and closed-won revenue impact.

This role is not a good fit for you if:

 - You prefer focusing purely on high-level creative ideation, copy, or audience insight development without building the operational execution machinery.

 - You prefer running single-channel or single-market marketing initiatives rather than orchestrating complex, multi-segment (SMB to Enterprise), multi-channel matrices.

 - You are uncomfortable navigating data, campaign flighting performance, budget allocations, and downstream pipeline attribution alongside brand metrics.
   
   


HOW YOU’LL DEVELOP IN THIS ROLE 

In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll:

 - Lead the architecture and rollout of the 2027 integrated brand campaign calendar across all target European markets.

 - Collaborate with the Brand Marketing Lead, country teams, and Marketing Ops to stand up the Master Briefing framework and streamline cross-functional execution rhythms.

 - Grow your skills in full-funnel orchestration and multi-market scale, driving measurable brand lift, consideration, and downstream pipeline velocity as Pleo continues to expand.

THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

 1. Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.

 2. Hiring Manager Interview: A 45 minute chat to deep dive into your experience

 3. Challenge & Team Interview: We will send you a take home test and invite you to present during a 60 minute team interview. This is an opportunity to show us how you would handle the day to day of the role

 4. Final Interview: A final interview with a senior leader

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired for this role, we received a total vast number of applications but only a few were selected for an intro call.Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

 - CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

 - Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

 - Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

### Where we are now

We started with the agent itself, the chat and the first skills and rules that made the daily routine faster: checking accounts and delivery, moving budgets to the winners, killing losing creatives early, relaunching the ones worth another run. Now we automate the whole media buying. Here's the full picture:

- **The agent.** Every regular decision runs on the agent, on AI skills and deterministic rules, on the client's own logic and their full-funnel data. On thousands of ads at once, each decision weighs delayed conversions, creative burnout, testing and scaling thresholds, cooldown days, and data quality.

- **A catalog of 100+ skills** that automates the recurring decisions: anomaly detection, data validation, results analysis, creative testing, experiment planning, budget forecasting, scaling decisions, and action recommendations. These are the media buying best practices for each channel that grew into the catalog.

- **A dedicated AI marketing engineer** connects the client's data and ad accounts, loads their business context, and adapts all of this based on their playbook. The system that runs on their unique setup, their processes, their data, and their funnels, and allows their team to do more with less.

So the client's marketers stop managing media buying by hand. They set the strategy and define the goals, Plurio handles the rest, and every decision is made faster, which moves their business forward. Their attention goes into creative and strategy, and the goal we share with them is to win the competition.

### The role

The AI marketing engineer owns the client's marketing targets and improves those metrics by automating the client's media buying. That means:

###### 1

**Onboard the client and set the business context.** You connect the client's full-funnel data and their ad accounts, and give the agent what it decides on: unit economics, P&L, products, geos, funnels. Their own media buying playbook goes inside the agent, as context, rules, and skills.

###### 2

**Adapt and build skills and automation rules.** From Plurio's catalog of prebuilt skills you adapt what fits the client's goals, their case, and their playbook. If the skills they need isn't there, you build it yourself. You backtest your skills and rule cascades on historical data before they go into the product and start running the media buying. The rules that manage the ads are deterministic SQL with the campaign logic written into them, and they run with guardrails: shutdown periods, double-checks, change history.

###### 3

**Explain the decisions and work directly with the client's team.** You walk the client's Heads of UA and CMOs through the logic the agent runs on, and through the methodology changes you propose. You help their marketers run the agent themselves, and you take the hard conversations about spend and KPIs. Every decision and every insight is checked on their data, so you can defend it.

###### 4

**Standardize what works.** What you get working on one client, you pack into the system: a template you reuse when launching the next ones. It also becomes part of the methodology every client runs on. You're closest to real campaigns and real clients, so what you find goes into the agent.

So you pack what worked into methodology, tools, and templates. That's what makes the next launch and the next client adaptation faster.

- **Strong English.** Confident speaking and writing with English-speaking clients.

**Scale new technology. Improve manufacturing. Build engineering capability.** 

**About Promethean** 

Promethean is scaling a new class of materials, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with the potential to transform the efficient capture, storage, and separation of industrial gases, in applications like biogas upgrading, industrial dehumidification, and carbon capture. 

As we continue to move from pilot-scale production to industrial manufacturing, we are looking for an experienced **Senior Process Engineer** to help continue the development of safe, reliable, and scalable manufacturing operations. 

This is an opportunity to play a key role in the growth of a novel chemical manufacturing business, solve challenging engineering problems, and help develop the next generation of engineers. 

​ 

**The Role** 

You will work across the various scales of Promethean's manufacturing facilities, supporting day-to-day production, plant improvement activities, equipment projects, and manufacturing scale-up. 

This is a hands-on manufacturing role within a small, but growing, engineering team. 

This is not an office-based, project management, or design-only position. We are looking for an engineer who enjoys working directly with plant, equipment, operators, and improving the safety, quality, productivity, and economics of manufacturing processes. 

You will be expected to spend significant time in the plant, supporting manufacturing campaigns, troubleshooting equipment and processes, commissioning new systems, and helping ensure product is manufactured safely, efficiently, and consistently. 

Alongside your technical responsibilities, you will play an important role in developing junior engineers through coaching, mentoring, and day-to-day support. 

**Key Responsibilities** 

**Manufacturing & Operations** 

- Support and improve pilot-scale and commercial manufacturing operations 

- Run and support manufacturing campaigns 

- Troubleshoot process, equipment, and operational issues 

- Work closely with operators, technicians and engineers to ensure safe and efficient production 

- Drive improvements in plant reliability, productivity, yield, and product quality 

- Monitor process performance and identify opportunities for improvement 

**Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement** 

- Lead process optimisation and continuous improvement initiatives 

- Investigate plant issues and implement practical, sustainable solutions 

- Conduct root cause analysis and drive corrective and preventive actions 

- Develop and improve operating procedures, standards, and engineering documentation 

- Support process safety activities including risk assessments, SOP development, and hazard reviews 

- Identify opportunities to improve safety, operational efficiency, and manufacturing robustness 

**Projects & Scale-Up** 

- Support the transfer of new processes from R&D into manufacturing 

- Specify, design, and implement plant modifications and equipment upgrades 

- Lead equipment installation, commissioning, and start-up activities 

- Support the development of manufacturing systems required for future scale-up 

- Work with internal and external stakeholders to deliver engineering projects successfully 

**Team Development** 

- Coach and mentor junior engineers through practical day-to-day engineering activities 

- Provide technical guidance and support across manufacturing and engineering teams 

- Review engineering work and share best practice 

- Help develop an engineering culture built around safety, ownership, problem-solving, and continuous improvement 

**What We're Looking For** 

We are looking for someone who combines strong technical capability with practical manufacturing experience. 

You will likely have: 

- A degree in Chemical Engineering.  

- 8+ years of experience in chemical manufacturing or chemical process engineering.  

- Experience operating, troubleshooting, and improving chemical manufacturing processes 

- A strong understanding of process safety and risk management principles 

- Experience delivering plant modifications, commissioning activities, or process improvement projects 

- Experience working within regulated or safety-critical industrial environments 

- Strong communication and problem-solving skills 

- Experience coaching, mentoring, or developing early-career engineers, technicians, or operators 

- Chartered Engineer status, whilst not a pre-requisite, will be a significant advantage for this role. 

**You must have full, unrestricted right to work in the UK.** 

**Why Join Promethean?** 

- Play a key role in scaling an innovative manufacturing technology 

- Work on products with the potential for significant environmental impact 

- Take ownership of meaningful engineering challenges from day one 

- Combine manufacturing, process engineering, continuous improvement, and project delivery in a single role 

- Help shape the engineering standards and culture of a growing business 

- Directly influence how new manufacturing facilities and processes are developed 

- Develop junior engineers while continuing to grow your own technical and leadership capabilities 

- Work in a fast-moving environment where good ideas can be implemented quickly 

**What Success Looks Like** 

After a year, you are a trusted senior engineer within the business. 

You have delivered measurable improvements to plant safety, reliability, productivity, and manufacturing performance. You are helping run manufacturing operations successfully, have led key engineering improvements and projects, and are recognised as a source of practical technical expertise. 

Junior engineers are developing faster because of your support and mentorship. Most importantly, you have helped build a safer, more reliable, and more scalable manufacturing operation capable of supporting Promethean's future growth. 

**If you enjoy solving real manufacturing problems, leading from the plant floor, and helping develop both processes and people, we'd like to hear from you.**

Who you work with

Running the transaction with the CEO & CFO

 1. Refresh the deck, the KPI pack and the data room every quarter.

Across both

 2. Keep the record: what each investor asked, what we answered, what we promised and what we learned.

 - One version of the story across the deck, the model and the data room.

 - The CEO pitches. You are the investors' contact for everything around the room. You are judged on how the round runs, not on the pitch.

As Senior Specialist, Payroll Client Services for the UK and Ireland, you will be the Tier 2 payroll expert and operational owner for this country pod. You will resolve complex and sensitive payroll issues, maintain operational readiness, and ensure customers receive accurate, timely, and compliant support. You will combine deep UK and Ireland payroll expertise with strong client service, cross-functional coordination, team enablement, and ownership of improvements that reduce repeat issues.

This is a senior individual-contributor role. You will make operational decisions within agreed portfolio priorities, coordinate work across Payroll Operations, Product, Engineering, Compliance, and Customer Experience, and influence outcomes without formal authority. You will also maintain backup capability and mentor P1 and P2 colleagues. Formal people management, staffing, capacity, and portfolio-wide prioritisation remain with the Portfolio DRI.

What you bring

Required

- Significant hands-on experience in end-to-end payroll processing, payroll operations, or complex payroll client support.
- Strong working knowledge of UK and Ireland payroll legislation, statutory requirements, compliance obligations, payroll calendars, and common operational dependencies.
- Demonstrated ability to independently investigate and resolve complex or ambiguous payroll issues spanning multiple systems, workflows, stakeholders, or products.
- Experience handling sensitive customer situations and high-impact escalations with clear, accurate, and empathetic communication.
- Strong analytical and root-cause problem-solving skills, including the ability to use ticket trends, service data, and customer feedback to identify recurring issues and risks.
- Proven ownership of operational improvements from problem definition through implementation and impact measurement.
- Ability to coordinate cross-functional investigations, establish clear owners and actions, and drive work to completion without relying on formal authority.
- Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with confidence working asynchronously and documenting decisions, processes, and guidance clearly.
- Experience maintaining payroll knowledge resources, SOPs, readiness materials, calculators, or escalation guidance.
- A collaborative approach to mentoring colleagues, transferring knowledge, and building reliable backup coverage.
- Ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced, international, remote-first environment while exercising sound judgement and escalating material risks appropriately.

Preferred

- Experience supporting enterprise, strategic, or high-value customers in a payroll, HR technology, professional services, or SaaS environment.
- Experience working across Payroll Operations, Product, Engineering, Compliance, or Customer Experience teams.
- Demonstrated contribution to legislative or product-change readiness, incident response, or country-level operational governance.
- Familiarity with ticketing, reporting, and knowledge-management tools used to monitor service health and identify trends.
- Experience coaching or onboarding payroll specialists in an informal leadership capacity.

## Job Description

### **What this job can offer you**

This is a transformative time to join Remote and make a personal difference in the global employment space as **Principal, Marketing Analytics**. As the highest-level individual contributor within our Marketing Analytics team, you won't just support our strategy—you will shape it.

We are looking for a visionary, highly autonomous expert to serve as the primary strategic partner to the Director, Marketing Analytics, the VP of Growth Marketing, and the broader executive leadership team. In this P5 role, you will own the long-term vision for our marketing data ecosystem, moving beyond project execution to architect frameworks that define our global marketing strategy. From pioneering next-generation predictive attribution models to unlocking the macroeconomic impact of brand equity, your governance will dictate Remote’s global investment strategy.

### **What you bring**

- **Professional Experience:** Distinguished track record in marketing analytics, business intelligence, or data science, with extensive experience specifically embedded in high-growth B2B SaaS or enterprise environments.
- **Architect-Level Attribution:** Mastery in designing, scaling, and defending complex attribution frameworks (Multi-Touch, Media Mix Modeling, and Unified Measurement) across complex, non-linear enterprise buyer journeys.
- **Macro-Funnel Vision:** Deep expertise in quantifying abstract, non-paid focus areas; a proven history of designing measurement frameworks for global brand health, organic ecosystems, Share of Voice (SoV), and long-tail market expansion.
- **Advanced Technical Mastery:** Expert-level proficiency across the modern data stack. You are comfortable writing production-grade code, architecting data models in **dbt**, optimizing complex **Snowflake** environments, and leveraging AI/automation to scale analytical workflows.
- **Ecosystem Governance:** Deep familiarity navigating and integrating enterprise CRMs and automation systems (Salesforce, HubSpot) with advanced BI ecosystems (Sigma, Tableau, Looker).
- **Executive Gravitas & Communication:** Exceptional ability to command a room of C-suite executives, transforming dense, highly technical data structures into high-impact strategic narratives that drive organizational change.
- **Language:** Professional fluency in written and spoken English.
- **Remote-First Mindset:** While experience working remotely isn't required, a strong knack for asynchronous communication, high autonomy, and self-driven documentation is highly valued.

### **Key Responsibilities**

### Strategic Vision & Predictive Modeling

- **Next-Gen Attribution & MMM:** Own and evolve the architectural vision for Remote’s attribution logic. Merge multi-touch attribution (MTA) with Media Mix Modeling (MMM) to build a unified view of both performance marketing and organic Top-of-the-Funnel (TOFU) streams.
- **Predictive LTV & Budget Optimization:** Architect and maintain advanced Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and predictive churn models. Direct how these high-quality predictive signals are fed back into ad platforms and algorithmic bidding engines to maximize efficiency.
- **Executive Planning & Capital Allocation:** Partner directly with finance and marketing leadership to drive annual and quarterly planning. Own the macroeconomic forecasting models that dictate global budget allocation and ROI expectations.

### Global Frameworks & Data Governance

- **Brand & Organic Quantification:** Establish the global standard for measuring non-paid marketing initiatives. Build robust, defensible frameworks for Share of Voice, brand sentiment, and organic compounding to justify long-term brand investments.
- **Macro-Funnel Optimization:** Analyze the end-to-end B2B funnel—from dark social and initial awareness to closed-won enterprise revenue—identifying systemic friction points and multi-million dollar white-space opportunities.
- **Data Strategy & Guardianship:** Act as the ultimate authority on marketing data integrity. Partner with Data Engineering and RevOps to design the upstream data infrastructure, ensuring information flowing through HubSpot, Salesforce, and Snowflake remains an unassailable "single source of truth."

### Leadership & Innovation

- **Organizational Multiplier & Mentorship:** While this role has no initial direct reports, you will serve as the technical and strategic lead for the analytics org. You will mentor senior analysts, elevate the team's technical bar, and foster a culture of analytical excellence.
- **AI & Automation Pioneering:** Standardize the deployment of AI, machine learning, and advanced automation within the marketing analytics stack to accelerate insight generation and eliminate manual reporting overhead.

Role Purpose

The Workforce Planning Expert is the enterprise subject matter expert responsible for ensuring Rolls-Royce SMR can deliver its strategic and programme objectives through an affordable, resilient and executable workforce plan. The role advises on the workforce construct required to deliver the target operating model, balancing capability, capacity, cost, productivity, delivery pace, and risk across permanent employees, contingent labour, strategic partners and outsourced services. 

The role is responsible for the design, development and continuous improvement of an integrated workforce planning approach spanning trusted in-year plans, rolling 2-3 year forecasts and a strategic 3-5 year workforce roadmap. It supports the translation of business strategy, operating model choices, programme delivery assumptions, and organisational design into quantified workforce demand, capability requirements, cost profiles, sourcing choices and clear interventions. 

The role provides independent, evidence-led challenge and expert advice to senior leaders, partnering across Finance, Portfolio and Programme, PMO, Organisation Design, HR, Talent Acquisition and functional leadership. It will establish the governance, modelling standards, data discipline and decision forums required to turn workforce information into enterprise action, enabling timely choices on build, buy, borrow, partner or outsource and ensuring material workforce risks, dependencies and constraints are understood and actively managed. Success is achieved through influential partnering, robust governance, evidence-based challenge and the translation of workforce insight into tangible business outcomes, capability readiness and programme delivery confidence. 

What we’ll need you to deliver

• A single, trusted and governed in-year workforce plan aligned to approved budgets, programme and commercial milestones, organisational design and recruitment capacity. 
• A rolling 2-3 year workforce forecast and 3-5 year strategic workforce roadmap that identify when, where and at what cost critical capacity and capability are required. 
• An integrated view of workforce demand and supply across permanent employees, contingent labour, partners and outsourced services, with clear recommendations on the optimum resource mix. 
• Workforce planning is embedded as a core business discipline through effective stakeholder engagement, governance, and decision-making forums, ensuring leaders are equipped to make timely, evidence-based workforce choices and are accountable for delivery of agreed actions. 
• Strategic workforce recommendations are translated into measurable business outcomes, including improved delivery confidence, reduced workforce risk, enhanced capability readiness, increased resource agility, and optimised workforce investment decisions. 
• Robust capacity, capability, cost, sourcing and scenario models that enable senior leaders to compare options and make explicit trade-offs between affordability, speed, risk, flexibility and delivery confidence. 
• A prioritised capability gap and workforce risk register, including dependencies, constraints, scarcity, succession exposure and mitigation actions with named ownership. 
• A sustainable enterprise workforce planning governance and approvals framework, supported by common definitions, planning assumptions, controls, standards and an agreed planning calendar. 
• Actionable workforce intelligence that shapes talent acquisition, internal mobility, learning and development, succession, contingent labour and strategic partner strategies. 
• Improved workforce effectiveness through regular review of utilisation, workload, productivity, spans, layers, role design and deployment, with evidence-based optimisation recommendations. 
• A strong enterprise community of workforce planning practice, strengthening capability in leaders and planning leads and embedding consistent, repeatable planning disciplines. 

What we’re looking for

• Extensive experience leading strategic workforce planning in a complex, regulated, safety-critical or programme-led environment.
• Ability to translate enterprise strategy, business plans and target operating models into integrated short, medium and long-term workforce plans, and to provide authoritative challenge and advice to senior leaders.
• Deep practical expertise across capacity, capability, sourcing, cost and scenario modelling. 
• Ability to determine the optimum mix of permanent employees, contingent labour, partners and outsourced services, evaluating build, buy, borrow, partner and outsource choices against cost, risk, speed, capability and flexibility.
• Advanced analytical capability with the ability to integrate complex workforce, finance, programme and organisational data; establish planning assumptions and data standards; create clear scenarios; and convert analysis into compelling executive insight, recommendations and decisions. 
• Comfortable challenging data quality and resolving conflicting assumptions.
• Strong understanding of organisation structures, accountability models, role design, role layering, spans of control, matrix relationships and capability frameworks. 
• Ability to distinguish organisation design from workforce planning and translate design choices into quantified capacity, capability, cost and resourcing implications.
• Proven ability to establish governance, controls, planning rhythms and enterprise standards, and to influence senior stakeholders across Finance, Portfolio and Programme, PMO, HR, Talent Acquisition, Organisation Design and functional leadership. 
• Ability to move from diagnosis to executable interventions covering recruitment, development, deployment, succession, contingent labour and partners.
• Recognised strategic workforce planning, people analytics, organisation design, change, project/programme or HR professional accreditation is desirable. 
• Demonstrable mastery of workforce planning methods, planning assumptions, scenario analysis, demand and supply modelling, capability assessment and financial evaluation. 
• Advanced proficiency in workforce data analysis, modelling and presentation tools, with the ability to explain complex analysis clearly to executive and non-technical audiences.

We're looking for a systems-obsessed GTM Engineer to own and architect our outbound revenue infrastructure across client accounts. This is a hands-on builder role, the person who sits at the intersection of data, automation, AI, and Outbound strategy, designing fully automated outbound systems that run at scale.

What you’ll do

- Architect end-to-end outbound systems: from ICP definition and TAM scoping all the way to campaign launch, CRM sync, and performance reporting

- Stay ahead of the tooling curve: test and adopt emerging data, enrichment, and AI tools before clients ask for them

Who you are

- You have 2+ years of experience building outbound or revenue systems: ideally at a B2B agency, GTM consultancy, or fast-moving SaaS company
- You're an existing Clay user, you know more than the basics, you've built complex workflows with AI columns, Claygent, waterfalls, and custom API integrations
- You think in systems, not tasks. When you see a manual process, your first instinct is to automate it
- You're technical without being a developer. Comfortable with APIs, webhooks, and JSON, and you can write a basic Python or JS snippet when no-code isn't enough
- You have a commercial mindset. You understand what a good ICP looks like, why a message fails, and how outbound performance connects to pipeline

- You're self-directed and accountable. You can take a client brief, define the system architecture, and ship without hand-holding
- You have experience in the Tech, SaaS, or B2B software space, you understand the buyers our clients are targeting
- Open to candidates coming from RevOps, outbound operations, Clay consulting, or senior BDR/SDR roles who have made the shift into systems building

In addition to joining a fast-growing GTM team, we also offer:

- Remote work, no more commutes
- Collaborative, friendly, and passionate team
- Paid vacation, days off, and sick leave
- Exciting team-building activities
- Free books and Kindles to help you grow
- Specialized training programs to become the strongest Clay and GTM expert
- Opportunity to work with international B2B brands, startups, and scaleups
- Exposure to modern AI, outbound, and GTM tools
- A role where your ideas can directly affect business growth for your clients
