The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with Scale Labs, we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety.

That work includes finding where models fail, checking whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Scholars take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded.

Each scholar owns a substantial part of a safety research project. You'll work alongside a mentor from the research question through the experiments to deciding what to test next.

Research Areas

Mentors will guide Research Scholars on projects in selected AI safety research areas in select AI safety research areas, such as:

• AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AIs, including detecting harmful intent or deception.

• Alignment auditing and evaluations: Building scalable methods to test whether models have hidden goals, misaligned behaviors or unsafe tendencies.

• Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior.

• Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) safety: Investigating how to keep AI systems safe and aligned as AIs increasingly contribute to their own development.

• Science of Evaluations: examining when and how models recognize they're being tested, and how situational awareness affects the reliability/validity of evaluations.

• Misuse risks and evaluations: Developing methods to assess how AI systems could be exploited by malicious actors, including evaluating their potential to enable harmful activities.

Projects are matched to demonstrated expertise; we don’t expect any candidate to cover every area.

Representative Research

• ASPI: 728 task–attack scenarios testing how clarification-seeking changes prompt-injection vulnerability in LLM agents.

• PropensityBench: simulating real-world pressure to choose between safe or harmful behavior

• BioRiskEval: evaluating whether safeguards for open-weight bio-foundation models remain robust under fine-tuning and probing.

• See more work from the Human Frontier Collective.

What You'll Do

Projects are mentor-guided. By default, you will be given a list of research proposals and match you with one based on your research interests and background. You’ll meet weekly with a Scale researcher who sets the direction and gives feedback, and you will drive the day-to-day work.

• Own research end to end: Turn a high-level safety question into hypotheses, baselines, and controlled experiments, and produce work that others can inspect and build on.

• Build the measurement: Implement and debug evaluation harnesses, agent environments, datasets, monitoring methods, or post-training experiments.

• Exercise research judgment: Identify confounds, separate what a model can do from what it tends to do, make sense of negative results, and decide what to try next without step-by-step direction.

• Make the work legible: Produce reproducible code, experiment logs, analysis, and precise technical writing. External outputs, where appropriate, remain subject to research, security, and communications review. Outputs also include research papers, which will be submitted to top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).

Who We're Looking For

You may be a good fit if you:

• are motivated by ensuring the safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems;

• are interested in technical safety research, such as alignment evaluations, AI control, monitoring, multi-agent safety, or open-weight model safety;

• are pursuing or have completed a PhD in CS, ML, statistics, mathematics, or a related field (we also encourage researchers with an equivalent track record to apply);

• can make progress with high-level guidance, including implementing, debugging, getting unstuck, interpreting results, and proposing next experiments;

• communicate research clearly and handle confidential information and internal systems responsibly.

Application Process

• Apply: Submit your resume or CV, your Google Scholar profile if you have one, and one research project you substantially owned, with 2–3 sentences on your contribution.

• Research background discussion: Walk us through a past project, including what you tried, what didn't work, and what you learned.

• Research design: Work through a research problem with us and propose how you'd approach it.

• Onboarding: Successful candidates complete the applicable recruiting, work-authorization, security, and project-onboarding steps.

POSITION OVERVIEW

As Junior Paid Influencer Manager, you will support the planning and delivery of SEGA’s paid influencer campaigns across EMEA.

Reporting to the Head of Paid Media, you will work alongside the Paid Media team to bring creator campaigns to life across SEGA’s portfolio of Western and Japanese titles. Your responsibilities will include creator research, preparing campaign briefs, coordinating content approvals, maintaining campaign records and supporting reporting.

You will work with agencies, talent partners and internal teams to keep activity organised, on schedule and aligned with agreed campaign objectives, helping deliver creator content that connects with local gaming and entertainment audiences across EMEA.

With guidance and support from the Paid Media team, you will take responsibility for day-to-day campaign coordination and agreed deliverables, building towards managing smaller activations within approved plans and budgets.

This role is suited to someone early in their marketing career who is organised, interested in gaming and creator culture, and keen to develop practical experience in paid influencer marketing.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Campaign Planning & Coordination

• Support the Paid Media team in planning and delivering paid influencer campaigns across EMEA.
• Coordinate day-to-day campaign tasks, maintaining timelines, tracking deliverables and following up with agencies and partners to keep activity on schedule.
• Coordinate the distribution of game codes, campaign assets and supporting materials, helping creators and partners prepare for activations.

Creator Research & Partner Support

• Research creators and review agency shortlists against agreed criteria, gathering information on audience demographics, content quality, engagement and market relevance to support creator selection.
• Support relationships with creators, talent agencies and influencer partners, handling routine campaign communications and escalating questions or issues where required.
• Help review agency proposals and creator deliverables against agreed briefs, flagging questions around content quality, audience suitability or local relevance to the team.
• Monitor creator content and trends across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Twitch, sharing relevant examples and ideas for future campaigns.

Content Approvals & Paid Amplification

• Organise creator concept and content reviews with Product Marketing, Studio Brand and other relevant teams, collating feedback and tracking approvals.
• Coordinate the handover of approved creator content for paid amplification, maintaining records of agreed usage rights, permissions and asset requirements.
• Track contractual deliverables and advertising disclosure requirements using agreed processes, flagging missing information or potential issues to the relevant colleagues.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Work closely with the Community team and colleagues across SEGA West Publishing to support alignment between paid and organic creator activity across campaign beats, sharing creator recommendations, campaign plans and performance learnings.
• Coordinate the day-to-day running of TikTok’s Gaming Incentive Programme for SEGA across EMEA territories, working with TikTok and the Product Marketing team to organise campaign briefs, track creator activity and deliverables, and report on results.

QUALIFICATIONS

Essential
• 1–2 years’ relevant experience in influencer marketing, creator partnerships, social media or campaign coordination, gained within a brand, agency, talent business or comparable environment.
• Familiarity with the creator landscape across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Twitch, and an understanding of how content algorithms and audiences differ between platforms.
• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to coordinate multiple tasks and campaign deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare briefs, consolidate feedback and provide concise updates.
• A collaborative approach, with confidence working with internal colleagues and external partners.
• Confidence using spreadsheets and presentation tools to maintain campaign trackers and support reporting.
• An interest in campaign performance and the ability to draw practical observations from creator and content data.
• A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the judgement to flag issues and seek guidance when needed.
• Passion for gaming, creator culture and the evolving influencer ecosystem.

Desired

### Principal Data Engineer

### Who We Are

Simple Machines is a global, independent technology consultancy operating across Sydney, New Zealand, London, and Poland. We design and build modern data platforms, intelligent systems, and bespoke software at the intersection of **Data Engineering, Software Engineering** and **AI.**

We work with enterprises, scale-ups, and government to turn messy, high-value data into products, platforms, and decisions that actually move the needle.

We don’t do generic. We build things that matter - **We engineer data to life™.**

## Requirements

### The Role

This is a **hands-on principal engineering role**, not an architecture-only seat and not a support function. You’ll be responsible for technical direction, platform design and architectural decision-making.

You'll design and build **greenfield data platforms**, real-time pipelines, and data products for clients who are serious about using data properly. You’ll work in small, high-calibre teams and operate close to both the problem and the client.

If you enjoy solving hard data problems, shaping modern architectures (data mesh, data products, contracts), and delivering real outcomes — this is your lane.

**Lead Platform & Architecture Design**

- Own the end-to-end architecture of modern, cloud-native data platforms
- Design scalable data ecosystems using **data mesh, data products, and data contracts**
- Make high-impact architectural decisions across ingestion, storage, processing, and access layers
- Ensure platforms are secure, compliant, and production-grade by design

- Design and deliver cloud-native data platforms using **Databricks, Snowflake, AWS, and GCP**
- Apply modern architectural patterns: **data mesh, data products, and data contracts**
- Integrate deeply with client systems to enable scalable, consumer-oriented data access

- Build and optimise **batch and real-time pipelines**
- Work with streaming and event-driven tech such as **Kafka, Flink, Kinesis, Pub/Sub**
- Orchestrate workflows using **Airflow, Dataflow, Glue**

**Work at Scale**

- Process and transform large datasets using **Spark and Flink**
- Design systems that perform in production - not just on paper

**Own Data Storage & Performance**

- Work across relational, NoSQL, and analytical stores (Postgres, BigQuery, Snowflake, Cassandra, MongoDB)
- Optimise storage formats and access patterns (Parquet, Delta, ORC, Avro)

**Cloud, Security & Governance**

- Implement secure, compliant data solutions with **security by design**
- Embed governance without killing developer velocity

**Consult and Influence**

- Work directly with clients to understand problems and shape solutions
- Translate business needs into pragmatic engineering decisions
- Act as a trusted technical advisor, not just an order taker

**Technical Leadership & Quality**

- Set engineering standards, patterns, and best practices across teams
- Review designs and code, providing clear technical direction and mentorship
- Raise the bar on data quality, testing, observability, and operational excellence

- Strong **Python and SQL**
- Deep experience with **Spark** and modern data platforms (Databricks / Snowflake)
- Solid grasp of cloud data services (AWS or GCP)

**Architecture & Design Judgement**

- Demonstrated ownership of large-scale data platform architectures
- Strong data modelling skills and architectural decision-making ability
- Comfortable balancing trade-offs between performance, cost, and complexity

**Data Platform Experience**

- Built and operated **large-scale data pipelines** in production
- Strong data modelling capability and architectural judgement
- Comfortable with multiple storage technologies and formats

**Engineering Discipline**

- Infrastructure-as-code experience (**Terraform, Pulumi**)
- CI/CD pipelines using tools like **GitHub Actions, ArgoCD**
- Data testing and quality frameworks (**dbt, Great Expectations, Soda**)

**Delivery & Consulting Mindset**

- Experience in consulting or professional services environments
- Strong consulting instincts — able to challenge assumptions and guide clients toward better outcomes
- Comfortable mentoring senior engineers and influencing technical culture

- You’ll be surrounded by senior engineers who actually know their craft
- You’ll have autonomy, influence, and room to grow

The Opportunity

Sinara is currently hiring for its 2026 intake of technical graduates in the fields of software engineering, QA and application support & DevOps.

We are looking for talented graduates who are bright, enthusiastic problem solvers to join our software engineering team and technical operations team in the autumn / winter of 2026.

Sinara’s graduate programme has been running for many years, and our company has grown from the success of our former graduates.

Whether you are a 2026 graduate or have a couple of years of work experience under your belt, we would love to hear from you!

Graduate roles at Sinara

We are recruiting for three distinct graduate roles:

1. Graduate Software Engineer
2. Graduate Quality Assurance Engineer
3. Graduate Support Engineer

Read more below to learn more about our different graduate roles and to understand which suits your interests and aptitudes best.

1. Graduate Software Engineer

You will join our Software Engineering team, our largest team in the company where you will begin on a career trajectory that could see you reaching Principal or even Head of Software Development.

About The Role

After initial training your first project may involve working on applications such as trading lifecycle systems, options pricing algorithms, or inventory management applications. In most projects, you will work across the full .NET/Vue.js tech stack, from the web or desktop front-ends, to back-end algorithms, including work with communications, databases and cloud deployments. The work is often technically challenging and will certainly help to accelerate your growth.

Working with Sinara, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills whilst working on an active project and make a meaningful impact. You will get the chance to work in teams committed to using the best programming techniques and share information and your own ideas with colleagues and even clients of both a technical and non-technical background.

About You

You are a recent graduate with a 2:1 or above in a Computer Science or any other STEM degree, or an early-career developer looking for a new challenge. You are passionate about code, have a desire to learn new technical skills and enjoy solving all kinds of problems.

You demonstrate creative thinking and attention to detail in order to design solutions to technical challenges. You are able to think beyond just what is stated in requirements to achieve quality, robust solutions.

If you are excited by the idea of building great software and willing to learn, then this role is perfect for you.

No previous financial knowledge? No problem! You will learn everything you need on the job.

Career progression in Software Engineering

As your career progresses, we will work with you to shape the scope of your role, whether that means focusing on programming, or shifting towards other parts of the engineering process such as business analysis, project management, or a balance somewhere in between. Some may develop an interest in team and people management and we can help you develop your role to incorporate this too.

We allow staff to engage in projects into new and emerging technologies as well as undertake training that will enhance their skills.

2. Graduate Quality Assurance Engineer

About The Role

You will join our dedicated QA team, where you will be working closely with our software engineers to help ensure our software is robust, reliable, user-friendly, and ready for release. You will design and execute test cases, identify defects, investigate issues, and contribute to improving our testing processes. This is an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience across the full software development lifecycle in a collaborative company where your input will make a real impact. You may even have the opportunity to work directly with clients when opportunities arise.

About You

This role would suit a curious, analytical problem-solver who enjoys fully understanding how systems work and identifying ways to improve them. We are looking for graduates with a 2:1 degree in Computer Science, or any other STEM subject. An interest in software quality, strong attention to detail, good communication skills, and a willingness to learn are more important than previous commercial experience. Any exposure to software testing, programming, automation tools would be an advantage.

3. Graduate Support Engineer

About The Role

The role is an interesting mix of DevOps engineering work on projects within Tech Ops team and providing technical support for our Sinara-built applications; maintaining our mission-critical applications, delivering application management support and providing technical support for Sinara software applications to a variety of customers.

You will be responsible for analysing, prioritising and resolving customer support incidents which may be application, data or system related.

About You

To excel in this role, we seek budding engineers who possess a passion for tackling diverse and complex IT challenges. You should have the aptitude and dedication to rapidly acquire new technical abilities and assimilate fresh domain knowledge as necessary.

We want people who are naturally curious about systems and technologies and thrive on problem solving. You should be proactive, self-driven, capable of independent initiative, and consistently consider the broader context and potential ramifications of the issues at hand.

It’s important that you exhibit exceptional attention to detail, coupled with proficient time management and organisational skills. It would be beneficial to have some experience working in a customer facing role.

Why Join Sinara?

We are a leading software development company that provides cutting-edge solutions for major businesses in the world of Finance. As well as getting to work in the exciting fin-tech industry and excellent development opportunities, Sinara offers a competitive compensation and benefits package to all new graduates.

What we offer

- Starting salary of £42,000 with salary reviews every six months for your first two years
- Two bonus schemes: profit-related bonus and service-related bonus scheme
- 25 days paid holiday plus 8 bank holidays
- Private pension and salary sacrifice option
- Private medical health scheme
- Income protection scheme
- Flexibility with a hybrid working model
- Weekly company lunches
- Cycle-to-work scheme
- Opportunities for career progression in various directions
- MSc support programme

Training

All graduate roles begin with 2-3 weeks of full-time training then we get you straight in to working on our live projects. The hands-on approach to learning the role makes it a steep learning curve but an effective one. You will get responsibility and exposure to many parts of the software development process or technical operations from early on.

Career progression

Sinara is committed to your growth and development. From day one, you will be paired with an experienced mentor in your department to guide you along your career path. As your career progresses, we will work with you to shape the scope of your role, whether that means focusing on further developing your programming, or other technical skills or shifting towards management, project management or other parts of the engineering process.

We encourage everyone within Sinara to take responsibility in a variety of areas including client relationship management, product innovation, documentation, technical quality, recruitment and mentoring.

Company culture

At Sinara your colleagues will be as talented and committed as you are yourself. Sinara is a collaborative company, where you can expect to know who everyone in the company is, and we encourage effective teamwork and inter-team collaboration.

We value every member of the company, and we are keen to show that with regular technical seminars, social lunches, and other personal and professional support.

Hybrid working

Sinara employs a flexible hybrid working policy with a mix of office days and home working days. There may also be opportunities to work on-client-site, perhaps at a leading exchange or other financial institution.

Nicole: I started here as a graduate software engineer in 2014, the autumn after completing my Computer Science degree.

Frequent catch ups and appraisals are held to inform you of your progress and areas to develop, and the project leaders are always looking for opportunities to improve the skills of junior developers within projects.

We also have dedicated tech leads on most of the projects at Sinara, so there is always an expert you can reach out to if you get stuck. Another good thing we have at Sinara is Professional Development Managers (PDMs) who you can talk to about anything including your career goals and how you feel about the projects you are working on.

job_description:
About Skyscanner 

Everyone loves travelling, but planning is not without its challenges ✈️. That's why we've spent 20 years building tools that turn travel-planning chaos into a breeze. Today, around 160 million travellers count on us every month to skip the whole “47 browser tabs open” phase and find flights, cars, and hotels quickly and easily 💻. 

Joining Skyscanner means becoming part of a global brand that's striving to become the planet's go-to travel hack accessible for all 🌍. 

Our vision? To be the world's number one travel ally. (Ambitious? 💪Yes, but, hey, that's what got us here). 

Now, we’re on the lookout for a **Global PR Lead** to help us bring that vision to even more travellers. 

About the role 
(Hybrid) 

This is a role at the heart of our fast-paced, high-volume PR team, helping keep our communications flying in formation across 23 markets worldwide. You’ll be the central point connecting plans, people, budgets, agencies and operations — making sure our global PR machine runs smoothly, efficiently and at scale.

Working closely with our Senior Director of Communications, regional PR leads, internal teams and global agency partners, you’ll help turn our international PR strategy into coordinated action. From shaping global initiatives to sharpening the way we plan, measure and operate, you’ll bring the structure that helps brilliant PR ideas travel further.

What you’ll be doing

- Driving global PR planning: You’ll lead the planning process with our global PR agency hub, partnering with the Senior Director of Communications to keep forecasting, budgets, resources and priorities aligned.

- Turning measurement into momentum: You’ll work closely with our measurement lead to make sure reporting is accurate, useful and connected to the strategies and decisions that matter.

- Optimising our PR ecosystem: You’ll partner with Procurement and Finance to make sure we have the right suppliers, commercial setup and financial tracking in place to support growth — without the spreadsheet drama.

- Keeping priorities moving: You’ll traffic-manage inbound requests, help the team navigate competing priorities and make sure resources are focused where they can have the greatest impact.

- Leading global PR initiatives: You’ll spearhead strategic PR initiatives and special projects beyond our core campaigns, while supporting the delivery of our Awareness strategy and Big Bet activity through PR.

- Making operations smarter: You’ll lead and collaborate on cross-functional improvements spanning tools and technology, including Tableau, ThoughtSpot, AI and our Product Ops model — finding smarter ways for a global team to work at scale.

- Creating consistency across markets: You’ll partner with market leads, our global agency hub and Corporate and B2B PR teams to develop playbooks, strengthen processes and drive consistent adoption and delivery across 23 markets. You’ll also manage and develop our PR Coordinator, keeping calendars, finance trackers and reporting firmly on course.

About you

- Global PR operator: You’ve worked in complex, international communications environments and know how to turn lots of moving parts into one joined-up plan.

- Strategic and operational: You’re equally comfortable shaping a global PR initiative and getting into the detail needed to make it happen. Big picture, meet beautifully organised spreadsheet.

- Stakeholder savvy: You build trusted relationships across senior leaders, market teams, agencies and cross-functional partners, bringing people together around shared priorities.

- Agency confident: You know how to get the best from global agency relationships, balancing clear direction, strong partnership and accountability for delivery.

- Commercially switched-on: You’re comfortable working with budgets, forecasting, suppliers, Procurement and Finance, and you understand how strong operational foundations help teams achieve more.

- Tech and data curious: You’re interested in how measurement, dashboards, AI and smarter tools can improve PR operations, reporting and decision-making at scale.

- Calm in the whirlwind: You thrive in fast-paced environments, can prioritise when everything feels important, and enjoy helping teams work more effectively. You’re also comfortable managing and developing others along the way.

What it's like here 

We are the real deal - no corporate gloss, no empty promises. Just a team of genuinely curious, caring humans ❤️, building things that help travellers explore the world a little easier 🧭. 

Skyscanner is made up of brilliant humans from every corner of the world. We believe travel makes the world better - and that the same is true of our diverse teams. Sound like your kind of adventure? 🚀 Apply now and help us shape the future of travel.

# Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy

London, Glasgow or Edinburgh

**About Skyscanner** 

Everyone loves travelling, but planning is not without its challenges ✈️. That's why we've spent 20 years building tools that turn travel-planning chaos into a breeze. Today, around 160 million travellers count on us every month to skip the whole “47 browser tabs open” phase and find flights, cars, and hotels quickly and easily 💻. 

Joining Skyscanner means becoming part of a global brand that's striving to become the planet's go-to travel hack accessible for all 🌍. 

Our vision? To be the world's number one travel ally. (Ambitious? 💪Yes, but, hey, that's what got us here). 

Now, we’re on the lookout for a **Principal Engineer - Identity & Privacy** to help us bring that vision to even more travellers. 

**About the role** 
**(Hybrid)** 

As our Principal Engineer for Identity & Privacy, you’ll shape the technical foundations that help us earn traveller trust while safely unlocking the data and AI capabilities behind brilliant product, personalisation, experimentation and advertising experiences.

This is a senior technical leadership role with impact right across Skyscanner. You’ll own the technical strategy and set standards for identity, consent and privacy engineering across our traveller-facing products, data platforms and operational systems — spanning web, app, backend, experimentation, analytics, advertising and machine learning. 

**What you’ll be doing**

- **Setting our technical strategy:** You’ll define and communicate the long-term vision and roadmap for identity, consent and privacy engineering, aligning it with our product strategy, traveller trust goals and data and AI ambitions.

- **Shaping identity at scale:** You’ll lead our technical approach to purpose-scoped identifiers and consent-aware data processing across sessions, tracking, advertising, accounts, consent and derived identifiers.

- **Connecting the dots end-to-end:** You’ll establish how identity and consent state flows from web and app surfaces through backend services, event streams and data pipelines to downstream consumers — making a complicated ecosystem feel a lot less complicated.

- **Turning privacy into engineering practice:** You’ll translate privacy principles and legal guidance into reusable engineering patterns, platform controls, decision frameworks and measurable standards, including clear expectations around retention, deletion, masking, access control and auditability.

- **Leading across Skyscanner:** You’ll partner with Engineering, Product, Legal, Privacy, Security, Data Governance, Data Science, Marketing, Ads and Analytics to navigate trade-offs, create clarity and turn ambiguous problems into decisions teams can deliver against.

- **Getting hands-on with the big stuff:** You’ll provide technical leadership for large-scale initiatives spanning consent platform capabilities, privacy-safe experimentation, data retention and deletion, and traveller-trust features, while guiding teams towards simple, scalable, reliable and cost-effective solutions.

- **Raising the engineering bar:** You’ll use observability, engineering health and incident learnings to improve how we operate, while coaching and mentoring engineers and championing high standards, constructive challenge and inclusive collaboration across our Engineering community.

**About you**

- **Privacy-engineering experienced:** You’ve translated privacy and data-protection requirements — including GDPR, PECR, CCPA/CPRA or equivalent global frameworks — into practical engineering decisions, working effectively with Legal, Privacy, Security and Data Governance partners.

- **Built for scale:** You’ve designed, built and operated large-scale distributed systems across identity, data platforms or adjacent areas such as consent, authentication, advertising technology or customer data infrastructure.

- **An influential technical leader:** You’ve led significant technical change across multiple teams without direct line authority, creating clarity, alignment and momentum when ownership is distributed.

- **Strong in technical judgement:** You’re comfortable making decisions where product value, traveller trust, privacy requirements, operational reliability and cost are all competing for a seat at the table.

- **End-to-end minded:** You can reason confidently across client surfaces, backend services, event streams, data products, ML features, analytics, partner exports and operational tooling — and understand how a decision in one part of the system can ripple through the rest.

- **Practical about standards:** You know how to turn policy into technical controls and measurable quality standards that teams can consistently use in real systems, rather than another document destined for a forgotten browser tab.

- **Clear, collaborative and credible:** You can create shared engineering practices, write clear technical strategy and work effectively with senior stakeholders across Engineering, Product, Legal, Security and Data Governance. **The role**

As a Geotechnical Engineer within our Engineering Team, you'll play a critical role in delivering some of the UK's and Europe's most exciting offshore wind projects. From early-stage development through to construction and operation, you'll provide technical expertise that influences major project decisions, reduces risk and helps deliver the engineering solutions that underpin successful offshore wind developments. This is an opportunity to work on technically complex projects, collaborate with industry-leading specialists and make a genuine impact on the transition to renewable energy.

**You Will**

- Develop and deliver geotechnical strategies that support offshore wind projects throughout their lifecycle, providing technical leadership, risk management and input into project programmes and delivery plans.
- Plan, coordinate and execute a broad range of geotechnical engineering activities, including offshore ground investigations, laboratory testing programmes, geotechnical interpretation, ground modelling, foundation engineering and cable installation assessments.
- Work closely with project, engineering and procurement teams to scope, specify and manage consultants and contractors, ensuring technical excellence, commercial value and successful project outcomes.
- Review and challenge third-party technical studies and designs, including desk studies, foundation designs, driveability assessments, cable burial risk assessments, cable installation analyses, sediment mobility studies, laboratory testing schedules, leg penetration assessments, geohazard evaluations and ground investigation reports.
- Support projects through development, construction and operations by contributing to DEVEX, CAPEX and OPEX planning, driving continuous improvement and innovation, and ensuring compliance with health, safety, environmental and sustainability requirements.

ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of new databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

 

Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

 

The work spans three strength areas:

Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

Operational / SRE practice — the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

We expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional — and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.




WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

Platform reliability & operations

 - Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

 - Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for new platform capabilities and major changes.

 - Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

 - Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

Software engineering

 - Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling — writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

 - Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

 - Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

 - Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

 - Contribute to the platform's continual testing automation — the test suites and pipelines that validate platform releases are fit for purpose before they reach tenants.

Tooling, ecosystem & architecture

 - Act as a platform reliability and architecture expert — contribute to failure-mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design for multi-tenant container workloads.

 - Evaluate and evolve the platform's tooling ecosystem (orchestration, runtime, networking, isolation, and observability stack) with a clear, opinionated view on trade-offs.

 - Improve system architecture to reduce infrastructure cost while balancing security, reliability, and performance across tenants.

 - Guide teams building on the platform to design sustainable on-call practices for their own services: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction.

 


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU

 - Have 5+ years in platform engineering, container/Kubernetes platform operations, SRE, or production infrastructure, and have operated production systems at scale and carried on-call for them.

 - Are genuinely deep in at least one — ideally two — of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):

 - Tooling & ecosystem — know the container/orchestration landscape well: Kubernetes, containerd and the OCI/CRI standards, and the surrounding CNCF ecosystem (e.g. Argo CD/Argo Rollouts for GitOps and progressive delivery; Cilium/eBPF networking and the Gateway API; Karpenter/KEDA-style autoscaling; and workload-isolation runtimes such as gVisor or Kata Containers). You reason about trade-offs rather than reaching for defaults.

 - Software engineering — write real production code (Go and/or a comparable systems language) and can build controllers, operators, and platform APIs — stepping back to the underlying problem and building the right solution when no off-the-shelf tool fits.

 - Operational / SRE practice — are fluent in SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs; have led incident response and blameless postmortems; and have driven down MTTD/MTTR for systems you operated.

 - Have worked with large-scale multi-tenant systems and understand isolation as a spectrum — from namespaces, RBAC, network policies, and resource quotas through to stronger primitives such as virtual clusters (e.g. vCluster) or VM-class runtimes.

 - Operate confidently on AWS (multiple accounts, IAM, VPC) and are comfortable with infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine) and Kubernetes.

job_title: Senior Backend Engineer - Developer Experience & Productivity
job_description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Taktile helps financial institutions make smarter, safer decisions with the power of AI. Internally, AI coding agents have made writing code dramatically faster. The bottleneck is now everything around the code: builds, tests, reviews, merges, and deploys.

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer focused on Developer Productivity and Developer Experience to remove that bottleneck. This is a high-leverage, internal engineering role on our Platform Team: your users are Taktile's backend and frontend engineers and the AI agents working alongside them, and your product is the path from first commit to production.

You'll make CI fast and reliable, make our serverless stack easier to build on, and turn "how fast can we ship safely?" into metrics we move every quarter.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build the deployment services that ship Taktile. Own the systems behind tens of thousands of stack deployments a week across dev, staging, production, and per-customer AWS accounts: progressive rollouts through monitoring and canary stages, deployment windows and gates, and fast rollbacks.

 - Keep our AI developer tooling sharp. Maintain and extend Claudius, our in-house AI engineering agent that investigates CI failures, triages issues, and opens PRs, and metadev, our sandboxed Claude Code and OpenCode setup that packages Taktile's engineering knowledge for every engineer.

 - Own the build → test → merge loop. Drive down CI runtime and flakiness across our main monorepos. Find the slowest and least reliable steps, fix them, and keep them fixed.

 - Evolve our CI/CD architecture. Build on our move to per-module GitHub Actions workflows and a self-hosted runner fleet. Improve caching, parallelism, and cost per build.

 - Shorten the inner dev loop. Make developing on our AWS Lambda stack fast, from running services locally against preview environments to faster, container-based deploys, so engineers aren't waiting on CloudFormation to test a change.

 - Build paved roads. Ship templates, CLIs, and self-service tooling so any team can take a new module from first commit to a running dev workspace in under a day.

 - Design for humans and agents. Make our tooling fast, deterministic, and scriptable so engineers and AI coding agents get quick, trustworthy feedback.

 - Measure what matters. Own DevProd metrics like PR lead time, CI runtime, CI flakiness, and PRs per engineer-day. Use them to decide what to fix next and to prove the impact of what you ship.

 - Own our AI developer tooling. Take ownership of Claudius, our in-house AI engineering agent, and decide where it goes next.

 - Treat engineers as customers. Talk to teams, triage CI incidents, write clear docs, and drive migrations and deprecations to completion.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 5+ years of professional backend engineering experience, with a track record of shipping and operating production systems end-to-end and leading technical projects across teams.

 - Strong, production-grade skills in at least one backend language. Python is our main language today, but we're open to others. This role is mostly writing software (tools, services, bots, and CI logic), not only configuring it.

 - Hands-on experience owning CI/CD at scale (for example, GitHub Actions): build and test performance, caching, parallelization, and debugging flaky tests and pipelines.

 - Solid AWS experience, ideally with serverless (Lambda, CloudFormation/SAM) and infrastructure as code (Terraform).

 - Comfortable with the latest AI coding and agent-orchestration tools (for example, Claude Code, OpenCode, subagents, and MCP). You use them daily and know how to make them work reliably for a whole engineering org.

 - A product mindset for internal tooling. You talk to your users, measure outcomes, and judge success by adoption and time saved.

 - Strong communication and stakeholder management. You can drive a change across many teams you don't manage: write the proposal, plan the rollout, and see it through.




IDEAL, BUT NOT REQUIRED

 - Prior experience on a developer productivity, developer experience, build/release engineering, or platform team.

 - Experience as a product-facing backend engineer, so you know firsthand where the development loop hurts.

 - Experience with frontend build and test tooling in the TypeScript/React ecosystem, so you can support our frontend engineers too.

 - Experience running self-hosted CI runners or build infrastructure at scale.

 - Experience with progressive delivery: canary deployments, automated rollbacks, and deployment gates.

 - Experience with monorepo tooling, build systems, or dependency management at scale.

 - Experience building AI agents or agent infrastructure, such as MCP servers, agent harnesses, or evals.




OUR STACK

 - AI: Claude, Claude Code, OpenCode

 - Programming Languages: Python and TypeScript (React) today; open to others where they fit better

 - Cloud & Infrastructure: AWS (Lambda, SAM/CloudFormation, ECR, CodeDeploy), Docker, Terraform

 - CI/CD: GitHub Actions, self-hosted runners

 - Internal Tools: GitHub, Linear, Notion, Metabase




OUR STANCE

 - We're eager to meet talented and driven candidates regardless of whether they tick all the boxes. We're looking for someone who will add to our culture, not just fit within it. We strongly encourage individuals from groups traditionally underestimated and underrepresented in tech to apply.

 - We seek to actively recognize and combat racism, sexism, ableism and ageism. We embrace and support all gender identities and expressions, and celebrate love in its many forms. We won't inquire about how you identify or if you've experienced discrimination, but if you want to tell your story, we are all ears.

 


ABOUT US

Taktile enables financial institutions to transform into AI-native organizations that are increasingly powered by autonomous agents. 

With our modular Agentic Decision Platform, customers combine AI agents, rules, relevant context, and human oversight to safely automate and optimize their decisions—approving more customers, reimbursing claims instantly, stopping fraud before it spreads, and financing every business worth funding. 

Founded in 2020, Taktile powers millions of decisions daily for institutions including Mercury, Monzo, Faire, and Pleo. 

With offices in New York, Berlin, London, São Paulo, and Iași, the company has raised $184M from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Index Ventures, Tiger Global, Balderton Capital, and Y Combinator. Learn more at taktile.com http://taktile.com.

job_description:
Bank of London is one of only six UK clearing banks with direct access to the country's payment systems. Built on modern, cloud-native technology, we provide businesses with secure, API-driven banking that's fast, compliant, and built for growth. Our role is simple: help ambitious businesses turn their plans into reality by removing barriers and simplifying complexity. If you want to work where technology meets banking, where security comes first, and where your work directly enables business ambition, you're in the right place. 

As part of the 2nd Line of Defence, the Financial Crime Risk Team sets the Bank’s Financial Crime Risk Policies and Standards framework, is responsible for monitoring and oversight of compliance with policy requirements, providing subject matter expertise advice and guidance, and internal and external reporting obligations.  

This Transaction Monitoring & Sanction Screening Analyst role ensures that AML/ Fraud and TM and Sanction screening processes operate to the highest standard by providing onsite leadership, clear oversight, expert risk assessment, and continuous challenge ultimately safeguarding the organisation against money laundering and financial crime. 

**Who we are looking for** 
We are looking for a results-orientated, self-driven individual with passion, enthusiasm, and ability to influence at all levels.   

At minimum, we expect you to have experience conducting similar reviews from either a FinCrime or AML Audit perspective. The successful candidate will also be able to demonstrate experience within Financial Services, particularly the payment industry or correspondent banking. Experience in performing Enhanced Due Diligence on regulated Financial Institutions and experience in performing Onsite reviews/Audits on regulated Financial Institutions and/or High-Risk businesses are essential requirements. Furthermore, it is desirable if you have financial crime related professional qualifications and experience in developing processes. 

Job requirements

•  2 – 3 years of relevant AML/Fraud and sanctions experience in fintech, financial services or regulatory environment. 
•  Strong knowledge of typical AML/CTF/sanctions frameworks (e.g. OFAC), ML/TF typologies and risk based transaction & account monitoring and card scheme regulations. 
•  Proven hands on experience in alert clearing, holistic reviews, RFIs, escalations to MLRO/FCC and/or SAR/UAR support. 
•  Experience with process improvement initiatives (e.g. KYC/CDD), and policy & procedure development (e.g. list maintenance, STR/STR equivalent drafting or review). 
•  Strong 2line discipline, comfortable managing queues, utilisation, SLAs and QA standards. 
•  Strong Crypto -assets or blockchain -related AML controls experience. 
•  Strong Foreign Exchange (FX) AML controls experience.

Job responsibilities

•  Perform Quality Assurance (QA) reviews of Transaction Monitoring (TM), Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), and Name Screening cases, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and quality standards.  
•  Conduct end-to-end financial crime investigations, including fund flow analysis, customer business profile reviews, adverse media screening, source of funds and source of wealth assessments, and transaction analysis.  
•  Conduct EDD reviews, quality assurance assessments, and investigations for Foreign Exchange (FX) customers and transactions, as well as Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), identifying and assessing financial crime risks, customer risk profiles, ownership structures, and transaction activity.  
•  Investigate complex and high-risk cases escalated from the First Line of Defence (1LoD), thematic reviews, internal intelligence, and referrals from other stakeholders, applying strong risk-based judgement to determine appropriate outcomes and escalating suspicious activity to the Second Line of Defence (2LoD) Financial Crime Investigations team where necessary.  
•  Support the review and investigation of transaction monitoring alerts, unusual activity, and high-risk customer relationships, including those involving digital assets, ensuring timely and high-quality investigations and regulatory reporting.  
•  Provide guidance and support to 1LoD teams on complex procedural requirements, transaction monitoring processes, and financial crime controls.

job_description:
This position can be done remotely within the UK. A central-London office is also available for hybrid work if preferred. You will be part of a friendly, international team. 
Job Summary
The Senior Legal Counsel, Privacy and Data Protection will provide sophisticated, practical, and business-oriented legal advice on EU/EEA privacy and data protection matters across Nielsen’s products, services, commercial relationships, and internal operations. This role will independently manage complex privacy workstreams, support Nielsen’s European privacy program, and serve as a trusted advisor to local sales and business teams. The role will work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and Legal colleagues across jurisdictions.
• Provide senior legal guidance on EU/EEA privacy compliance, data governance, and risk mitigation for business operations, products, partnerships, and commercial transactions.

• Apply in-depth knowledge and experience to solve complex privacy and commercial legal problems, using best practices and a practical understanding of Nielsen’s business.

• Work independently with minimal guidance, lead smaller projects and complex workstreams, and act as a resource for colleagues with less experience.

• Draft, review and negotiate complex data protection exhibits on both the buy-side and sell-side.

• Build consensus among stakeholders by explaining complex, difficult, or sensitive privacy and data protection issues in clear, actionable terms.

Responsibilities
• Provide day-to-day legal advice on the EU/EEA General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), applicable national implementing laws, European Data Protection Board (EDPB) guidance, supervisory-authority decisions, ePrivacy requirements, marketing and consumer protection rules, and other relevant European data protection and digital regulations.

• Maintain deep practical knowledge of EU/EEA privacy and data protection requirements and translate legal developments into clear, actionable guidance, contract language, policies, notices, processes, and implementation requirements for local and global stakeholders.

• Draft, review, and negotiate data processing agreements, data protection exhibits, data sharing and data use agreements, data transfer arrangements, and related privacy provisions in commercial contracts, representing Nielsen on both the buy-side and sell-side.

• Support local sales and business teams on privacy aspects of customer agreements, proposals, product offerings, data services, partnerships, and other commercial opportunities, providing timely and commercially practical advice.

• Conduct and oversee privacy impact assessments (PIAs/DPIAs), transfer impact assessments, legitimate interest assessments, and other privacy risk assessments for products, features, data uses, partnerships, and operational initiatives.

• Conduct privacy due diligence on third parties, vendors, customers, and strategic partners, including reviewing questionnaires and security materials, assessing processing activities and data flows, identifying gaps, negotiating remediation, and supporting ongoing oversight.

• Advise on advertising technology, audience measurement, analytics, identity, cookies, pixels, SDKs, targeted advertising, consent and preference management, data monetization, and related media and marketing data practices. Experience in adtech or media technology is strongly preferred.

• Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and other stakeholders to assess proposed data collection, use, disclosure, retention, and deletion activities and to support compliant product launches and operational changes.

• Communicate with, or support communications with, local data protection authorities and other supervisory authorities as required, including in connection with regulatory inquiries, consultations, complaints, audits, filings, investigations, and data incidents.

• Support privacy incident and data breach response, data subject rights escalations, regulatory inquiries, audits, and other privacy compliance matters in coordination with local business teams, security, legal, and outside counsel.

• Contribute to and improve privacy program materials, including policies, procedures, playbooks, templates, training, records of processing, data inventories, data retention requirements, and compliance reporting.

• Monitor developments in EU/EEA and national privacy law, enforcement trends, and related digital regulation; assess their impact on Nielsen’s business and communicate recommendations to stakeholders.

• Extensive experience practicing privacy, data protection, technology, commercial, or related legal work in-house, with a track record of producing high-quality independent work.

• Law degree or equivalent legal qualification; qualification or admission in the UK is required, consistent with the requirements for the role.

• Deep, practical knowledge of the GDPR and applicable national privacy and data protection laws in at least one relevant European jurisdiction, with the ability to apply requirements across products, contracts, and business processes.

• Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing DPIAs/PIAs, transfer impact assessments, legitimate interest assessments, and privacy risk assessments, including documenting risks and tracking mitigations.

• Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating DPAs, data protection exhibits, and other privacy-related contract terms, including experience advising both buyers/customers and sellers/providers of data or services.

• Experience advising business, sales, product, technology, or commercial teams on complex privacy issues and translating legal requirements into practical, commercially workable solutions.

• Experience engaging with or supporting communications to supervisory authorities, regulators, or other public-sector stakeholders is preferred and may be required for certain matters.

• Strong legal research, writing, negotiation, analytical, and issue-spotting skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgment and build consensus among diverse stakeholders.

• Excellent written and verbal English communication skills; fluency in an additional European language is a plus.

Preferred Qualifications
• CIPP/E certification is greatly preferred, but it is not a hard requirement. CIPM, CIPT, or an equivalent privacy credential is also a plus.

• Adtech, martech, media measurement, audience analytics, data licensing, or digital advertising experience is strongly preferred.

• Knowledge of U.S. privacy and data protection requirements, including U.S. state privacy laws and the CCPA/CPRA, is an advantage.

• Knowledge of APAC privacy and data protection regulations—particularly India’s Digital Personal Data Protection framework, Australia’s Privacy Act and Australian Privacy Principles, or South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act—is an advantage.

• Familiarity with international data transfers, standard contractual clauses, cross-border data sharing, consent and preference management, privacy management tools, data mapping, and records of processing activities.

•

• 
Proven track record of exceeding targets and growing accounts, fueled by a passion for delivering value to clients

• 
Demonstrable problem solving, communication and client relationship building and management skills

• 
Exceptional collaboration, prioritisation,  critical thinking, and influencing skills

• 
Excellent research and investigative abilities 

•

Lead Developer wanted for work that requires human thinking.

• Not a ticket queue.

• Not one microservice in an engineering org of fifty.

• Building where you watch real people use the thing, then go and fix what wasn’t obvious.

About Thunk

We’re a small Digital Innovation company, mostly remote, occasionally Kings Cross, London. We work across all sorts of innovation projects: climate infrastructure, healthcare systems, emerging tech. We’re deep into what we do. So deep that we’re quietly very good at it.

We design things people actually use. Increasingly, we build them too. We need someone to own how.

Your work

You’ll be Thunk’s lead developer: the person who owns how we build, not just what gets built. Most of your week goes on our flagship climate project. You’ll lead its frontend and work directly with the client and partner teams.

The rest goes across Thunk: prototypes we test with real users, our own products and internal tools. And the bit that’s yours to shape: how we review, test, ship and run our own services. In time, who joins you.

Day-to-day, you’ll work closely with the whole team. Nine people, so the org chart is more of an org sentence. We’re a close, friendly bunch. Small team, short line to decisions.

The flagship project

It’s a climate resilience platform for UK infrastructure. It helps network operators understand how climate threats spread across connected systems.

It’s a long-running, multi-phase programme delivered by a consortium. Thunk designs and builds the frontend; partner teams own the backend, data and hosting.

• Frontend: Next.js with IBM’s Carbon Design System

• Data: partner APIs, a knowledge graph and GeoServer map data

• Code and delivery: GitLab with CI/CD pipelines

• Auth: Keycloak

• Releases: feature branches, merge requests, tagged release candidates, then production

• Environments: six — dev, staging and production, each mirrored as a demo running synthetic data

We’ll share more about the project and the partners behind it at interview.

What you’ll do

• Lead the frontend: architecture, code quality, performance and releases.

• Set technical direction with the client and partner teams, and turn it into a plan.

• Build Thunk’s designs into map-led features — asset visualisation, prioritisation, export, onboarding.

• Integrate with partner APIs and GeoServer layers across all six environments.

• Own the release process in GitLab: reviews, tagged release candidates, production deploys.

• Keep the demo environments sharp for stakeholder presentations.

• Sit in on user testing, and turn what you see into fixes.

• Pay down tech debt — maybe starting with a smoother local setup — and keep the docs current.

Shaping how Thunk builds

• Set our engineering standards: code review, testing, CI/CD and documentation.

• Lead technical scoping in discovery and pitches — approach, estimates, risks.

• Make infrastructure and tooling decisions, including how we run our own services.

• Explore where AI belongs in the products we build for clients.

• Mentor other developers, and help hire the next ones as we grow.

Across Thunk

• Build prototypes for client discovery: real enough to test, quick enough to throw away.

• Contribute to Thunk’s own external products, internal automations and websites.

• Bring a developer’s view into early design and research: what’s feasible, quick or risky.

You

• You’ve shipped enough production code to have opinions, and enough to hold them loosely.

• You’ve integrated with APIs you don’t own, and written the calm, precise issue when they broke.

• You notice when the spacing’s off. (You’ll work with designers. They’ll notice too.)

• Accessibility is your default, not a ticket for later.

• Code review is a habit, whoever (or whatever) wrote it. You’re as good at taking it as giving it.

• You can explain a trade-off to a client with words regular humans use.

• You use AI coding tools daily, and still read the diff.

If you tick most of the boxes below but not all, apply anyway. The people who hesitate are usually the ones we want.

What you’ll bring

• 5+ years building and shipping production software, ideally in a consultancy or agency.

• Strong React, Next.js and TypeScript, and modern CSS.

• A track record of owning projects end to end, from requirements to production.

• CI/CD and infrastructure in practice: pipelines, multiple environments, infrastructure as code.

Nice to have

• Web mapping: GeoServer, WMS/WFS, or libraries like Mapbox, OpenLayers or Leaflet.

• IBM Carbon or another enterprise design system.

• AWS, Terraform or OpenTofu, and OpenID Connect auth such as Keycloak.

• Knowledge graphs, linked data, or data visualisation with D3 or WebGL.

• Node.js services, PHP, or automation tools like n8n.

• Climate, infrastructure, utilities or public-sector work.

• Mentoring developers, or supporting user research and usability testing.

The catch

It’s a consortium project. We own the frontend; partners own the backend, data and hosting. Some days you’ll be waiting on someone else’s roadmap. Six environments. The local setup could be smoother. Fixing might be your first job. You’ll set the standards rather than inherit them. Great if that excites you, less great if you’d rather someone else made the calls.

If you want a large engineering team to disappear into, this isn’t for you. Short feedback loop. No hiding.

Fit

We’re a small, remote-first team, allergic to consultant-speak and innovation theatre. We have hard earned values we stand by, we hope you will too. Feedback between the team is always direct rather than softened, because there’s no time for any other way. We care about craft over hype, and about the people behind the work more than the jargon we could wrap around it. We’re humanist technologists, so if you like humans AND technology you’ll fit right in. A dry sense of humour also helps.

Technology

We’ll supply everything you need to get the job done. Shiny laptop, any other hardware, licences and subscriptions to the tools you need. We’re pretty flexible here too.

Shape

Mostly remote (ad hoc meet-ups), full-time permanent, salaried. £50–70k (DOE) full-time. 25 days holiday, Xmas shutdown.

There’s room to grow, too. The role starts as lead developer; where it goes from there is largely up to you.

Description

As a Senior Risk Analyst at TrueLayer, you'll play a critical role in ensuring we can innovate, scale and expand our Pay by Bank products safely across the UK and Europe. Reporting to the Head of Compliance, you'll work across our Risk and Compliance function and the wider business to identify, assess and manage the risks that come with operating a growing, multi-jurisdictional payments business.

This is a hands-on, second-line risk role with meaningful ownership and visibility. You'll lead key risk assessment activities, challenge existing controls and work with teams across the business to ensure material risks are understood, appropriately mitigated and escalated where necessary. Your work will help protect customer funds, maintain regulatory confidence and ensure that business growth is supported by effective risk management.

You'll be expected to go beyond documenting risks. You'll turn complex risk information into clear, actionable insight, influence decisions and follow through to ensure that agreed controls and mitigations are effective. You'll help the business understand not only where risks exist, but what they mean, what needs to change and how we can manage them within our risk appetite.

What success looks like

• 
Risk visibility: Material risks across our products, operations and customer portfolio are identified, assessed and clearly understood by the right stakeholders.

• 
Effective controls: Risk assessments and control testing lead to practical improvements, with weaknesses escalated and remediation tracked through to completion.

• 
Safer innovation: New products, payment methods and material business changes are assessed early, enabling informed decisions before implementation.

• 
Stronger customer risk management: Customer and counterparty exposures are assessed and monitored, with appropriate risk ratings, limits and mitigations in place.

• 
Confident decision-making: Senior management and relevant governance committees receive clear, evidence-based reporting that supports timely and informed decisions.

 

What we expect from you as a Senior Risk Analyst

Risk Self-Assessments & Frameworks

• Facilitate RCSAs: Lead and coordinate the Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) process across business units to map, evaluate, and challenge operational and product-level risks.

• Maintain Risk Registers: Own the maintenance and quality of the corporate risk register, ensuring material risks, KRIs, owners and mitigation actions are current and actionable.

• Control Testing: Execute or coordinate independent control testing, assess design and operating effectiveness, and track remediation of identified weaknesses.

Impact Analyses & Governance

• Change Risk Impact Analysis: Execute detailed risk impact analyses for structural business adjustments, major system updates, or shifting regulatory mandates (such as DORA or FCA Operational Resilience rules).

• Scenario Analysis & Stress Testing: Model potential "tail-risk" events, assessing how extreme merchant defaults, system outages, or fraud spikes would impact the firm's capital and operational capacity.

• Board & Regulatory Reporting: Translate complex risk insights into concise, data-driven dashboards and reports for the Audit & Risk Committee (ARC), regulated Board, and authorities.

Product Risk Management

• New Product Risk Assessment (NPAP): Conduct end-to-end risk assessments for new payment features, rails, and cross-border capabilities before deployment.

• Product Safeguarding: Evaluate the structural risk of payment flows to ensure compliant isolation and safeguarding of user funds under FCA, CBI, and Swedish FSA rules.

• Vendor & Third-Party Risk: Perform risk assessments on critical third-party product dependencies, including payment gateways, and cloud infrastructure.

Customer Risk Management

• Customer Risk Profiling: Work with FinCrime and relevant business teams to maintain effective customer risk segmentation, ensuring risk ratings inform appropriate monitoring, limits and mitigation measures.

• Credit & Exposure Monitoring: Monitor ongoing customer portfolio health, evaluating settlement cycles, and potential exposure to consumer credit or liquidation risks.

• Threshold & Limit Management: Work with FinCrime to define and adjust transactional velocity limits and reserve requirements for high-risk customer categories.

 

About You

Curious, pragmatic and independent-minded. Comfortable challenging constructively and working in a fast-moving environment.

• Experience: Relevant and demonstrable experience in risk management (Second Line of Defence) within a regulated payment institution, Electronic Money Institution (EMI), or fintech.

• Domain Expertise: Proven track record of independently running RCSA cycles, conducting product risk reviews, and designing customer risk matrices.

• Regulatory Acumen: Strong familiarity with European and UK payment regulations, including PSD2/PSD3, FCA operational resilience guidelines, and safeguarding requirements.

• Analytical Skills: Advanced Excel to pull transactional data, analyse risk trends, and build automated KRI dashboards.

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Risk Management, Finance, Business, Law, or a related analytical discipline.

• Group collaboration: Comfortable operating within a matrixed, multi-jurisdictional risk and compliance function.

• Governance: Confident presenting to Boards and Senior Management, providing clear, evidence-based reporting on risks.

• Language: Fluent English, both written and spoken.

Job Overview

Hybrid: 2 days/week in London
Location: London

At Uswitch, our goal is to be the UK’s favourite way to choose and manage home‑life essentials – from broadband and mobiles to energy and insurance. As we continue to grow, we are looking for talented individuals who share our passion for making a positive impact on people’s lives. If you want to be part of a team transforming the way consumers navigate household services, we would love to hear from you.

We’re part of RVU, a group of online brands that include Confused, Tempcover, money.co.uk and Mojo Mortgages.

The analytics team strives to simplify some of the most complex and daunting consumer marketplaces, to improve the lives of our customers. We give millions of people the information required to save thousands of pounds per year by helping them make more informed decisions about their utility bills and finance products at the right time.

We Answer Questions Like

• How do we most effectively let customers know when they could be switching to a better deal?

• How can we deepen our understanding of our customers to improve their experience with our marketing?

• How do we identify and prioritise what currently matters most to each segment of our customer base?

About the Role

As a Senior Product Analyst (Marketing & CRM), your input will be crucial in driving decision‑making. You will be the voice of our data, using it to influence and guide strategy, as well as identifying opportunities that may benefit the business. You will own both the “what” and the “why” behind performance – not just reporting results, but identifying the drivers and recommending action. This is a hands‑on senior analyst role focused on understanding customer behaviour and evaluating the impact of CRM activity across uSwitch.
You’ll join our Marketing Analytics team – a team looking to understand and optimise all marketing channels from the effectiveness of Above The Line/Brand to improving the efficiency of key conversion drivers such as Paid Search.

Our ambition is to build a best‑in‑class customer experience. You’ll play a leading role by enabling us to understand our customers better, harnessing data and discovering insight across all touch‑points, campaigns, and marketing activity.

Key Responsibilities

Using tools and databases including Google Sheets, BigQuery (SQL), Tableau and Python you’ll tackle intriguing and exciting problems that we’re only just starting to understand, in order to:

• Own the analytical evaluation of CRM activity, including deciding how impact should be measured, what success looks like, and how confident we should be in conclusions.

• Diagnose changes in customer and CRM performance, forming hypotheses and narrowing down root causes under time pressure.

• Design and conduct experiments (e.g. holdouts, A/B tests), with a clear understanding of causality, limitations and risk.

• Turn analysis into decisions and clearly articulate what the data does and does not support.

• Work closely with CRM, marketing and analytics stakeholders, adjusting depth and rigour based on audience and context.

• Improve how we measure and understand customers over time, not just reporting on what has already happened.

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone comfortable making data‑informed decisions under ambiguity, prioritising impact over perfection, and evolving strategy based on customer response rather than waiting for complete certainty.
You’ll Ideally Have Experience In

• Applying analytical judgement to real business problems, including choosing between different methods and understanding their trade‑offs.

• Evaluating CRM or customer activity where causality is not always obvious.

• Structuring ambiguous problems and narrowing them into clear analytical questions.

• Explaining analytical reasoning clearly to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

• Working hands‑on with data to support decisions, not just generating outputs.

• Proficiency in SQL is essential; experience using analytical and data BI tooling such as Tableau (Git, dbt – nice to have).

Our Commitment to You

We are dedicated to developing valuable, inclusive, and user‑friendly products and services that deliver positive outcomes for all of our customers. To achieve this, it’s essential that our teams reflect the diverse range of people in our community. We believe in being the change we wish to see in the world, by embracing our differences and holding ourselves accountable to being open and inclusive teammates and wider community members.

• A hybrid working approach with 2 in‑office days per week and up to 22 working days per year to “work from anywhere”.
